Quick Answer
macOS 27 Golden Gate has far more useful features than the ones you will notice immediately after updating. I tested more than 27 of them and picked the 27 worth trying, including Siri AI, custom Safari extensions, smarter Shortcuts, new Photos tools, and several smaller additions. Go through this list, and you will likely find a few features that can make the way you use your Mac easier.
Apple has finally released macOS 27 Golden Gate, and unlike the last few macOS updates, this one feels like a much bigger update. Apple has changed how macOS looks, added the new Siri AI, brought several Apple Intelligence features to its built-in apps, and made noticeable changes to Safari, Photos, Notes, Calendar, and many other places that you will notice once you start using your Mac.
I have been using macOS 27 and trying these features on my Mac, and some of them are genuinely useful. Some of my favorites is the new Siri that does many more things than previous, also Safari that lets you create your own extension simply by describing what you want it to do.
There are plenty of smaller additions like this throughout macOS 27. Some solve problems I have had with macOS for a long time, while others add things that previously required a third-party app or a much longer workaround. In this article, I will show you the best macOS 27 Golden Gate features I have found so far, what has changed, and how you can try them on your Mac.
Table of Contents
27 Best macOS 27 Golden Gate Features
macOS 27 Golden Gate comes with countless new features and small changes, and covering every single one of them in one article isn’t possible. After digging deeper into the update and trying many of these features myself, I have picked the best 27 that I found the most useful and that I think most Mac users should know about. Some are easy to notice, while others are hidden inside the apps and settings you already use every day.
Talk With Siri AI and Continue Your Previous Conversations
Siri has received one of its biggest changes on the Mac with macOS 27. Instead of only appearing as the small Siri interface we have been using for years, Siri AI now has its own app where you can start a conversation, ask follow-up questions, and return to your previous conversations later.
This is particularly useful when I have already given Siri all the context about something, and whenever needed, I can reopen that conversation instead of explaining everything again.
To use the Siri AI app on your Mac, first make sure Siri is enabled.
Once it is enabled, open the Siri app, where you will find all your previous conversations in the left sidebar and the chat window on the right. You can select any previous conversation to continue chatting or start a new conversation with Siri. If you right-click on any conversation in the sidebar, you will also see additional options to pin or delete the conversation.
Search Your Mac and Ask Siri Directly From Spotlight
Spotlight is one of the features I use almost every day on my Mac. With macOS 27, it also becomes a quick way to access Siri AI, so I don’t have to open the dedicated Siri app whenever I have a small question.
You just have to press Command + Space to open Spotlight and continue typing normally when you want to find an app, file, document, or setting. When you want to ask Siri AI something instead, just type your query normally and hit return to get an answer. You can also access whatever you have searched in Spotlight in the dedicated Siri app as a separate conversation.
I prefer using this for quick questions and keeping the Siri app for longer conversations where I know I will need follow-up questions.
Create Your Own Safari Extension Just by Describing It
Safari already supports extensions, but I still have to find an extension that does exactly what I need. With macOS 27, I can simply describe the functionality I want, and Safari can create an extension for me using Apple Intelligence.
I tried this with Instagram. I sometimes watch Reels on Instagram’s website, but it doesn’t give me a playback bar to quickly move forward or backward in a Reel. Instead of searching for an extension, I asked Safari to create one using this prompt:
Prompt: Create an extension for Instagram that adds playback controls to Reels and lets me move forward or backwards in the video while watching a Reel.
Surprisingly, it worked. After enabling the generated extension, I could seek forward and backwards while watching Instagram Reels. If there is a small website-specific feature you have always wanted, this gives you a way to try building it yourself.
To create one:
- Open Safari on your Mac and visit the website for which you want to create an extension.
- Click on the Page menu inside Safari’s address bar and select Describe Extension.
- Describe exactly what you want the extension to do. “I recommend keeping the request focused on one particular problem instead of asking it to change several unrelated things on the website.”
- Safari will first check whether an existing extension from the App Store can do what you described. If you don’t want one of the suggested extensions, click Create to generate your own.
- Once Safari creates the extension, click Try and test it on the website. Don’t save it immediately; use the website normally for a few minutes and make sure the extension actually behaves the way you expected.
- If something isn’t working correctly, click Edit and describe what you want Safari to change. Once you are happy with the result, click Save to keep the extension.
If you are new to browser extensions, you can check our list of the best Safari extensions for Mac to see what else extensions can add to Safari.
Create Shortcuts by Simply Explaining What You Want
Shortcuts can automate plenty of repetitive tasks on a Mac, but creating a complicated shortcut manually isn’t always easy. macOS 27 lets you describe what you want in normal language, and Apple Intelligence can put together the required Shortcut actions for you.
For example, I created a simple shortcut for work. Whenever I start working, I need to open TechPP, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress. Instead of opening each website manually, I created a shortcut that opens all four websites in Chrome whenever I run it.
Prompt: Create a shortcut that opens techpp.com, Gmail, Google Docs, and WordPress in Chrome.
Here’s how you can create it:
- Open the Shortcuts app on your Mac and click the plus (+) button.
- Enter the prompt in the Describe a shortcut field and let Apple Intelligence create the shortcut for you.
- Once it is created, click Run or the Play icon to test it.
Use Visual Intelligence to Understand What’s on Your Screen
Visual Intelligence on the Mac works differently from the camera-based experience on the iPhone. In macOS 27, I can select something already visible on my screen and ask Siri AI about it, which is useful when the thing I am looking at is easier to show than describe.
Suppose I see a chair in an image and want to know what kind of chair it is or find similar designs. Instead of describing its shape, material, and appearance, I can press Command + Shift + 6, select the chair on the screen, and choose Ask Siri to ask about it. There is also an Image Search option when I want to find visually similar results online.
Adjust How Much Liquid Glass You Want on Your Mac
Apple introduced Liquid Glass across its operating systems last year, but macOS 27 now gives you more control over how transparent the interface actually looks. Instead of having to accept one fixed appearance, there is now a slider that lets you choose how clear or tinted you want Liquid Glass to be.
To adjust it:
- Open the System Settings on your Mac and click Appearance in the sidebar.
- Find the Liquid Glass adjustment inside the Appearance settings.
- Move the slider toward the left if you want the interface to look clearer and more transparent. Move it toward the right if you want more tint and less of the background showing through.
Hide Extra Menu Bar Icons and Access Them When You Need Them
My Mac’s menu bar gets crowded quickly because several utilities I use throughout the day add their own icons. macOS 27 handles this better with a new overflow control that hides icons when there isn’t enough space and gives you a double-arrow button to reveal them whenever you need them. This means I don’t have to remove a useful menu bar utility just because I don’t need its icon visible every minute. This is especially useful on MacBooks with a notch, where menu bar space is already limited.
Let Safari Automatically Organise Your Tabs Into Topics
I am terrible at keeping my browser tabs under control, particularly when I am researching something and have several unrelated pages open at the same time. Safari already has Tab Groups on Mac, which are useful when you manually organize related tabs. macOS 27 takes this a step further by using Apple Intelligence to automatically identify related tabs and organize them into topics. Each topic gets a label and a tab count, and you can collapse a topic when you aren’t working on it without actually closing those tabs.
For example, while researching for this article, I might have 10–15 tabs open about different macOS features, along with a few Amazon shopping tabs and some work-related pages. Instead of showing all of them together in one long row, Safari can automatically identify which tabs are related and organise them into separate topics such as macOS 27, Shopping, and Work. I can keep the macOS 27 topic expanded while I am researching and collapse Shopping and Work to hide those tabs temporarily. Whenever I need them again, I can simply expand that topic without having to search through all my open tabs.
To enable it:
- Open Safari on your Mac and click Safari in the menu bar at the top left of the screen.
- Choose Settings, and then switch to Tabs section.
- Then click the drop-down menu right to Organise tabs and select Automatically Create Topics.
- Continue browsing normally and open a few pages related to the same subject. Safari will identify related tabs and place them under a topic when it recognises the connection.
Change the Perspective of a Photo With Reframe
Cropping can remove unnecessary space from a photo, but it can’t change the angle from which the photo appears to have been taken. The new Reframe feature goes further by using Apple Intelligence to change the perspective and angle of an existing image.
I find this useful when I like a photo but wish I had taken it from a slightly different angle or positioned the subject differently. To use it:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo.
- Click the Edit button in the top-right corner to open the photo editing tools.
- Click Tools and select Reframe from the available options.
- Drag the photo or use the available perspective controls to change how you want the final image to be framed. I recommend making smaller adjustments first instead of immediately trying to create a completely different camera angle.
- Once you have the angle you want, click Reframe and wait for Apple Intelligence to generate the additional parts required for the new perspective.
- Pay particular attention to faces, hands, and other objects whose shape is easy to recognize. If everything looks right, Finally click Save Changes.
Expand a Photo Beyond Its Original Frame With Extend
There have been times when I had a good portrait photo but couldn’t use it as a wallpaper or inside a presentation because converting it to a wider aspect ratio would crop an important part of the image, and where the new Extend feature comes in. It generate additional content outside the original frame with Apple Intelligence.
To try it, open the image in Photos, click Edit, and open Tools. Select Extend, drag the edges beyond the original photo or choose the aspect ratio you need, and click Extend to generate the missing area.
Check the newly generated areas carefully before saving the result. If you don’t like what it created, adjust the frame and try again instead of keeping an obviously generated section.
Remove Unwanted Objects From Photos With Clean Up
Apple introduced the Clean Up tool with Apple Intelligence, and macOS 27 improves how it handles larger unwanted objects. If I take a photo at a tourist spot and someone is standing in the background I can select that person and let Photos remove them.
Here’s how you can remove an unwanted object from a photo:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and double-click the photo you want to edit.
- Click Edit in the upper-right corner and open Tools.
- Select Clean Up, and your Mac will analyse the image. In some cases, Photos may automatically highlight objects it thinks you might want to remove.
- Click on a highlighted object to remove it, or use the Erase brush to paint over the object yourself. You can also circle the object if that makes it easier to select.
- And, finally, click Clean Up.
Resize the iPhone Mirroring Window
iPhone Mirroring is useful when I want to access something on my iPhone without picking it up, but using everything inside a phone-sized window on a large Mac display isn’t always ideal. macOS 27 fixes this by letting you resize the iPhone Mirroring window just by dragging its corner. You can also use keyboard shortcuts to quickly resize the iPhone Mirroring window. Press Command + Plus (+) to increase the window size and Command + Minus (-) to decrease it. If you want to return the window to its default size, press Command + 0.
But macOS 27 takes resizing a step further with supported apps. When you open a resizable app and make the iPhone Mirroring window wider, the app can actually adjust its layout and show more content instead of simply making the same iPhone interface bigger.
For example, if I open a supported app and drag the iPhone Mirroring window into a wider layout, I can get more usable screen space and information inside the app. Not every app supports this yet, so in unsupported apps, resizing may simply make the existing interface larger or smaller. You can press Command + 9 whenever you want to return the window to the standard iPhone size.
Let Your Mac Suggest Better Names for Files and Folders
My Downloads folder has taught me how quickly bad filenames can become a problem. A name such as “Untitled” or “Document 2” becomes useless once I forget what is inside them.
With macOS 27, Apple Intelligence can suggest names for files and folders based on what they contain. Instead of having to open a document again just to remember what it was about, macOS can look at the content and suggest a name that actually describes it.
First, you have to make sure this feature is enabled on your Mac. To do so, open Finder and click the Finder button in the menu bar. Next, choose Settings and make sure you are in the General tab. Now, check the box next to Suggest Filenames.
Now, to use this feature, right-click any document, photo, screenshot, or folder in Finder and select Rename. Wait for around five seconds, and Finder will show you a few suggested names based on the file’s contents. You can select the name you like and use it instead of typing one manually.
Create and Edit Calendar Events by Describing Them
macOS 27 makes creating Calendar events faster by describing the event naturally instead of filling in every field separately. I can type something like “Pankaj’s birthday next Monday,” and Calendar can use those details to create the event.
To try it, open Calendar, click the plus (+) button, and enter your description in Describe Event. You can also describe changes to an existing event instead of manually changing individual details.
Draw Directly Inside Apple Notes on Your Mac
Not everything you want to save in a note needs to be written as text. For example, if you’re planning the layout of a room, sketching a quick idea, making a simple diagram, or noting down something that is easier to remember visually, a quick drawing can be more useful than typing it out. With macOS 27, you can now create these drawings directly inside a note on your Mac and keep them saved along with the rest of your notes.
Previously, you could create drawings in a note from an iPhone or iPad, but macOS didn’t let you draw directly inside Notes on the Mac. Now, you can use your mouse or trackpad to create a quick sketch without leaving the Notes app.
Here’s how you can draw inside a note:
- Open the Notes app.
- Click the Markup button in the Notes toolbar to open the drawing tools.
- Choose the drawing tool you want to use, and adjust its thickness and colour depending on what you are trying to draw.
- Start drawing directly inside the note using your mouse or trackpad.
- Once you are finished, click the Markup button again to exit the drawing tools and continue working on the rest of your note.
Generate Images in More Styles With Image Playground
I tested Image Playground on Mac when Apple first introduced it, and one of my biggest complaints was how limited the available styles felt. Now, Apple has made Image Playground much more flexible in macOS 27. You now get more styles, including create photorealistic images, and the Any Style option lets you describe the kind of visual appearance you want instead of choosing only from a small set of presets. You can also choose square, portrait, or landscape output depending on where you plan to use the image.
Another change I find more useful is targeted editing. If most of the generated image looks good but there is one part I want to change, I can select that area and describe the change instead of generating the entire image again and hoping everything else remains the same.
If you are using Image Playground for the first time, I recommend reading our complete Image Playground guide for Mac, where we have covered the interface, creating images, using your own photos, and managing generated images in more detail.
Record Your Mac Screen With System Audio
This is one of my favorite smaller additions in macOS 27, especially because I regularly work on tutorials. macOS has had a built-in screen recorder for a long time, but recording the sound coming directly from the Mac hasn’t been nearly as straightforward as recording the screen itself.
The difference between system audio and microphone audio is important here. If I am recording a tutorial and an app plays a sound, system audio captures that sound directly. I don’t have to turn up my MacBook speakers and let the microphone record them along with keyboard sounds, fan noise, and everything else happening in the room.
Here’s how you can record your Mac screen with system audio:
- Press Shift + Command + 5 on your keyboard to open the built-in screenshot and screen-recording toolbar.
- Choose whether you want to Record Entire Screen, Record Selected Portion, or Selected Window depending on what you want to capture.
- Click Options in the toolbar and enable Include System Audio so that sounds playing on your Mac are included in the recording.
Add Extra-Large Widgets to Your Mac Desktop
I have been using widgets on my Mac desktop since Apple introduced them with macOS Sonoma. but the existing widget sizes don’t always work when an app has more information to show.
macOS 27 adds new Extra Large widget sizes, including a portrait layout for supported widgets. The additional space lets apps show considerably more information on the desktop.
To add an extra large widget on your desktop:
- Right-click anywhere on your Mac desktop and select Edit Widgets.
- Find the app whose widget you want to add and look through the available widget sizes. If the app supports the new sizes, you should see Extra Large or Extra Large Portrait among the options.
- Select the size you want and add the widget to your desktop.
If you haven’t used desktop widgets before, we have a complete guide explaining how to add widgets to your Mac desktop, including how to customise the widgets already on your Mac.
Share Photos and Videos in Full Resolution With Shared Albums
Shared Albums are convenient when I want to collect photos from a trip, event, or family function in one place, but there has always been a compromise: the photos and videos shared through them weren’t necessarily kept in their original quality.
Apple changes that with the new Shared Albums experience in macOS 27. Newly created permanent Shared Albums can store photos and videos at full resolution
Let Android and Windows Users Add Photos to Your Shared Albums
The Shared Albums update gets even more useful if your friends or family don’t all use Apple devices. Previously, you needed several WhatsApp chats, Google Drive folders, and people sending pictures individually
With macOS 27, people on Android and Windows can access the updated Shared Albums through a web browser, and they don’t necessarily need an Apple Account to participate. More importantly, you can allow them to contribute photos instead of limiting them to viewing the album.
Save Any Frame From a Video Directly as a Photo
Sometimes the best photo from a moment is actually hidden inside a video. Before macOS 27, if we spotted an interesting moment in a video, the easiest way to save it as a photo was to take a screenshot. But a screenshot doesn’t preserve the video frame as cleanly as a dedicated photo, and you may end up with lower quality or unwanted elements from the screen. With macOS 27, you can now save any video frame directly as a separate photo in your Photos library.
Open the video in Photos, pause it at the moment you want, and check the nearby frames until you find the best one. Then right-click the frame and select Save Video Frame as Photo. The saved frame appears in your Photos library, where you can edit and share it just like any other photo.
Start a Slideshow Directly From a Photo Album
I usually organise photos from a trip or event into an album, but when I want to show those pictures to someone, opening them one by one isn’t the nicest way to do it. macOS 27 makes this easier by letting me start a slideshow directly from an album in Photos, so I can show the entire collection without having to open every photo individually.
Slideshows themselves aren’t new on the Mac, but I like that I can now start one directly from an album I have already organised. Once the slideshow starts, I can quickly customise how it plays by changing the transition and duration, adding music, and deciding whether it should loop.
Here’s how you can start a slideshow from an album:
- Open the Photos app on your Mac and find the album you want to show.
- Control-click the album and select Start Slideshow from the menu.
- Once the slideshow starts, click Customise if you want to change how it plays.
- Adjust the Transition & Duration settings to control how quickly the photos move from one to another, and choose music if you want something playing in the background.
Change How Fast and Expressive Siri Sounds
I don’t always want Siri to speak at the same pace. If I am following instructions, a slightly slower response can be easier to understand. And if the current voice feels too slow, you can make it speak faster. macOS 27 also lets you change more than just how fast Siri speaks. On supported Macs and voices, you can also adjust how expressive the voice sounds. Increasing this setting gives Siri’s speech more variation and emphasis, which can make the spoken responses feel more natural and animated.
Get Better Resolution Support for External Displays
macOS 27 improves external display support, including 5K at 120Hz on certain compatible ultrawide monitors. Apple has also improved how macOS restores window positions and display arrangements after disconnecting and reconnecting a monitor, which I find more useful when regularly docking and undocking a MacBook.
After connecting your monitor, open System Settings, select Displays, and choose the external monitor to see the available resolutions and refresh rates.
Make Buttons and Other Controls Easier to See With Show Borders
macOS 27 adds a new Show Borders accessibility option that makes the boundaries around buttons and other interface controls easier to distinguish. This can be useful if you don’t want some controls to blend into the background with the Liquid Glass design.
To enable it, open System Settings and click Accessibility in the left sidebar. Select Display from the right-side panel, find Show Borders, and turn on the toggle next to it. You can also try Reduce Transparency from the same section if transparency itself is making parts of the interface difficult to see.
Explore Cities With More Detailed 3D Views in Apple Maps
Apple has improved the 3D city experience in Maps with more detailed buildings and surroundings in supported locations. I don’t use 3D Maps every time I need directions, but it can be useful when I want to understand the layout of an unfamiliar area before visiting it.
To try it, open Maps and search for the city or location you want to explore. Click View in the menu bar, select Show 3D Map, and enable Satellite if you want to explore the area using the detailed imagery.
Try the New Golden Gate Wallpapers and Screen Savers
Finally, macOS 27 comes with new Sunset and Night views of the Golden Gate Bridge, along with a new abstract wallpaper. The Golden Gate scenes can also be used as screen savers.
To try them, open System Settings and select Wallpaper from the left sidebar. Browse through the new macOS 27 backgrounds and select the one you want to use.
macOS 27 Feels More Useful Once You Start Finding the Smaller Changes
After trying more than 27 new macOS 27 features, creating custom Safari extensions is still the one I enjoyed the most, while several smaller additions have also made my everyday Mac experience better. If you enjoyed this guide, also check out our 27 best iOS 27 features you should try on your iPhone.
FAQs about macOS 27
1. Do All macOS 27 Features Work on Every Mac That Supports macOS 27?
No. Your Mac may support macOS 27 but still miss some features because individual features can have additional hardware, language, or region requirements.
2. Can Safari Extensions I Create Be Shared With Other People?
Not directly. Safari’s Describe Extension feature creates custom extensions for your own use. You can sync compatible extensions across your own Apple devices, but Apple currently doesn’t provide an option to send a generated extension directly to another person.
3. Can I Downgrade to macOS 26 After Installing macOS 27?
Yes, as long as macOS 26 supports your Mac. However, downgrading isn’t available like a normal software update and may require erasing your Mac and reinstalling the older macOS version. So, make sure you have a complete backup before proceeding.

The government’s attempts to provide 24×7 specialty care services in general and district hospitals is faltering, with the Health department barely able to run round-the-clock services in Punalur taluk hospital, where the initiative was piloted, despite concerns raised by stakeholders about the acute shortage of human resources in Health Services.
Health officials said that the idea had been to redeploy doctors with PG qualification, working in the periphery hospitals as assistant surgeons, at Punalur. However, this proposal has reportedly been met with stiff resistance from the local political leadership as well as the people.
Many PG doctors who had been pulled from institutions in Yeroor, Neendakara, Thevalakkara, Mayyanad, Kundara, Pathanapuram, Nedungolam, could not be retained at Punalur because of political interventions at the local level, who demanded their return.
It was last month that the Health Minister made the announcement that in the first phase, 24x7 services specialty services will be provided in General Medicine, General Surgery, Orthopaedics, Anaesthesia, Paediatrics, and Gynaecology.
The Kerala Government Medical College Officers’ Association (KGMOA) had pointed out that there are 799 vacancies of doctors in the Health Service — of which, 300 vacancies are in the specialty cadre — making it impractical that round-the-clock service provision can be made possible through just working arrangements, without post creation.
The government had, however, maintained that they had studied the patient load in various institutions and that judicious redeployment of specialist doctors from hospitals where patient load was much less, was enough for the time being to provide round-the-clock specialty services in many districts. It was pointed out that even some senior residents from Kollam Government Medical College could be utilised on working arrangement basis to provide specialty services at Punalur.
The government later placated the KGMOA that the plan was to provide specialty services from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., and teleconsultation services from 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. It was also stated that a minimum of nine specialist doctors in each medical specialty will be ensured in all hospitals so that 24x7 specialty services can be run smoothly.
Key challenges
“We could run the scheme if at least six specialist doctors could be made available in every speciality. Even that has not happened and the pressure from local political leadership could not be overcome. As for doctors, none are keen on seeing this initiative work and are unwilling to step out of their comfort zone,” a Health department official said.
At present, Punalur has just two or three PG doctors in each specialty against the nine promised.
In Malappuram, the idea was that the 24x7 specialty services can be introduced at Tirur and Nilambur by redeploying doctors from Manjeri Medical College on a temporary basis but this has not happened reportedly due to non-cooperation from doctors.
KGMOA State president PK Sunil denied that government doctors were resisting the initiative as it would affect the private practice that they are legally allowed to do after work hours.
“Only about 30% of the government doctors have the so-called “lucrative” private practice. The basic issue is that unless the human resource shortage is resolved, this plan will not work. We are not resisting the initiative but when a specialist is moved from the periphery hospital, there will be local protest,” he said.
Post creation is not as straightforward as it is being made out, as the Finance department is is no position to approve such proposals. Even during the previous government’s term, the Health department secured only 202 posts out of the 1,520 positions it sought, and that result was achieved after prolonged negotiations.
The Health department has now pushed a proposal to the government for the creation of 1,120 posts of specialist doctors and that of 520 posts of casualty medical officers, sources said.

AI applications need up-to-date information and clear rules on what they can access to work reliably at scale, according to executives speaking at the inaugural edition of Inc42’s ‘The CTO Summit 2026’ in Bengaluru. The challenge is to make information spread across databases, data warehouses, and documents available to these applications while preserving its quality and controlling its use. The panel, ‘Building The Data Foundation For AI At Scale’, featured PhonePe’s head of engineering, merchant payments, Kisalay Ranjan; OceanBase’s GM, India business, Bhanu Jamwal; and Fibe’s CTO Anil Sinha. Digio EIR Kshitij Shah moderated the discussion. Ranjan said PhonePe tracks where data comes from and sets rules for its use at the level of individual data elements, across both transactional databases and data warehouses. Adding these controls later through individual applications becomes increasingly difficult as companies automate more tasks, he said. “The power is first ensuring that whatever data we are consuming is of high quality,” Ranjan said. Teams must also know where information is stored, whether it is sensitive, whether its use meets compliance requirements, and which applications can access it. PhonePe uses shared platforms to maintain a single authoritative source of sensitive customer data instead of duplicating it across systems, he added. Jamwal said organisations’ data is spread across separate systems used to process transactions, run analytics, and support AI searches, alongside data lakes. Companies deploying AI agents need to connect these sources so their applications can retrieve current information quickly and accurately, he said. “There would be a time when you need high accuracy for your agents,” Jamwal said. “You need one single solution which can give you data sitting at one point, but more importantly, give you that fresh data with low latency.” The OceanBase executive advocated a unified data layer to make information across these systems available to agents and other AI applications with minimal delay. At IPO-bound lending tech startup Fibe, the focus includes extracting useful information from documents that vary in format, such as records from hospitals, clinics, and educational institutions. Sinha said Fibe uses generative AI to extract signals from these documents and feeds the signals into its existing credit model, rather than asking GenAI to make lending decisions. He said the model has expanded from 8,000 to 23,000 variables as the company incorporates more information. Beyond data quality and access, companies also have to balance AI model performance against cost and response times. Ranjan said smaller models running within PhonePe’s own technology environment can suit tasks that involve large volumes and require quick responses. More advanced models may be useful for tasks requiring stronger reasoning, with the choice depending on the use case, model availability, and cost. The emphasis on underlying systems also featured in a separate session at the CTO Summit, where Razorpay’s SVP of engineering Prabhu Ram cautioned that AI cannot compensate for weak engineering foundations, including inadequate systems for monitoring performance and detecting problems.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Thursday that the government will draw up an action plan by the end of the year to promote the use of artificial intelligence, which she regards as an accelerator for economic growth.
“The societal implementation of high-performance AI is essential for realizing the government’s growth strategy,” Takaichi said at a meeting of the Council for Japan’s Growth Strategy.
She instructed relevant Cabinet ministers to compile a concrete vision for AI utilization, as well as regulatory and institutional reforms.
At the meeting, participants discussed a growth strategy implementation program to be compiled at year-end alongside the government’s budget proposal for fiscal 2027.
Takaichi said her government will designate the five years starting next April as an intensive period to promote public and private investment in 17 strategic sectors, including AI and semiconductors, and include priority sectors and investment amounts in the program.
In the priority sectors, projects that are expected to effectively boost the potential growth rate will be identified based on factors such as profitability and ripple effects.
To provide predictability for private-sector companies, the government will also clarify budgetary measures spanning multiple fiscal years.
The government plans to manage sectors of particular importance to economic security separately in a special account, contingent on projects that contribute to ensuring “autonomy of the socioeconomic structure,” “competitive advantage over other countries and regions” and “indispensability to the international community.”
Takaichi also instructed Cabinet ministers to compile a policy package aimed at resolving labor shortages in the construction sector, which could hinder growth-oriented investment.

Taiwan confronts surge in drug-driving as new narcotics rapidly emerge
“Zombie vapes”, online dealers and new, unlisted narcotics. CNA examines how deadly drug-driving cases are a visible sign of a much wider drug problem in Taiwan.
TAIPEI/KAOHSIUNG: Taiwan is known for having some of Asia's toughest drunk-driving laws, but authorities are now confronting another threat on its roads: Drug-driving.
At a late-night police checkpoint in Taipei, officers have only a few seconds to decide which vehicles require a closer look.
“We will pay attention to vehicles as they approach and after they spot our checkpoint, whether they brake suddenly, swerve or possibly make an abrupt stop by the roadside,” police sergeant Chen Kuan-ting told CNA.
Officers also check whether drivers appear unfocused or mentally sluggish.
When drug use is suspected, they can screen motorists on the spot using a saliva test. The test can detect substances including etomidate, an emerging drug commonly consumed through electronic cigarettes.
The introduction of roadside screening in 2025 has also helped police detect more cases.
Drug-driving cases rose from 43 in 2021 to 8,659 in 2025 – an increase of more than 200 times.
Crashes involving drug-driving killed 19 people and injured 229 in 2025, up from 11 deaths and 85 injuries a year earlier.
But drug-driving is only one part of a wider challenge, as Taiwan confronts a rapidly changing illicit drug market.
THE “ZOMBIE VAPE”
Among the substances to emerge in recent years is etomidate. Originally developed as a medical anaesthetic, etomidate has become known as the “zombie vape” when consumed through e-cigarettes.
“Etomidate is a depressant for the central nervous system,” said Alex Chao, deputy director of the Drug Enforcement Division at Taiwan's Investigation Bureau.
“Its side effects are that it can make people dizzy and nauseous, and it can cause the limbs to twitch. In severe cases, the limbs will convulse, so using this can lead to some impairment of movement or involuntary movements.”
Chao said the number of positive urine tests for etomidate jumped fivefold in 2024 from a year earlier, prompting authorities to tighten controls over the substance.
Etomidate was upgraded to a Category 1 drug in June 2026, increasing the penalties for offences involving the substance.
RACE TO IDENTIFY UNLISTED DRUGS
The emergence of new substances is a continuing challenge for Taiwan’s authorities.
Inside the Investigation Bureau's forensic laboratory, around 30,000 drug samples from about 2,400 major cases are examined every year.
Most can be matched against substances already in its database. The harder cases involve compounds scientists have never encountered before.
“The big challenge we face here is that new types of drugs, and the (so-called) ‘precursor materials’ for them mutate rapidly,” Chao said.
The laboratory encounters about four to five previously unlisted substances each year.
Such substances must first be identified before authorities can decide whether to control them – a process that takes time.
“Some unscrupulous individuals may exploit this small loophole to modify the structure of banned substances,” said Investigation Bureau laboratory investigator Yen Yao-te.
“This then turns it into a banned substance that isn't on the scheduled list, which means it temporarily can't be regulated, (and it could be) an emerging drug that may be harmful to the human body.”
Once scientists have identified a new substance, their findings are submitted to the Ministry of Justice's Drug Advisory Committee, which considers whether it should be classified as a controlled drug.
According to Investigation Bureau statistics, more than 90 per cent of drugs in Taiwan come from overseas, Chao said. They can arrive with travellers, through international parcels, or in larger shipments carried aboard ships or inside cargo containers.
THE STRUGGLE WITH LIFELONG ADDICTION
Supply is one challenge. Drug use and addiction are another.
More than 47,000 drug suspects were arrested in Taiwan in 2025, according to the National Police Agency – 25 per cent more than the previous year.
The biggest increase was seen among young people. Arrests of suspects aged 12 to 17 increased nearly 68 per cent, while those involving people aged 18 to 23 rose 41 per cent.
At the government-run Kaohsiung Drug Abuser Treatment Center in southern Taiwan, more than 1,000 people pass through its drug observation programme each year.
Among them is Peter Yu, 38, whose struggle with drugs began as a teenager. He has been detained four or five times since.
“I saw an older friend taking amphetamines. I didn't even know what it was. I was curious. He gave me some and I tried it,” he said.
“If you wanted to get drugs, it was pretty easy to obtain some. Because you're in that circle, everyone's using. You just ask your drug buddies. They'll show you where to get it or get it for you.”
Another patient, Chou Chih-ming, started abusing drugs much later, at 35.
“I was hooked from the start. That one injection plunged me into addiction. It even ended my 16-year marriage. I've spent about 17 years in and out of prison, seven times,” he said.
Chou moved house three times while trying to restart his life, but he could never put enough distance between him and the drugs.
“The hardest part of quitting is your mind and your circle of friends. Even after you've been out for a while, you meet an old friend, they say one thing and it can bring all those thoughts back.”
The centre tries to prepare patients for life after release through counselling and skills training, while helping them rebuild family relationships and find work.
“What worries us most is what happens after they leave,” said counsellor Ko Chun-ming.
“If they go back to those complicated environments. Once you have an addiction, it's a lifelong thing. There's no such thing as successfully quitting drugs, only how long you've stayed clean.”
DRUG DEALING PREVALENT ONLINE
But access to drugs has moved beyond personal networks.
Ko estimated that 70 to 80 per cent of the drug trade was taking place online, with drugs being sold through social media platforms and online groups.
“Nikkie” began using drugs when she was 18 and, at one point, spent more than US$3,000 a month on them.
The 23-year-old, who has been drug-free for almost a year, asked to use a pseudonym to protect her identity.
She showed CNA how she used to buy drugs online.
A friend would give her the WeChat contact of a dealer. She would message the account with her order and a delivery location.
“If I wanted etomidate, I'd order one or two cartridges and give them the address. They'd drive over. I'd give them the money. They'd give me the drugs and then leave,” she recounted.
The entire transaction could take less than an hour, she said.
E-cigarettes have been banned in Taiwan since 2023, but CNA was able to access a website selling them by bypassing a Ministry of Health and Welfare block.
CNA contacted one account, received a reply and went no further.
Responding to queries, Taiwan's National Police Agency said the internet has become one of the main channels for drug dealing.
From January 2025 to June 2026, police arrested 6,708 suspects accused of supplying drugs online. They accounted for about 85 per cent of all suspected drug dealers arrested during the period.
Nikkie said she has helped police in two operations.
“I show the police the call records. Then, I make a statement identifying the person. After that, I arrange to meet them to collect the drugs.”
But she said dealers could quickly set up new accounts after arrests.
STEPPING UP ENFORCEMENT
Along with targeting dealers online, police are also carrying out enforcement at venues where drugs may be used or sold.
At nightclubs in Taipei, officers conduct identity checks, look for wanted suspects and pay closer attention to people with previous drug offences.
The government is also expanding its enforcement network.
Minister without Portfolio Chi Lien-cheng, who is overseeing an anti-drug enforcement effort launched this year, said in June that a drug enforcement command centre would be established at the Taiwan High Prosecutors Office, with “war rooms” at district prosecutors' offices around the island.
The aim is to pool resources and improve coordination among the authorities involved in drug enforcement, Chi said.
Authorities also plan to establish 9,000 inspection points around more than 3,600 schools, concentrating on places where students gather and locations linked to previous drug incidents.
The government also wants schools to make greater use of anti-drug campaigns.
“If every school could run these short videos on the electronic display boards at their gates, then students would know … just how serious the harm from this drug epidemic is for their bodies and minds, and to their families,” Chi said.
"I CAN'T LET HIS DEATH BE FOR NOTHING"
Observers say drug-driving is one of the most visible signs of Taiwan's wider drug problem.
A series of deadly crashes has left some people fearful even of crossing the road, while others worry that drugs are reaching their children.
Among those demanding action are families who have lost loved ones.
One case that drew widespread attention was the death of Liu Tsung-hsin, a police station chief in New Taipei City, in 2024. He was killed after a drug-impaired driver refused a police check and dragged him with her vehicle before he struck a guardrail.
His father Liu Chih-yuan, 63, has since called for stronger government action.
“I want to tell the government they need to take this drug epidemic seriously because there are so many undeniable facts now. Drugs have already made their way into schools. Even teenagers are using,” he said.
He also called on authorities to trace where the drugs were coming from.
“Only then can they cut off the supply, only then will drug use come down and only then can (Taiwan) and society find stability,” he added.
The government has moved to toughen penalties for drug-driving.
In June, Taiwan's Cabinet approved draft amendments that would raise the maximum prison term from three to five years, with heavier sentences when serious injury or death is caused. The changes still require legislative approval.
For families affected by drug-driving, the impact of those efforts will ultimately be felt on Taiwan's streets.
“I can't let Tsung-hsin's death be for nothing,” Liu said.

One day after he rejected an Iranian proposal to end the war, President Trump told Axios in a phone interview on Sunday that he expects U.S. negotiators to engage in more talks with the country this week.
Why it matters: Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, but the two sides are far apart on the key issues.
While Iran wants to focus any talks on the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. naval blockade, the Trump administration is demanding that Iran agree to nuclear concessions.
Two regional sources confirmed Trump's comment about more talks this week. They said they expect another round of indirect dialogue between the U.S. and Iran as early as Monday. But it isn't clear if the gaps can be bridged.
What he's saying: "I expect more talks with Iran [this week]. They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make. It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand," Trump said.
Asked if he is considering resuming strikes against Iran, Trump said: "I am always thinking about it."
State of play: In the meantime, Trump said, the U.S. military is facilitating a lot of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz.
He said that over the weekend the largest amount of oil transited through the strait since the war began. "More than 20 million barrels," Trump said.
A U.S. defense official confirmed Trump's assertion, saying that on Friday night 22 million barrels of oil were exported through the strait.
Driving the news: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held a new round of indirect negotiations with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York last Tuesday.
Qatari officials participated, passing messages between the two sides.
Araghchi delivered to Witkoff and Kushner Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks.
Iran proposed reopening the strait and restarting nuclear talks in a week, if the U.S. lifts its naval blockade, removes sanctions on oil sales and reinstates a ceasefire across the region.
Trump rejected the Iranian proposal on Saturday.
Behind the scenes: But a U.S. official and two regional sources told Axios that Qatari mediators are continuing shuttle diplomacy to try to reach a deal.
On Thursday, the prime minister of Qatar met in New York with the Iranian president and discussed the potential deal with the Trump administration.
Shortly after, senior Qatari officials met Witkoff and briefed him.
A regional source with knowledge of the indirect negotiations said the Qatari mediators discussed the original Iranian proposal with both parties and provided a compromise proposal to both sides to review.
What to watch: Over the weekend, the Qatari mediators have been going back and forth separately with Iranian and U.S. negotiators on changes to the text.
Qatari mediators are expected to meet separately with Araghchi and Witkoff as early as Monday.
The other side: Araghchi told NBC on Sunday that despite Trump's rejection of the Iranian proposal, Iran still wants a diplomatic solution.
He said that the midterm elections aren't part of Iran's calculations. "We only care about our national interests. We are ready for negotiations," he said.
"Although we heard from President Trump that he's rejecting this deal ... we are still waiting for an official response through the mediators," Araghchi added.

SC declines One Nation One Election panel's proposal to interact with CJI Kant, others
Legal experts voiced alarm over the proposed interactions, marking significant discussions around the constitutional implications of upcoming electoral changes.
The Supreme Court administration on Thursday declined a proposal from a parliamentary panel, examining bills aimed at rolling out simultaneous elections, to interact with Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and other sitting judges, with the court’s secretary general informing the committee that the proposed constitutional amendments could eventually be subject to judicial review.
People aware of the matter said that the apex court secretary general’s office, in a communication sent to the joint committee of Parliament on Thursday afternoon, stated that the proposal for an informal discussion with the CJI and other judges on simultaneous elections was discussed among the Supreme Court’s senior judges.
The communication, people cited above said, stated that as the proposed amendment might become a subject of judicial review before the Supreme Court, it may not be expedient or desirable to discuss the issue on the administrative side. The proposed meeting was accordingly “cancelled.”
The decision followed a discussion between CJI Surya Kant and some senior judges, after which the CJI directed that the proposed interaction should not proceed, the people cited above said.
The joint committee chairman and Bharatiya Janata Party member PP Chaudhary told news agency PTI that the visit was put off as the dates of committee members did not match. “I also have other commitments to attend to,” he told the agency.
Also Read | Plea seeks recall of SC order on challenge to CEC appointment law
The communication from the secretary general’s office came even as earlier in the day, independent Rajya Sabha member and senior advocate Kapil Sibal publicly objected to the proposed visit, describing it as “unconstitutional” and contrary to the principle of separation of powers.
The joint committee, headed by Chaudhary, had proposed a visit to the Supreme Court on October 6 as part of its consultations on the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024. The programme described the visit as a “local study visit” and proposed an informal discussion with the CJI and other judges on simultaneous elections.
The developments came against the backdrop of growing concern over the propriety of a parliamentary committee discussing the merits or constitutional implications of proposed legislation with sitting Supreme Court judges when the legislation could eventually come before the court for adjudication.
Sibal, at a press conference on Thursday, said he was “shocked” by the proposed interaction and questioned how the judiciary could accept an invitation from a parliamentary committee when the bills raised issues of “fundamental importance to the polity of this country” and to the working of the Constitution.
Also Read | Supreme Court to hear plea raising doubts over CEC Gyanesh Kumar's decisions next week
“How did the judiciary accept that invitation from the joint committee, knowing full well that this bill raises issues of fundamental importance to the polity of this country, fundamental issues relating to the working of our Constitution?” Sibal asked.
He said Parliament has the prerogative to introduce and consider legislation, with a parliamentary committee examining a bill and submitting its report to the House. Parliament would thereafter debate and vote on the legislation, while its constitutional validity, if challenged, would be considered by the judiciary.
Sibal said he had never encountered an instance in the country’s history of a parliamentary panel holding an interaction with sitting Supreme Court judges on legislation that could subsequently be challenged before the court.
The Supreme Court’s communication, however, confined the reason for cancelling the interaction to the view expressed by the CJI and senior judges that discussing the issue on the administrative side would not be “expedient or desirable” since the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review.
The joint committee is examining two bills that seek to facilitate simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes, among other things, insertion of a new Article 82A dealing with simultaneous elections and amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327. The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes consequential changes to facilitate simultaneous elections in the Union territories as well.
Also Read | SC asks Election Commission to resolve TMC factions’ symbol row within 3 months
Both bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and referred to the joint committee for examination. The committee comprises members from both Houses and is headed by Chaudhary.
The committee has conducted consultations with political parties, legislators, constitutional experts and other stakeholders on the proposed electoral changes. It has also consulted former Chief Justices of India, former Supreme Court judges and other legal experts on the constitutional questions surrounding simultaneous elections.
The proposal, commonly described as “One Nation, One Election”, seeks to align elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. The government has argued that simultaneous elections would reduce the frequency and cost of elections and provide greater continuity for governance, while Opposition parties and other critics have raised concerns relating to democratic accountability, federalism and the constitutional implications of synchronising the terms of elected legislatures.

Dawood Ahmed of M/s RS Profiling has been elected president of the Association of Industrialists, Industrial Estate Rangreth, for the 2026–28 term.
A statement issued here said that the election was held on Tuesday through a voting process, with polling conducted from 10 am to 12 noon. The Election Commission said the electoral process was completed peacefully and in an orderly manner.
Nasrullah Jan of JKW Associates was elected vice president, while Mumtaz Gilani of M/s Admiral Phones was elected general secretary.
Yaseen Samdani of Rahimi Laboratories was elected finance secretary, while Farooq Ahmed of Chinar Electricals was elected publicity secretary.
The results were formally declared by the Election Commission following the completion of polling and other electoral proceedings.

WASHINGTON — The Trump administration published a final rule aimed at lowering Medicare prices for drugs administered in doctor offices. It applies to only four companies.
The Global Benchmark for Efficient Drug Pricing, or GLOBE, is one of two mandatory pilot programs that are part of President Trump’s plan to get drugmakers to lower prices in Medicare to levels charged in other rich countries, a policy generally referred to as most-favored nation pricing. The other pilot, called GUARD, is still in the proposed stage.
The pilots are tied to Trump’s separate voluntary deals with drugmakers to offer MFN prices to drugs for Medicaid recipients. The companies that struck those deals are exempt from the GLOBE pilot, according to the model’s final rule.
The initial proposal did not contemplate excluding companies based on separate voluntary deals with the administration, and as a result included many more drugs. The final rule says GLOBE will now apply to four companies, but it does not specify which ones.
The rule also excludes drugs for rare diseases. However, drugs that treat both rare diseases and other conditions that are not rare will not receive the exclusion.
Medicare actuaries estimate the model’s estimated savings have been reduced from nearly $12 billion in the proposed rule to $440 million now. Thomas Hwang, a Harvard researcher who studied GLOBE’s potential savings, said that reduction is in line with his estimate.

After introducing PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) on PS5 Pro, PlayStation is bringing a new tier of AI upscaling to the base PS5 with Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR). According to PlayStation’s latest blog, QSSR came from Project Amethyst, PlayStation’s AI graphics collaboration with AMD, and the upscaling tech builds on PSSR with two key improvements: a more efficient neural network and a hand-optimized implementation designed to maximize performance on the PS5.
QSSR offers noticeable improvements to both image quality and detail, and will appear as an additional graphics mode, likely next to Fidelity or Performance, in Marvel’s Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei today. This comes just in time for the Ghost of Yotei’s Echoes of Sekigahara expansion.

Leaders from Imran Khan’s party have vowed to go ahead with a nationwide demonstration in Pakistan to demand the former prime minister’s release, even as the government deployed tens of thousands of police to Islamabad, barricaded highways and issued arrest warrants to try to stop the march.
The state has taken extreme measures to prevent Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party from proceeding with the march. It was announced after mounting concerns of the treatment of Khan, who has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges.
On Friday, PTI leaders said they would postpone the start of the march until 4 October, a week after the original 27 September date, saying they hoped the delay would put further strain on the government.
Analysts said the protest could present a major challenge to the military-backed government, which is widely regarded as weak, illegitimate and unpopular, while Khan remains a popular rallying figure. The ruling coalition is led by the prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, but the army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, is widely seen as the country’s de facto leader.
This week, dozens of PTI leaders and ministers have been detained or made subject of arrest warrants, while Khan’s three sisters were arrested on Monday and remain in jail, charged with posing a grave threat to security.
Among those facing arrest is Sohail Afridi, the chief minister of Khan’s home province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, PTI’s stronghold, from where thousands of supporters are expected to join the march to the capital.
Afridi said the PTI would carry out the march unless the government made significant concessions over Khan’s treatment and conditions in jail, including a fair hearing for Khan’s cases.
“The government is panicking – that’s why they have put Islamabad under siege, that’s why they are abducting our ministers,” he said. “But Imran Khan is the most popular leader of the country and people will come out for him. I am certain they won’t be able to stop the public power of the masses when they come out on streets and take to Islamabad.”
Afridi acknowledged that the scale of the security deployment had led many to fear there could be a violent confrontation to prevent Khan’s supporters from entering the capital, as had been seen in previous demonstrations.
The government has already deployed tens of thousands of security officials to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and shut down the main highway connecting the provincial capital, Peshawar, to Islamabad.
“I know they can go to any extent to stop us by brute force, we have no doubt about it,” Afridi said. “But if we have a large number of people, they can’t open fire at us. Our plan is to bring so many people that they surrender.”
Faisal Karim Kundi, a central government appointee as governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, defended the security measures being taken against PTI as precautionary and accused the party of trying to create “instability and violence”. “The state can’t allow any violent group to march on Islamabad,” Kundi said.
Public frustration has mounted in Islamabad as the government’s measures to stop Khan’s party supporters having any way to enter the capital has led to the city resembling a high-security fortress.
More than 1,000 shipping containers, many fortified with spikes, have blockaded roads and sandbags were placed on bridges, while a key highway into the capital was closed. Public gatherings have been banned in Islamabad and 22,000 police and other security personnel have been deployed across the capital.
The government’s shutdown has fuelled anger and frustration in the capital, with many businesses unable to get supplies. Shahid, 76, a retired businessman, said: “The entire city is suffering. The government has shut down the whole city and we, as citizens, are helpless. I have never seen such a situation. Joblessness, inflation and insecurity has made our lives hell but does the government care? No.”
Despite the considerable efforts by the government and the military to crush Khan’s party and remove the former prime minister from the public consciousness – with media organisations instructed to not even refer to him by name – Khan is still viewed by many as the political alternative to the current regime.
The PTI alleges Khan is being held in solitary confinement and has been denied adequate medical treatment and any contact with his family or his lawyers for months.
Khan denies all the charges against him and alleges he is being imprisoned due to the political threat he poses to the government and the military. All but one of the court rulings against Khan have been overturned.
Analysts say the government and its military backers fear the PTI protest could escalate into a movement that could topple their administration, similar to protests seen in nearby Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
“They have an eye on what has happened in south Asia over the last five years, where country after country has seen huge protests snowballing suddenly out of nowhere and sweeping away a government,” said Niaz Murtaza, a Pakistani political columnist.
“Given the breadth of grievances in Pakistan at the moment, the performance of the government has been so poor on the economy and security, while the repression is so high, that they are very nervous that the whole situation could combust very quickly.”

ICE has received more than $75 billion to expand operations since President Trump returned to office — and wasted millions on scaled-back and mismanaged projects, a new GAO report found.
Why it matters: In rushing to execute Trump's mass deportation agenda, the agency failed to properly develop a strategic plan, according to the Government Accountability Office report.
Driving the news: The report found that ICE invested billions in six new initiatives without conducting necessary analyses.
The report concluded that "[i]n the absence of a comprehensive strategic plan to guide detention expansion, ICE has wasted funds on unsuccessful detention initiatives and lacks important information about the long-term affordability of its investments."
For example, the agency purchased more than $2.5 billion in detention facilities and warehouses but didn't calculate how much the properties would cost to maintain after the first three years, when its current federal funding will expire without additional congressional authorization.
Catch up quick:ICE received an unprecedented amount of money to bolster operations, including $45 billion through the One Big Beautiful Bill in 2025 and more than $31 billion from the Secure America Act in June 2026.
That additional funding helped increase ICE's daily detained population by 71% between January 2025 and July 2026.
By the numbers: ICE rushed to purchase 11 warehouses to be converted into immigration facilities, but in June 2026, ICE officials told GAO that they were going to sell seven of them.
The reported cost of all 11 warehouses was roughly $1.07 billion. The sell-off caused ICE to lose about $7.7 million in nonrecoverable purchasing costs, such as zoning assessments.
ICE continues to pay utilities and security costs at these locations, costing an additional $12.8 million, per August estimates.
The agency also spent $7.1 million on unneeded meals at Fort Bliss because the vendor contract didn't allow for fluctuations in occupancy levels. At Guantanamo Bay, the Defense Department spent $2.85 million assembling tents that were never used after Homeland Security determined they "did not meet detention standards."
Zoom out: In some cases, the agency bypassed its normal contracting procedures, without negotiating costs.
At the since-shuttered, so-called Alligator Alcatraz in Florida, the bed rate was $249 per day, approximately 171% higher than ICE's median rate of $92.
What we're watching: GAO recommended ICE develop a comprehensive strategic plan, and the Department of Homeland Security agreed.
But ICE projected that the plan won't be completed until Aug. 31, 2027, prompting GAO to conclude that given the "potential for continued waste of taxpayer dollars, more timely completion may be warranted."
The White House referred Axios to DHS for a request to comment. DHS did not respond to repeated requests for comment.

Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami
- Published
As Nigeria begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign, former international Segun Odegbami, who won the tournament on home soil in 1980, says the country is experiencing the "worst time" in its football history.
Over the past 12 months both the Super Eagles and Super Falcons failed to qualify for their respective Fifa World Cups.
But beyond the failure of the senior national teams, Nigeria has also endured disappointing results at age-group level and in African club competitions - although the West Africans recently reached the quarter-finals of the Under-20 Women's World Cup.
Odegbami says the diminishing returns represent a "tectonic shift" for one of the continent's traditional powers.
"It has never been this bad in our entire history that we didn't qualify for the World Cup," the 74-year-old told BBC Sport Africa.
"Our girls (the Super Falcons), who were African champions, failed to win a competition (the 2025 Women's Afcon) that was just there for their taking. All our junior teams are not doing well.
"Our local league is not bringing in money. Something is definitely wrong."
The crisis has already triggered major changes within the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).
Its president Ibrahim Gusau, general secretary Mohammed Sanusi and multiple members of the federation's executive committee resigned last month following mounting criticism.
Odegbami says Nigerian football had not been represented by its "first XI administrators" and has called for a restructure to create the conditions for long-term development.
"The outcry by Nigerians was total. Everybody wanted them out, to the extent that the President of the country himself (Bola Tinubu) made the pronouncement that he wanted reforms," he said.
"Everything came together like a jigsaw puzzle and is working now for us to produce a blueprint that will cover every aspect of our football development."
- 'Motherhood should not be the end of anyone's story' 
  - Published23 July
Sweeping changes at the NFF
A joint delegation from world governing body Fifa and the Confederation of African Football (Caf) has been involved in discussions with the National Sports Commission (NSC) over the future structure of Nigerian football.
The parties are working towards a roadmap for comprehensive reforms but NFF elections, scheduled for 27 September, have been suspended.
President Tinubu stated his desire for reform to overcome what he called "repeated failures".
Emmanuel Ikpeme has been appointed NFF interim general secretary, with Ademola Olajire the interim deputy general secretary.
The changes have prompted renewed debate among stakeholders over whether the country needs a deeper restructuring.
Nigerian sports journalist Fisayo Dairo believes any reform must extend beyond a change in leadership.
"The reform should be the setting up of a proper framework and structure that our football can thrive on," Dairo told BBC Sport Africa.
"[We need to] develop national teams, harness talent from the grassroots and have governance that incorporates all forms of stakeholders.
"The corporate world has to be fully represented so that the administration is able to generate funds."
'What is Nigeria's football style?'
For Odegbami, the current situation is a stark contrast to the era in which he helped transform the Nigerian game.
Nicknamed 'Mathematical' for his precision and skill on the ball, the forward was part of the Super Eagles side that won the country's first continental title in 1980, beating Algeria 3-0 in the final in Lagos.
"We had unprecedented support and fortunately the stars aligned with us," he said.
"It was an indescribable atmosphere during that period.
"That experience you can't even describe and compare. [It remains] indelible in our minds."
Nigeria lifted the Afcon trophy again in 1994 and 2013, and finished as runners-up at the 2023 edition.
The team also finished third in 2019 and at this year's finals in Morocco.
However, Odegbami argues sport has "not been a priority" of successive governments and believes his nation has been failed by football administrators since the mid 1990s.
"The pilots are not guiding us well, they haven't guided us well," he said.
"And that has affected every aspect of our football development: the grassroots, the discovery of players, the development of the players, the establishment of the institutions that will take care of them, the academies, the clubs that they will go into both locally and internationally.
"What is the coaching methodology? What is the philosophy of our football in the country?
"What is our culture, what is our style?"
Decaying infrastructure
Yet, alongside the failure to reach the past two men's World Cups, concerns over deteriorating infrastructure and inadequate investment have become recurring themes in discussions about the state of the Nigerian game.
Across Africa, meanwhile, other nations have continued to invest in hosting major competitions.
Senegal will be the venue for the Youth Olympic Games next month, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia are holding next year's men's Cricket World Cup, Kenya will stage the 2029 World Athletics Championship, and Morocco will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Spain and Portugal.
Odegbami has bemoaned the fact that top-class stadiums which Nigeria used to possess have fallen into disrepair after being neglected.
He name-checked the National Stadium in Surulere, Lagos, which hosted games during the 1980 and 2000 Afcons, the Liberty Stadium (now Obafemi Awolowo Stadium) in Ibadan, Kaduna's Ahmadu Bello Stadium and the UJ Esuene Stadium in Calabar.
"I weep when I think of the amount of damage they have done to Nigerian football - the infrastructure that we had in the country, some of the historic monuments that were facilities for football in this country," he said.
"Whether it was wilful, whether it was ignorance, they did irreparable damage to what was Nigeria's heritage.
"Uyo is the best we have in Nigeria, but it is not half as good as what we had from the 1960s to the 90s."
The Super Eagles will begin their Afcon 2027 qualifying campaign against Madagascar at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo on Friday (16:00 GMT) before travelling to Guinea-Bissau on 29 September.

Somali pirates killed oil tanker crew before rescue, official tells BBC
- Published
Five crew members of an oil tanker seized by pirates off the coast of Somalia were killed before local security forces retook the vessel, a senior regional official has told the BBC.
Puntland Deputy Information Minister Bile Qabowsade said the five were killed by pirates before regional forces boarded MT Hoarner 25.
He said the dead included three Pakistani nationals, one Indian and one national of Myanmar. Four other crew members were injured, including three Pakistanis and one Indian.
The tanker, which was carrying about 18,500 barrels of oil destined for the Somali capital, Mogadishu, was seized in April by six armed men while sailing off the coast of Somalia.
Sixteen suspected pirates have been arrested, while others escaped and were being pursued, officials said.
Qabowsade rejected suggestions that forces from Puntland, a semi-autonomous region of Somalia, had helped some of the pirates escape. The authorities have not given further details how the five crew members were killed or how the pirates took control of the vessel.
The hijacked tanker was anchored near the Somali coast between the fishing towns of Xaafun and Bander Beyla.
In April, officials had said there were 17 crew members on board when the vessel was hijacked. They included 10 Pakistanis, four Indonesians, one Indian, one Sri Lankan and a Myanmar national.
Piracy off the Somali coast fell sharply after 2011 following international naval operations, but attacks and hijackings have increased again in recent years.

Judge dismisses sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys star Mike Smith
Complainant says trial dismissed because she was 'unwilling to sacrifice' mental health to proceed
A Nova Scotia judge dismissed a sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys actor Mike Smith on Thursday, as the complainant tells CBC News she decided the emotional toll of testifying would be too difficult to endure.
The three-day trial of Smith, known for playing Bubbles on the comedy series, was set to begin on Thursday in provincial court in Dartmouth, N.S.
But the Crown offered no evidence in the case, so the defence requested the case be dismissed. Judge Jill Hartlen dismissed it.
Smith, 54, was charged in October 2025 with sexual assault in relation to an alleged assault on Dec. 30, 2017, in Dartmouth.
He pleaded not guilty to the charge in February.
CBC spoke with the complainant, who cannot be named due to a publication ban on her identity, on Wednesday.
In a statement, she said the trial was dismissed "because I am unwilling to sacrifice my mental health" by testifying.
The statement says evidence in sexual assault cases "hinges almost exclusively on the testimony of the victim."
"This process retraumatizes survivors, subjecting their experiences to dissecting public scrutiny. Meanwhile, the accused seldom speak; they are exempt from the pain of taking the stand, giving testimony, and facing cross-examination," the statement reads.
Crown prosecutor Bryson McDonald declined to confirm Thursday that the complainant had refused to testify.
He told reporters he could not discuss private communications between the Crown and the complainant.
"The Crown made the assessment based on our prosecution standard that we felt that the realistic prospect of conviction was no longer there," McDonald said, noting that the determination was made this week.
The complainant said in her statement that since the burden of evidence in sexual assault cases relies so heavily on the character of the witness, victims face "character assassination" during cross-examinations, and defence lawyers can even "insinuate that victims played a part in the crime — or deserved it."
"I am intimidated by a system, despite it being 2026, where defence attorneys still use tactics that blame victims for surviving and reporting sexual assaults," the statement continues.
"I know what happened that night in 2017. My stepping away from the case does not change the facts of that incident. Rather, it is a gesture of reclaiming my agency after investigating options within a system that strips me of my voice."
Speaking with reporters after the case was dismissed, Smith's lawyer, Stan MacDonald, said his client is "pleased that this matter is now behind him and he's ready to move forward."
A statement issued Thursday morning by Trailer Park Boys Incorporated said now that the court matter has concluded, Smith is resuming his responsibilities with the company. He previously held the role of managing director.

England avoid Australia & India in World Cup draw
- Published
England have avoided defending champions Australia and world number one-ranked side India in the group-stage draw for the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.
India and Pakistan are, once again, placed in the same group, alongside Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier.
England, who won the trophy in 2019, are in the same group as co-hosts South Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, New Zealand and a qualifier.
Harry Brook's side, who have enjoyed a resurgence in the 50-over format, begin their campaign against Bangladesh on 8 October, and Sri Lanka on 13 October in Windhoek, Namibia.
They will come up against South Africa in Gqeberha on 16 October before travelling to Harare to face a qualifier on 20 October. They round off the group stage when they face New Zealand, again in Gqeberha, on 23 October.
The visit to Zimbabwe is significant, with England having not played there since 2004.
Political unrest in Zimbabwe under the regime of former president Robert Mugabe caused problems for England's men's team throughout the 2000s.
England boycotted their fixture against Zimbabwe in Harare at the 2003 World Cup - a decision which ultimately derailed their campaign.
Relations have improved in recent years, however, and BBC Sport reported in 2025 that the two cricket boards were discussing a potential England tour of the country in the next cycle of international cricket between 2027 and 2031.
After three matches to decide the final two qualifiers, the tournament group stage will open with a repeat of the 2023 final when India and Australia face each other in Cape Town on 7 October.
Arch-rivals India and Pakistan, who do not play each other outside tournaments, will meet in Johannesburg on 10 October.
The top three, plus the best fourth-placed finisher, from the two groups progress to the Super 7 stage.
From there, the top four teams will qualify for the semi-finals, which are scheduled for 17 and 18 November, before the final on 21 November in Johannesburg.

May become matter of judicial review: SC wrote to ONOE panel
