Kerala High Court allows 30-week pregnancy termination for rape survivor
The Kerala High Court allowed the medical termination of a 30-week pregnancy of a 15-year-old rape survivor, directing the state to arrange the procedure and provide necessary care for the newborn if it survives.
The Kerala High Court has allowed the medical termination of a 30-week pregnancy of a 15-year-old rape survivor after her mother moved the court. The court also directed the state government to make arrangements for the procedure.
Justice Harisankar V Menon passed the order after a medical board, constituted by the court to examine the girl, said medical termination was the most suitable option. The board said continuing the pregnancy would significantly affect the mental health of the 15-year-old sexual assault survivor.
The plea was filed by the girl's mother seeking termination of the pregnancy. In its report, the medical board said that as the gestation had crossed 30 weeks, the baby would be born alive and had more than a 95 per cent chance of survival if there were no major anomalies or perinatal complications.
The board also said the baby would require a stay in the neonatal intensive care unit for about two months. Based on the report, the court directed the state to ensure that the procedure was carried out after obtaining an undertaking from the victim and her mother that the girl was willing to undergo it.
The court said, "If the child survives, the state shall provide appropriate measures and standard neonatal care. If the child still develops complications, as voiced by the report of the medical board, the necessary medical aid shall be provided by the state to the child, as and when it arises."
The court also directed that if the baby did not survive, the state should preserve tissue and blood samples of the foetus for necessary medical tests, including DNA, fingerprinting and mapping, as an FIR had been registered in connection with the sexual assault of the girl. With this, the court allowed the termination plea and laid down the steps the state must follow during and after the procedure.

New York City residents struggling to get out of recurring subscription fees can now submit complaints to the city government. As of Thursday, the city’s click-to-cancel rule has taken effect, which requires businesses to make it as easy to cancel a subscription as it is to sign up. That means a gym that lets you join online, for example, can’t make you call or go in person to end your subscription.
NYC is now the first city in America that bans sketchy subscriptions
A new consumer portal promises not to send complaints into a “chatbot doom loop.”
It’s the first municipality to see the rule take effect, after an appeals court struck down a federal version for procedural issues. The city expects it to save New Yorkers anywhere from $21.5 million to $162.5 million annually. And to NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) Commissioner Samuel Levine, it’s an example of how state and local governments can hold companies accountable when federal efforts fail. “No one should need 45 minutes of hold music to stop paying for something they never wanted,” NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. “If a company can take your money with one click, you should be able to get your money back with one click. And now, if they won’t let you cancel, the City is coming for them.”
Levine was the Federal Trade Commission consumer protection chief under Lina Khan, and he tried to usher in the click-to-cancel rule at a national level. He says the experience of implementing the rule in NYC has been “night and day.”
“We proposed this rule this year. We finalized it this year. It’s taking effect this year. This is the speed of government as it should be,” Levine tells The Verge in an exclusive interview. While Levine says he’s proud of his work on the FTC rule and sees it as a “model” for other state and local governments, “at the end of the day, it took more than four years. And then after all of that, it never actually gave Americans the relief they needed.” While the FTC under current Chair Andrew Ferguson has taken an initial step toward potentially reestablishing a similar rule, Levine is betting that more municipalities will do so first. While that leaves fewer Americans protected, it still creates a deterrent for businesses to engage in deceptive subscription practices.
“This is the speed of government as it should be”
In New York, consumers can use a new portal to file complaints if they believe a business gave them unclear subscription terms, delayed cancellation, or failed to inform them the subscription would auto-renew. After filing a complaint, DCWP will review it and could reach out for more information and try to get consumers’ money back and help them cancel relevant subscriptions. If the agency sees a pattern of noncompliance at a certain business, it could prompt further investigation and legal action. Under the rule, businesses could face fines starting at $525 per violation.
The mayor’s Public Interest Technology (PIT) Crew built the portal in 10 weeks; Levine assures consumers that the experience will be far different from the White House’s newly launched America.gov, which he says appears to be “just an AI chatbot layered on top of the federal government’s existing infrastructure.” When consumers submit a complaint to the click-to-cancel portal, Levine says, “they’re not going to be diverted into a chatbot doom loop. We’re going to have actual people whose full-time job is to help them.”
He also says it won’t be like going to a DMV office to renew your driver’s license. “If we want to restore people’s faith in government and the ability of government to deliver, we need to show that government can create excellent products. We need to show that every experience is not going to the DMV. And I mean, no offense to our colleagues at the DMV,” Levine says. “People have really bad associations with interacting with the government, and sometimes that deters them from filing complaints. You can have the best laws in the world, but at the end of the day, if your eyes and ears, the people you’re working to protect, don’t want to actually deal with the government and tell us what happened, those laws are not going to be effective.”

According to the advisory, special traffic arrangements will remain in place in the areas from 5 am to 11 am on Friday.
The Delhi Traffic Police has issued a traffic advisory ahead of programmes at Rajghat and Vijay Ghat on October 2 to mark Gandhi Jayanti and the 122nd birth anniversary of former prime minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS

Gujarat trio allegedly held captive in Ethiopia released, no ransom paid: Police
Three members of Gujarat family who were taken captive in the East African nation of Ethiopia reached Mumbai on Thursday after being released
The three members of a Gujarat family who were taken captive in the East African nation of Ethiopia while on their way to the US through an illegal migration route reached Mumbai on Thursday after being released, with police saying no ransom was paid for their release.
The three, Rutvik Jansari, Mamta Chavda and Mayuri, from Mehsana and Gandhinagar, left for the US on September 20 with the help of agents. They last contacted their kin on September 22, according to the complaint lodged with the Gujarat Police.
A man identifying himself as “Khan” allegedly contacted the family and demanded ₹1 crore ransom for their release. Jansari’s grandfather, Kanubhai, said they had paid ₹60 lakh after the three were taken captive, but the abductors continued to demand ₹1 crore.
Inspector AM Ghelot of the Langhnaj police station, where the missing persons complaint was filed, told HT that the three were released after police negotiated with the people holding them captive. He said the police told the captors that the families were not in a position to pay the ransom and persuaded them to release the three.
“We explained to them that the financial condition of the families whose relatives they had held captive. We tried to reason with them on phone. Following the negotiations, they released the three and put them on a flight to India,” Ghelot told HT over the phone.
Ghelot said no ransom was paid for their release. He said the police had informed the central government and the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) about the case, but he did not have information on what role they played in securing the release of the three.
The three reached Mumbai airport on Thursday noon and are on their way home to Mehsana, Ghelot added.
The alleged abduction is the latest in a series of cases involving perilous routes for illegal immigration from Gujarat.
In October 2025, four people, including a couple from Gandhinagar, allegedly headed to Australia, claimed they were held captive in Tehran before they were released after the Indian government’s intervention and returned home.
A family from Gujarat’s Mehsana attempting to illegally enter the US from Mexico was among at least 16 people on a boat that capsized in waters off Torrey Pines State Beach in May 2025. In January 2022, a family of four from Dingucha (Gandhinagar) froze to death while trying to cross from Canada into the US. A year later, a Mehsana family drowned in the St Lawrence River during a similar attempt.
Despite deportations, illegal immigration continues. Smuggling networks charge exorbitant fees to transport migrants through complex international pathways. Alternative routes include hazardous sea passages to Europe.
In December 2023, French authorities grounded a chartered Legend Airways flight from Dubai to Nicaragua carrying 303 Indians, including 66 from Gujarat, exposing a human trafficking operation.

Christa Pike execution latest: Satanic killer survives two lethal injections and rushed to Tennessee hospital
Pike was due to be the first woman put to death in the state in more than 200 years

Tennessee has failed in its attempt to execute Christa Pike, who survived and was rushed to hospital late Wednesday, despite being administered two doses of a lethal drug.
Pike, 50, was due to be the first woman put to death in the state in 206 years, after a court overturned a late stay of execution. Experts say her survival is unprecedented.
Officials administered pentobarbital to Pike twice, but she was later heard snoring. Witnesses say the curtain to the execution chamber was drawn and reopened on two separate occasions before the procedure was halted and they were asked to leave.
The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 8 p.m. local time.
Pike was being executed for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student she tortured and killed when she was 18.
The execution had already been delayed for hours after a panel of the Sixth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals issued a stay to allow further review of her legal challenges.
The U.S. Supreme Court later lifted that stay at Tennessee's request in a 6-3 decision, allowing the execution to proceed before Pike's death warrant expired at midnight.
Pike could be left with brain injury, medical expert says
Dr Joel Zivot, a professor at the Emory University School of Medicine in Atlanta, Georgia, who has been retained by Pike’s legal team, has told the BBC the convict is unlikely to have received a sufficient quantity of pentobarbital in her blood to cause the apnoea and cardiovascular failure intended for her execution.
“It’s very possible that as a consequence of the delay of the beginning of resuscitation she will have a brain injury,” Zivot said of the possible consequences of last night’s episode.
‘Nothing about today was normal’
Media witnesses have held a press conference describing what they saw after Pike was administered with the injections.
Be warned, you might find the reporter’s account below distressing to hear.
Christa Pike's failed execution is Tennessee's second botched attempt in months
The failed attempt to execute Christa Pike is the second botched lethal injection in Tennessee this year, after officials spent about an hour trying and failing to establish IV access on inmate Tony Carruthers in May.
Maria DeLiberato, an attorney for Carruthers, said at the time the medical staff repeatedly stuck his arms and feet with needles, then attempted unsuccessfully to insert a central line through his collarbone and shoulder. Carruthers groaned in pain and bled from puncture wounds, she said.
Governor Bill Lee halted the attempt after more than an hour and later granted Carruthers a one-year reprieve.
More than 40 doctors and nurses wrote to Mr Lee afterwards, calling for executions to be paused and for health workers to be removed from the process, arguing Tennessee's rules conflict with medical ethics guidelines set out by the American Medical Association, which bars doctors from participating in executions.
Nine Republican state lawmakers have joined defence attorneys in demanding a moratorium on the death penalty and an overhaul of the state's execution methods.
Since 2020, 170 people have been executed across 17 states, mostly in Florida, Texas and Oklahoma, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Six states have recorded botched lethal injections in that time.
What is pentobarbital and why did Biden ban it?
Christa Gail Pike survived on Wednesday after being given two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital, according to her lawyers.
Pike, 50, was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and was taken by an ambulance from the prison, her attorneys said. She was being treated at a hospital, but they said they hadn't been told about her condition.
She had been scheduled for execution at 10 a.m. Wednesday for the killing she committed at age 18 and would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
Officials gave Pike two doses of pentobarbital, her attorneys said in court filings late Wednesday. The Biden administration had previously removed pentobarbital from the federal protocol for single-drug lethal injections over concerns about the potential for unnecessary pain and suffering.

Christa Pike: What is pentobarbital and why did Biden ban the lethal injection drug?
'I met Christa Pike 20 years ago. This is why she shouldn’t be executed'
I met Christa Pike 20 years ago. This is why she shouldn’t be executed
Pike's execution was an unprecedented failure, death penalty expert says
Robin M Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said what Pike experienced is "singular and unparalleled."
Seven other people have survived medical problems due to an execution team's failure to access a vein to administer lethal injection drugs, but no one has stayed alive after receiving the drugs used in such executions, she said.
Pike said she never intended to kill Colleen Slemmer
Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens. Pike believed Slemmer had insulted her and was trying to take her boyfriend away from her.
The murder drew intense media attention in Knoxville, Tennessee, after Slemmer's body was found with an inverted pentagram, a symbol associated with satanic groups, carved into her chest.
Pike denied carving the symbol herself. Two other residents of the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the killing both before and after it took place, and had shown them a piece of Slemmer's skull.
In a clemency petition, Pike said she had intended to beat Slemmer, not kill her, but was unable to "put the brakes on".
"I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid," she said in a statement. "It took me numerous years to even realise the gravity of what I'd done. Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone's child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime."
Slemmer's mother said that she wanted the execution to go ahead, telling the Associated Press she had waited decades to see Pike's sentence carried out.
Tennessee governor halts all executions after failed attempt
Tennessee governor Bill Lee said in a statement that he had ordered “a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred” and the remaining scheduled execution would not take place this year.
“Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State’s most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective,” he said.
Pike's legal team say she was put through 'unnecessary agony'
While the execution was under way, Pike's legal team filed an emergency motion in the Tennessee Supreme Court to immediately stop the process, saying that after receiving the two doses she was still alive and experiencing "unnecessary agony”.
They said the prolonged nature of the attempt had caused her "superadded physical and mental suffering".
"Ms Pike has lost consciousness and still has a heartbeat and is audibly snoring."

Gujarat Giants gave itself plenty of work to do heading into the mega-auction for the 2026 edition of Women’s Premier League. The Ahmedabad-based franchise retained just two players, Ashleigh Gardner and Beth Mooney, heading into the competition, and was faced with rebuilding the squad from close to scratch.
It is a measure of how successful that process was that a year on, it has opted to let go of just four players (Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Titas Sadhu, Ayushi Soni, and Shivani Singh) and heads into the 2027 mini-auction with arguably the least work to do.
“I’m pretty confident with the skill sets we’ve got at the moment within our squad. In theory, we could get zero players at the auction because we’ve got our minimum of 15,” quipped head coach Michael Klinger at a media roundtable.

“I’m confident with our starting XI at the minute and our group there. So, it’s probably going to be more sort of top-up players to add depth to the squad, especially with our local players. Potentially an overseas player could come in and give us a bit of a different mix, but it’ll be more skill sets that we just feel we need to add some depth to.”
GG ended the league phase in second last year, behind eventual champion Royal Challengers Bengaluru, before falling in the Eliminator for the second year in a row. Klinger reflected positively on the campaign, opining that his side was well-placed to make the next step beyond the Eliminator.
“We had a pretty good season to be honest. Unfortunately, we lost the Eliminator for the second year in a row, so there’s no doubt we’re trying to go another step further from that,” he said.
“But we’ve got to start from fresh and every team’s going to look pretty strong, especially their starting XI. So, I feel like we’re in a good place in terms of putting our best foot forward in this tournament. I believe we’ve got a strong squad with different combinations we can go with.”
Big seasons for Yastika and Anushka
One player who Klinger will be able to call upon this year is Yastika Bhatia, who GG picked up at the mega-auction despite knowing she would not be fit for the 2026 season. Klinger said that the call to sign the wicketkeeper-batter was a “no-brainer” despite her injury at the time.
“In my first couple of years, she was at Mumbai Indians, and she always seemed to play pretty well against us. So for me, it was a no-brainer to get her,” he said. “We felt looking long-term, especially in the two-year cycle of WPL, that given she was on target for her knee to be right sometime in the middle of this year, she would have a really good lead into the WPL.”
“She’s scored runs everywhere she’s gone, whether it’s been India or India A. She got a taste of the national team and did pretty well, then after being left out of that squad, she made runs for India A, made runs in the CPL just recently. So that’s a really good sign for us, and I hope we can do everything we can to help her get back as a permanent fixture in the Indian team.”

She’s had a really good India A series now against Australia A, had a taste of international cricket and probably could have been there a little bit longer potentially with more opportunities,” the Australian noted. “But I’m hoping that will work in our favour, to be honest. After getting a taste of international cricket, I’m sure she’s going to be desperate to do everything she can to get back there.
Both her and Yastika are probably in the same boat playing for India A at the moment. I’m sort of hoping they’re going to have a lot of motivation to have a really good WPL to help break both of them back into that Indian starting XI lineup.”
Auction placement
Klinger also noted that the placement of the 2027 mini-auction presented franchises a new challenge given that it takes place just two days after the start of the domestic season unlike previous years.
“This year is probably a little different,” he admitted. “We’re probably not going to get the feedback on good performances from players in domestic cricket, both ours and also potential buys in the auction.”
“But we’ve held two camps just in the last six weeks. We held one about six weeks ago with all our local players and a few invited players that we’re sort of looking to scout potentially for whether it’s this auction or auctions in the future.”
He also praised the GG management for its investment in the scouting system, saying, “We’ve got our physios and Strength and Conditioning coaches here to see how everyone is travelling physically.
But we’ve also got a great scouting programme just to see what else is out there where we have people going to watch all the domestic competitions and that information getting fed back to me is extremely helpful coming into an auction.”

You can get Microsoft 365 for free through an eligible Education plan, free web and mobile versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other apps, or a 30-day Microsoft 365 trial with full desktop apps and 1 TB of OneDrive storage.
Microsoft 365 (formerly Office 365) is a subscription service that gives you access to various Microsoft products. This includes productivity apps like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and OneNote; 1 TB of OneDrive cloud storage; and tools like Teams, Forms, and Loop.
As of writing, a paid subscription starts at $1.99 a month or $19.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Basic and goes up to $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Premium. Whether getting a subscription is justified depends on which of the included apps and services you use and how much.
If you’re not too sure about that and don’t want to buy a subscription right away, you can get Microsoft 365 for free using the following methods. Which method to pick depends on whether you’re a student/educator and your requirements.
Get the Microsoft 365 Education Plan
Microsoft 365 Education is a special plan for students and educators that provides free access to Microsoft 365 apps and services. You need a valid school, college, or university email address to be eligible. You’d have one if you’re a student or educator at an accredited institution with a Microsoft Education license.
To check if you qualify, visit the Microsoft 365 Education portal, type your institution-issued email address, and hit Next. If you’re eligible, you’ll be prompted to log in with the same email address. Or you may receive a verification link in your inbox. Subsequently, you’ll be able to use the Microsoft 365 apps within the browser or download them to your devices, based on the plan your institute offers.
Microsoft 365 Education is currently available in three plans: A1, A3, and A5. Your institute will most likely offer an A1 plan since it’s free, though some may offer an A3. The major difference between them is that A1 is web-only, whereas A3 supports downloads, so you can use the apps even when you’re offline.
If you don’t have an institute-provided email address or it isn’t eligible for the Education plan, you can get Microsoft 365 for free using the next method.

Use Microsoft 365 for the Web or Native Mobile Apps
Unless you have advanced needs — creating and running macros (VBA) in Excel, multi-device installation rights, or fully offline mode — you don’t really need a Microsoft 365 subscription. The online version of Microsoft 365, which offers access to basic versions of its apps, along with 5GB of free cloud storage, should serve your needs just as well.
All you need for this method is a Microsoft account and a web browser. In your preferred browser, visit the Microsoft 365 online portal and sign in with your Microsoft account. Create a new Microsoft account if you don’t have one.
Next, click the app launcher icon in your dashboard and select the app you want to use. This will open the app in a new browser tab, where you can create a new document or work on an existing one in your OneDrive storage. Any changes you make to the document are automatically saved to the cloud. Keep in mind, though, that the app’s functionality halts completely when you lose the internet connection.
Just like Microsoft 365 for the web, Microsoft also offers mobile apps for many of its productivity apps. So, if you just want to work on a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint document, you can download their mobile apps on your phone or tablet and use them. Just note that these apps offer limited functionality, similar to the web version. However, unlike their web versions, mobile apps support some offline functionality, allowing you to view a cached version of the document or edit local documents, even without an active internet connection.
Get the Microsoft 365 Free Trial
Microsoft offers a 30-day free trial to Microsoft 365. This trial gives you full, unrestricted access to the service, including complete offline capabilities and the ability to download desktop apps to your PC or Mac. You also get 1 TB of OneDrive cloud storage.
A free trial is great for someone who wants full-blown access to Microsoft’s productivity suite for a brief period. It also makes sense for those who want the Microsoft 365 service without committing to an upfront payment.
To subscribe to a 30-day Microsoft 365 free trial, you need a Microsoft account and a valid payment method. Open a browser and go to the official Microsoft 365 free trial page. Click the Start Free Trial button, and log in with your Microsoft account when prompted. If you haven’t taken a free trial with this account previously, you’ll be asked to add a valid payment method. Complete the checkout process. You now have complete access to Microsoft 365.
Set a reminder to cancel the subscription before the 30 days are up. If you forget, Microsoft will convert the trial to a monthly or annual subscription and charge you for the same on your added payment method.
Identify Your Use Case to Find the Right Method
You can use any of the above methods to get Microsoft 365 for free. However, not all of them offer the same level of access. As such, it’s important to identify your use case before choosing a method.
For example, if you want a full-blown Excel experience for a few weeks, the free 30-day trial makes more sense. Meanwhile, you might want to subscribe to the Microsoft 365 Education plan if you’re a student or educator and want desktop access to productivity apps for a longer period. Or use their mobile apps on your phone or tablet if you only need to view or maintain a few Excel sheets.

The Pentagon may soon deploy an additional aircraft carrier along with up to 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, giving US commanders more military options as President Donald Trump weighs his next steps in the conflict with Iran, Bloomberg reported on Thursday (October 1) citing a US official.
According to the news outlet, the USS Theodore Roosevelt left its home port in San Diego on Sunday. The US official, according to the news report said no final decision had been made on the carrier's destination, but its movement provides US Central Command (CENTCOM) with additional options in the region.
If the Roosevelt is deployed to the Middle East, the number of US carrier strike groups in the region would rise to three.
The carrier itself has about 5,000 sailors and Marines, while thousands more personnel are deployed aboard its accompanying vessels, according to Bloomberg.
The USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington carrier strike groups are already in the region and would remain there, the news outlet stated.
Bloomberg noted that before the 2026 military operations against Iran, the last time the US had three carrier strike groups in the Middle East was in 2003, during the early phase of the US-led invasion of Iraq.
CENTCOM declined to discuss the movements, saying it does not disclose unit schedules for operational-security reasons.
The potential carrier deployment comes alongside the movement of another US amphibious force.
The USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group, which includes an assault ship, aircraft and about 2,200 Marines, departed on Monday, the US official told the news outlet.
The USS Boxer amphibious readiness group is already operating near the Strait of Hormuz, providing another US military capability close to the strategically important waterway.
The reported deployments come as major US and Iranian military strikes have entered a lull amid attempts to restart diplomatic negotiations.
However, talks aimed at ending the war remain deadlocked, with the status and control of the Strait of Hormuz among the key issues.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has suggested in recent private discussions that Tehran could restore access for nuclear inspectors to facilities damaged in attacks, in exchange for sanctions relief.
The proposal comes as Washington and Tehran explore avenues for negotiations, but significant differences remain over sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz.
According to AP, the possible deployment of three carrier strike groups would represent an unusually large concentration of US naval forces in the region, with the overall presence potentially exceeding 20,000 sailors and Marines.
US President Donald Trump has said it is “possible” that he could intensify bombing operations in Iran after the November 3 elections, while declining to disclose details of his military strategy.
In an interview with Time magazine published on Thursday, Trump was asked about the possibility of further US strikes as the war with Iran continues. The interview was conducted on Monday.
“I can't tell you that because look, you know, you're asking, where are you going to bomb?” Trump said when pressed about his strategy.
Trump also said he had rejected Iran’s latest ceasefire proposal, arguing that the terms did not go far enough.
“Things that I wouldn't have approved a year ago I wouldn't have today,” Trump said.

The Best Kids’ Mattresses, Put Through the Toddler Test
Featured in this article
Kids, especially toddlers, aren’t mattress reviewers. They don’t wake up and tell you the pressure relief is lacking or that they appreciated the vegan foam and airy woven top. Instead, as a parent, it’s your job to become the observer, paying attention to the little things, like how easily they can climb into bed, whether they stay asleep, if they seem comfortable while moving around, plus how well the mattress can handle inevitable spills, jumping, and tumbling.
For the last few months, my toddler daughter tested each mattress in this guide in her bedroom on a Simply Sori Montessori twin bed frame. I narrowed down the mattresses tested by looking for beds specifically designed for children and prioritizing a mix of constructions, price points, and features. I paid close attention to everything from how well she slept, how easily she could climb onto the mattress, the edge support for myself during bedtime stories, and how cool each cover felt on a warm summer day. Some mattresses stood out for specific features, while others offered impressive value or the ability to grow with your child. Regardless of the specific accolade, every pick here earned its spot through toddler testing.
Want more mattress-buying advice for every kind of sleeper? Check out our guide to the Best Mattresses, the Best Organic Mattresses, and the Best Mattresses for Side Sleepers.

Also Tested
Nolah Nurture Kids Mattress for $919 (Twin): My biggest complaint with the Nolah Nurture Kids Mattress is, unfortunately, the reason I had to stop testing it. It was just short enough that it didn’t fit in my daughter’s twin bed frame, leaving a solid 8-inch gap between the bottom edge of the mattress and the foot of the bed frame. Every other twin mattress I tested fit the frame without any issues, making the Nolah the odd one out. It’s a bummer, because the mattress otherwise had a lot going for it. It’s got the flippability of many mattresses we tested, and its hybrid design was very comfy, with great edge support. If it’d fit the bed frame properly, I think it would’ve been a contender.
FAQs
What’s the Difference Between a Kids’ Mattress and a Regular Adult Mattress?
Many kids’ mattresses have firmer sleep surfaces for younger children and specific features like flippable designs, waterproof and stain-resistant covers, or reinforced edges that stand up to roughhousing. Kids’ mattresses also typically have a lower profile, which makes it easier and safer for kids to get in and out of bed.
They’re also available in smaller sizes, most commonly twin and full, which are typical for kids’ bedrooms and smaller bed frames. A full-size mattress can make sense for a child who needs more room but still benefits from the features mentioned above. Once your child reaches their teen years or no longer needs these features, an adult mattress may make more sense.
Why Are Many Kids’ Mattresses Flippable?
Many kids’ mattresses are designed to grow with your child. They typically have a firmer side for younger children as they transition from a crib mattress and a softer side for older kids. Being able to adjust firmness by flipping the mattress can save you from replacing it after a few years when your kid’s wants change.
What Do Mattress Certifications Mean?
You’ll probably come across several mattress certifications while shopping. Here’s what the most common ones mean:
- CertiPur-US applies to polyurethane foam and verifies that the foam has been independently tested for emissions, durability, and certain chemicals, including formaldehyde and specific flame retardants.
- GreenGuard Gold certifies that a mattress has been tested for low chemical emissions, known as volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which can cause irritation in the nose, eyes, throat, as well as other ailments.
- Global Organic Latex Standard (GOLS) verifies that latex is responsibly sourced and processed according to environmental and production standards.
- Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS) certifies organic textile materials like cotton and wool. It ensures the materials meet strict environmental and manufacturing standards, with no VOC emissions or off-gassing.
We have more info about mattress shopping terms.
Should I Buy a Foam or Hybrid Mattress for My Child?
Foam mattresses are usually lighter and easier to move, which helps when you’re changing sheets or rotating the mattress. Hybrid mattresses combine foam with coils, which can boost pressure relief, edge support, and airflow to help prevent overheating. Neither is inherently better; it comes down to your little one’s needs and what feels most comfortable.
How Long Does a Kids’ Mattress Last?
A quality kids’ mattress should last anywhere from 7 to 10 years, depending on how heavily it’s used. Replace a mattress if you notice sagging, permanent body impressions, or tears. Also, if your child has outgrown the mattress’s size, it’s probably time for a new one.
What Should You Look for in a Mattress?
- Materials: Kids’ mattresses use many of the same materials as adult mattresses. You’ll commonly see memory foam for cushioning, higher-density foam for support, latex for a responsive, bouncy feel, and steel coils for extra support, airflow, and edge support. You’ll also see materials like Tencel, which is a plant-based fiber often used in mattress covers because it’s soft and breathable. Cotton and wool are often found in natural or organic mattresses. When researching mattresses, you might also see materials described with the brand’s proprietary names, whether it's gel-infused memory foam or a stain-resistant treatment. When shopping for and comparing mattresses, look past the marketing name to see what the material actually is and what purpose it serves.
- Firmness: There’s not much strong research or official medical guidance on mattress firmness for children. However, the American Academy of Pediatrics does specify that infants should sleep on a firm, flat mattress to reduce the risk of sudden unexpected infant death (SUID). When it comes time to transition out of the crib and into a “big kid bed,” it stands to reason that a firmer mattress will be more comfortable and familiar to a young child. Mattress firmness for kids of any age is ultimately a matter of preference, not a medical mandate, but we recommend consulting your child's pediatrician for additional advice.
- Pressure Relief: A mattress that properly supports a child's weight can help with body development and spinal alignment as they grow. It can also help prevent restless nights and lead to better sleep.
- Edge Support: This refers to how reinforced a mattress's perimeter is. As a parent who loves reading with my daughter, the last thing I want is for the mattress edge to sink in as I sit next to her. It also helps protect a child from falling out of the bed.
- Shipping, Trial, Warranty: Most online mattresses ship compressed in a box and are delivered directly to your door, and some brands offer in-home delivery and setup. A sleep trial gives you a window to test the mattress at home and return it if it isn’t a good fit. Be sure to pay attention to the fine print, though; some brands charge return or processing fees. The warranty covers manufacturing defects for a set period but typically not normal wear and tear, spills, or damage.
- What Else to Consider: Be sure the mattress fits your child’s bed frame. Also consider the height, especially if the mattress will be used on bunk beds and trundles. If you’re hoping to keep a mattress for several years, a flippable model can offer more flexibility. Also consider the practical stuff: stain-resistant and water-repellent covers can come in handy for inevitable spills or accidents.
Should I Buy a Mattress in a Store or Online?
All of the mattresses I tested for this guide were purchased online, and most were shipped vacuum-sealed in a box. Many come with sleep trials so you can test them at home and return them if they don’t work for you.
Buying online often makes it easier to compare prices, materials, and certifications without driving from store to store. That said, shopping in person lets you get a sense of a mattress’s firmness before committing.
How I Tested
My almost 2-year-old daughter tested each mattress in her own bedroom over several months, sleeping on them in the same Simply Sori Montessori twin bed frame. Because toddlers don’t provide detailed feedback on things like lumbar support and motion transfer, I took a more observational approach by paying attention to how well she seemed to sleep and how easily she could climb into bed.
I also tested each mattress from a parent’s perspective by sitting on the edges, climbing into the beds for nighttime cuddles, and monitoring things like how easy it was to set up, whether my daughter seemed hot while sleeping/after waking up, how supportive it felt, and how the mattress held up to normal toddler behavior. I also considered each mattress’s construction, materials, and price.
I narrowed down the mattresses by focusing on models designed and marketed for children rather than smaller versions of adult mattresses. I wanted to test a range of price points and constructions, as well as explore features relevant for kids, like flippable designs, stain resistance, and lower heights.

The winter season in Delhi usually results in poor air quality, outbreaks of seasonal influenza, a heavy burden on hospitals and increasing medical expenses. Hidden within the yearly air quality reports is a health problem that is preventable, and yet costs the city’s citizens lakhs. Among the elderly, especially those who have diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart disease or a suppressed immune system, a viral infection can develop into bacterial pneumonia and require hospitalization. Industry estimates suggest that the average cost of a hospital stay is about ₹50,000, while intensive care can amount to ₹1 lakh. A single such incident can erase months’ worth of income and cause households relying on pensions and daily wages to slip down the income scale.
The battle against pneumonia
India has achieved real advances in the fight against pneumonia, mainly as a result of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) as part of the Universal Immunisation Programme in 2017 and through Mission Indradhanush. Free three-dose vaccinations are provided to infants, and by 2023, vaccination rates among infants in India had reached 83%, according to the WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC).
The grandparents of these infants, however, are almost completely unprotected: National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) 80th Round Data on Health reveals that vaccination coverage among people aged 60 and over is only 0.40 per cent. While one generation is covered by the national programme, the other is left to avail of vaccines from a private market they may struggle to afford.
This gap is most significant in Delhi, since in the winter, the conditions can turn common respiratory infections into serious health issues.
Toxic winters
In December 2025, the city experienced its most toxic month in six years, with an average Air Quality Index of 351. Colder months naturally place a greater strain on the respiratory system. Winter air, which tends to remain stagnant, traps particulate matter near the ground: prolonged exposure compromises the lungs’ defensive abilities.
Government records show that there were more than 2,00,000 cases of acute respiratory illness and 30,000 hospital admissions in just six Delhi government hospitals between 2022 and 2024. When the pollution lasted throughout December 2025, doctors reportedly noted a 20% to 30% increase in the number of patients with respiratory problems, including some who had never before had such a condition.
These figures do not reflect the full extent of the problem, as they exclude people treated in private clinics, those who take medication on their own, infections that have never been confirmed by a laboratory test, and cases recorded as pneumonia rather than influenza.
Vaccine present, policy absent
What makes the number of hospitalisations and their resultant expenditure tragic, is that a a significant portion of this could perhaps be avoided with a vaccine that is already available. The 2026 Indian consensus guidelines concerning immunisation in adults recommend pneumococcal vaccination based on age and level of risk. It recommends the PCV20 vaccine for all adults between the ages of 18-49 years with chronic medical conditions or those considered at risk based on their health and lifestyle, or a single dose of the vaccine for all adults aged 50 and above. The guidelines also include adults who have immunosuppression and chronic diseases. For residents of Delhi, in winter when pollution makes the air toxic, this could mean the difference between a minor ailment an episode of hospitalisation.
India has no National Adult Immunisation Policy, and as a result, vaccination rates rely on individual awareness, access to a doctor, and the ability to pay out of pocket, a situation that systematically excludes older people in lower-income families. While this a critical problem ahead of winter in Delhi, it is not merely a Delhi problem: in 2022, India was estimated to whom were 149 million people aged 60 and over, a large number of whom are still economically active and support households.The Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (2017-18) showed that of Indians aged 45 and over, only around 0.6% had received a pneumococcal vaccine, a figure that has not changed much since then.
The burden in lives
The figure for deaths due to pneumonia recorded by India’s Medical Certification of Cause of Death in 2024 was 35,987, making it the leading cause of respiratory deaths, although it remains relatively out of the spotlight compared to other causes. Even this figure is an under estimate since the system covers only about one fifth to one quarter of all registered deaths nationally, and older people who die at home rather than in a hospital where certification takes place almost never get included at all.
Data on a year-by-year basis from Delhi shows that this is not an isolated occurrence but a consistent pattern, affecting precisely the group for whom a vaccine is already available but for whom no public system provides it.
Pollution raises the stakes
It is impossible for Delhi to solve its problem of air pollution by vaccination, and there is no suggestion here that it should. Reducing emissions at the source must continue to be the main course of action. However, the two measures operate at different stages of the same risk pathway. In the winter of 2025, the AQI reached 450 at a number of monitoring stations and people suffering from respiratory and cardiac conditions were told to remain indoors, a recommendation that is not a policy. When pollution increases baseline vulnerability, the removal of an additional infectious trigger becomes all the more important.
Before winter sets in this year, there is a concrete option available. Delhi could provide free pneumococcal vaccination to adults aged 60 and over who have recorded comorbidities via its present dispensary and mohalla clinic network and then assess both the uptake and the hospitalisation outcomes. The cost of each dose, at a few thousand rupees, is significantly lower compared to ₹65,000 for a hospitalisation episode.
Delhi already vaccinates the grandchildren; the medical case for vaccinating the grandparents is no different, it is merely administratively missing.

Quick Answer
Snapchat’s distinct navigation uses custom icons across its main features: the bottom bar accesses Snap Map, Chat, Explore, Stories, and Spotlight. In chats, color-coded arrows and squares signal message types (pink for audio-less snaps, purple for video/audio snaps, and blue for text chats), while outlined versions show opened status or screenshots.
Snapchat successfully positioned itself as “the social media platform for Gen Z”. With its ephemeral nature and best retention features such as Snapstreaks, Snapchat is one of the most popular social media platforms currently.
However, I took my time to understand the platform better and finally became a user. But still, I am far from being a snapper, a word I use for those who are obsessed with Snapstreaks, including my close friends.
Despite being a user for months, I still find the Snapchat interface harder to navigate. Part of the reason is that it is completely detached from the common interfaces used in other social media platforms.
Moreover, Snapchat uses its own terms, such as Planets, Best Friends, and Chats, which can confuse new users. So, as part of our icon explanation series, in this guide you will learn everything about icons and their meanings on Snapchat. For quick reference, here is the Snapchat legend, followed by various icons on each screen and what they mean.
Table of Contents
Snapchat Icons Legend
Snapchat Icons and Symbols and Their Meanings
Snapchat Bottom Navigation Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Open Snapchat > View the bottom navigation bar
Snapchat is still one of the apps that uses a bottom navigation bar, which lets you switch between different Snapchat core features such as Snap Map, Chat, Stories, Discovery, and Spotlight
- Snap Map: Snap Map is an interactive feature that lets you see your friends’ current locations and also locations with the most Snap activity
- Chat: The chat icon lets you switch to the Chats tab
- Explore: Using this icon, you can browse various Snapchat lenses and filter options
- Stories: Takes you to the Snapchat stories tab
- Spotlight: Spotlight is another name for the short video feed in the Snapchat app, just like Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts
Snapchat Chat Screen Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Chat icon
Now, moving on to the chat feed, which many of us also spend more time on, you will find various icons and symbols. This screen can be confusing for the user with various symbols. Here is what each symbol means.
- Add Friends: This is the same add button that you see on other screens, where it lets you discover or add new friends
- More Options: This option opens additional chat screen options, including the ability to create new chats, create new groups, manage them, manage friendships, and also customize friend emojis and more.
- Viewed Snap Without Audio: This means you have viewed your snap without audio
- Snap Reply: If you see a reply, it means you can reply to a friend with a snap again
- Unopened Snap With Audio: If you see this icon, it means it is an unopened snap with audio
- Chat: The chat icon lets you start a new conversation with your friend.
- New Chat: The new chat icon lets you create a new chat with any of your friends
Snapchat Chat Status Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Chat icon
Snapchat also uses various colored arrows and squares to represent the type of snaps. If you see a pink arrow icon, it means you sent a snap without audio. If you see a purple arrow, it means you sent a video snap; in other words, you sent a snap with audio or video.
If you see blue, it means the chat was sent; in other words, you sent a chat message. If you see gray, it means your chat is waiting for the person to accept you.
If the arrow turns into an outline pink arrow, it means the recipient has opened your Snapchat without audio. If you see purple, it means the recipient opened your Snapchat with audio or video, and it’s the same for the blue outline arrow.
If you see a square-shaped icon in pink, it means you received a new snap without audio. If you see a purple square box, it means you received a new snap with audio or video.
If you see a blue square-shaped icon, it means you received a chat message. If you see the outline messages, it means you have viewed all the chats and messages.
If you see a double-arrow outline pink arrow, it means someone took a screenshot of the snap without audio, and it is the same for the other arrow types, including video and chat.
If you see a reload symbol, it means someone replayed your snap without audio. If you see a purple arrow, it means someone replayed your snap with audio or video.
Snapchat Chat Call Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Chat icon > Open a conversation
Chat screens can be confusing initially with the various arrow and square icons, but it consists of a similar interface to other chat applications, such as the ability to voice call and video call, and also an input bar with various options to send a message
- Camera: It opens the camera to send a snap as a reply
- Voice Call: Snapchat also supports voice calls. Tapping on this icon, you can make a voice call to your friend.
- Video Call: Along with the voice call, Snap also supports video calls. You can tap on the video icon to start a video call with your friend.
Snapchat Chat Toolbar Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Chat icon > Open a conversation
Snapchat uses different icons to represent various inputs for the message toolbar. Here is what each of the icons means.
- Camera: It opens your camera to send a snap quickly
- Voice Note: You can also quickly record a voice note and send it as a message
- Stickers: This is a sticker icon that lets you add stickers, Bitmoji, and other reaction options
- Notifications Off: If you see a bell icon with a cross, that means you have turned off notifications for the chat
- Photos: Lets you send your memories or camera roll photos to your friend
- Games: This icon opens the games you can play in the chat
Snapchat Chat Message Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Chat icon > Open a conversation
More icons from the chat interface, and here is what each of them means
- Reply: You can reply to your conversation in a thread to a message in your friends’ chat
- Stickers: Lets you access stickers, Bitmoji, and other emoji reactions
Snapchat Friendship Profile Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Chat icon > Open a conversation > Tap on your friend’s profile
Snapchat friends’ profiles can also be confusing for new users. It also consists of various icons similar to your profile page. Here is what each of them means.
- More Options: It opens more options for the friend you are viewing, including the ability to manage pin chat, manage location history, and much more
- Share Profile: You can share your friend’s Snapchat profile with others
- Send Snap: You can also send a snap to your friend from a Snapchat profile
- Chat: You can also initiate a conversation directly from your friend’s network profile
- Voice Call: You can also have a voice call with your friend by tapping on this icon
- Video Call: You can have a video call with your friend by tapping on this icon
- Activity Indicator: The green dot represents the activity indicator. If you see a green dot, it means your friend was recently active. However, unlike WhatsApp or other platforms, it does not mean that your friend is currently active
Snapchat Snap Map Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Snap Map icon
Snap Map shows your friends list and snap activity visually. It also includes various icons that can confuse beginners, especially when it shows Ghost Mode and other map settings.
- Ghost Mode: If you see this icon, it means your location is hidden from friends on Snap Map. You can tap on the icon to allow or disallow your location.
- Map Settings: It lets you manage your location and see your location. It also controls whether Snapchat can access your location.
- Satellite View: Snapchat supports both heat map and satellite view. You can switch to satellite mode using this icon.
- Explore Layer: The Explore option lets you see Public Snap and Activity Hotspots
- Battery Status: The battery icon shows a friend’s phone battery status. Remember that they should enable this option from their settings.
- Compass: It is a digital compass that lets you check the direction and reorient the map
- Friend Finder: It lets you search for and find friends who are visible on a Snap Map.
Snapchat Camera Screen Icons
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Camera icon
The Snapchat camera is the default screen that opens every time you launch Snapchat. It consists of various icons and symbols meant for different purposes. While we haven’t highlighted the multi-state capture button, which is the primary shutter button, you can use it to capture snaps. Remember that long-pressing will record a video.
- Search: This is a global search option that lets you search for your friends or groups. Recent search results also appear here.
- Notifications: View all your Snap notifications here
- Add Friends: You can find and add new Snap friends here. Tapping on this icon brings up your friends discovery page.
- AI Snaps: You can create AI snaps from here. Snap offers various lenses created using AI, which require a Snapchat+ subscription.
- Camera Zoom: While taking a snap, you can use this toggle to zoom in or zoom out the camera
Snapchat Camera Screen Icons
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Camera icon
Snapchat camera screen consists of various icons, so it’s hard to explain. In this part, let’s explore all the camera tools, which include the ability to switch cameras, control the flash, add music, HD mode, and much more.
- Profile: This is a global profile icon. Tapping on this takes you to your profile page.
- Notifications: Again, the same global notification icon that lets you see all your Snap notifications in one place
- Memories: Open your saved snaps and memories using this icon
- Switch Camera: While taking a snap, you can switch to rear or front camera options
- Flash: Lets you turn on or off the flash depending on your need
- Sounds: Let’s show you access various music options or sounds to add to your Snap
- HD Mode: Using HD mode captures snaps using a higher-quality camera mode
Snapchat Lens Category Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Camera icon > Open Lenses
If you want to quickly send a snap to your friend inside the chat, it also offers various options along with the camera interface. On the bottom navigation, you can find all the personalized options such as your favorite reactions and much more.
- Recents: This icon lets you view the lenses you recently used
- Favorites: View your favorite lenses that you previously saved as favorites
- For You: Snapchat uses your data to browse lens recommendations for you. You can access them by tapping on this icon.
- Reactions: Lets you browse Lenses specifically made for reactions
- Aesthetic: You can access aesthetic-style Snapchat lenses by tapping on this icon
Snapchat Profile Screen Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Profile icon
Snapchat profile screen is one of the most confusing screens, with various icons. Here’s what each one means.
- Back: You can use the same global button to take the user to the previous screen or to the home screen
- Share Profile: Using this share icon, you can share your Snapchat profile or the Snapcode with others
- Bitmoji Outfit: It opens a Bitmoji outfit screen where you can customize your current outfit
- Settings: It opens Snapchat global settings
- Birthday: If you see a balloon icon next to the date on your profile or in your friend’s profile, it represents their birthday date
- Snapchat+: If you want to upgrade to Snapchat+, you can tap on this. Snapchat+ is a Snapchat subscription that brings additional features. You can see the full differences here.
- Snapscore: You can view your current Snapscore from here
- Zodiac Sign: You can open your Snapchat astrological profile by tapping on this zodiac sign
Snapchat Friends and Stories Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Profile icon > Scroll down
Scrolling down to the bottom of the profile page also shows more options with different icons. Here is what each of them means.
- Back: The same global back button takes you back to your home screen or the previous screen
- Settings: Takes you to the global settings screen.
- Add Friends: You can add friends from here. Tapping on this icon takes you to the friends discovery page.
- My Friends: Here you can view all your Snapchat friends and also manage them from here.
- New Story: You can add a new story on Snapchat by tapping on this icon.
- More Options: Lets you view additional Snap story options.
Snapchat Add Friends Screen Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Add Friends icon
Snapchat friends discovery screen is one of the minimal screens found on Snapchat, with a less confusing approach. It follows a similar approach to other user discovery screens but uses slightly different terms. Here is what each of them means.
- Back: This is a global back button that takes you to the previous screen
- Scan Snapcode: With the Snapcode, you can scan a Snapcode saved in your photos and add them as friends. You can simply tap on the scan code icon in Discovery, and a photo library opens. You can select the photo with the Snapcode.
- Add Friend: To add a friend, you can simply click on the Add button
- Dismiss Suggestion: If you don’t like any suggestions or want to hide them, you can tap on the X icon
Snapchat Spotlight Icons and Symbols Explained
How to access this screen: Home > Tap on the Spotlight icon
Like other social media platforms, Snapchat also quickly adopted a short video feed, and they named it Spotlight. You can access this screen by tapping on the play button icon in the bottom navigation bar.
- Create Spotlight: You can create a new Snapchat Spotlight, which is, in other words, a short video
- Add Friends: You can also add new friends from here. Tapping on this icon takes you to your new friends discovery page.
- Captured on Snapchat: If you see this icon, it means it was captured and recorded in Snapchat
- Location: It lets you view the location tagged in the Spotlight
- Sound: It shows some music used in the Spotlight. You can also tap on it to open it and learn more about it.
Understanding Snapchat Icons Is Easier Now
Those are the various icons and Snapchat symbols that mean something on each page. Snapchat also has many different icons in chats, including arrow symbols, square boxes, and various planet and zodiac signs.

Investigators probe why co-pilot stabbed captain of flyDubai flight to Israel
The suspect, an Omani citizen, is under arrest and Saudi authorities are working with countries, including Israel, to determine a motive
Investigators worked on Thursday to determine why an Omani pilot stabbed the captain of a flight to Israel, causing the plane to plummet dangerously before others on board landed it in Saudi Arabia.
Passengers on the FlyDubai plane – which was carrying 174 people, mostly Israelis, from the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv – have described how the bloodied Indian captain managed to open the cockpit door to let them in before they grappled with the co-pilot and stabilised a descent so sharp that the plane’s rudder was torn away.
“We felt helpless, suspended in mid-air, and I didn’t know who to turn to. But it was all instinct to survive,” Asaf Rajuan, who was among those who intervened, said in a statement shared by Israel’s presidency.
A regional official briefed on the investigation said the suspect, an Omani citizen, was under arrest and confirmed that Saudi authorities were working with countries, including Israel, to try to determine a motive. He said the UAE, the United States and Oman also were involved.

No one does daring fashion quite like Dakota Johnson.
On red carpets, the "Fifty Shades of Grey" star has made sheer, sultry outfits her signature. Her everyday style is a little more laid back, but still bold, elevated, and the epitome of cool.
If you're unfamiliar, Johnson's fashion has been on display throughout this year as she's promoted projects including a short film called "Flesh Impact," Taylor Swift's "Patient Zero" music video, in which she stars, and her coming film "Verity."
Here's everything she's worn, ranked from least to most daring.
The outfit Dakota Johnson wore for a September outing in New York City was the opposite of daring.
She was photographed leaving a "Verity" press event in ripped vintage jeans, a black tank top, and the $1,390 Swan wool jacket from Nili Lotan.
For accessories, Johnson chose $1,140 Khaite flats, $73,240 worth of layered jewelry, and $515 Valentino sunglasses.
Though the outfit was expensive, it was extremely subtle in style.
The same could be said of her fashion when she stepped out again two days later.
Johnson attended another "Verity" event in a long black skirt and a semi-sheer sweater that revealed her red tank top beneath it.
The outfit was perfect for fall and was accessorized with feminine touches, like white pumps, a diamond necklace, a slouchy leather bag, and the same Valentino sunglasses.
Still, there was nothing shocking about the outfit.
Johnson played it safe for New York Fashion Week in February.
For a Calvin Klein runway show, Johnson wore the brand's high-waisted black skirt with a blazer that was tied in a knot at her waist.
She seemingly wore the latter with no shirt beneath it, and completed the outfit with leather boots, a white purse, and thick sunglasses.
Though the top half was unconventional, the outfit overall wasn't the boldest choice she could have made for a fashion-show appearance.
The baby-pink gown she wore at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards was pretty, but tame.
Still, Johnson looked stunning in the baby-pink number from Calvin Klein. It was sleeveless, covered in transparent sequins, and the tiniest bit sheer.
The actor also wore a Messika diamond choker and custom rings.
The actor chose a little black dress with a plunging neckline for a Valentino event.
Her satin dress from the fashion house was sensual, lined with lace at its deep neckline and embellished with a matching satin choker.
Johnson also wore black pumps, statement earrings, and an oversize velvet sweater.
The outfit leaned into her daring style but didn't go all the way.
She made a statement shoe choice in April.
Valentino designed the flowing white gown Johnson wore at the 2026 Time100 Gala in New York City.
It was sleeveless with gathered fabric at the neckline, a floor-length skirt, and a matching cape clasped with a crystal-covered, wing-shaped brooch.
Not only was the dress style a departure for Johnson, but her shoes were unexpected as well. She wore $1,250 leather heels with crystal snake embellishments from Valentino.
The "Verity" star stood out in a bold two-piece set for her film's premiere.
Johnson wore a custom Calvin Klein outfit that was perfect for a party. It featured a high-waisted skirt covered in beaded fringe and a matching bralette top.
She made it even more festive with a diamond necklace, earrings, and red lipstick.
The outfit was flashier and more fun than expected.
Johnson subtly showed her love of see-through clothes with a mesh skirt.
While in New York City, Johnson essentially ditched pants and instead wore a mesh skirt that revealed her undergarments.
She also sported black ballet flats, a loose-fitting button-up top, her Valentino sunglasses, and an assortment of gold jewelry.
The outfit summarized Johnson's style: provocative, but simple.

She was there wearing a black ensemble from Valentino. It comprised a cropped, ruffled jacket worn atop a sheer bodysuit with a plunging neckline that dipped to her stomach.
She wore the latter tucked into a miniskirt that had a longer lace lining.

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday lauded Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to seek an end to the Ukraine conflict, saying that he has “good ideas” for achieving a peaceful resolution.
"Prime Minister Narendra Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good and even friendly relations, personal good relations, constantly raises the question and asks the question about putting an end to the conflict in Ukraine," Putin said.
Asked about the issue at the Valdai Club forum, Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been actively working to find mutually acceptable solutions to the Ukraine conflict.
"He has an avid interest and very good ideas aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions. In that sense, naturally, the Prime Minister takes a neutral position but with an interest in the end of the conflict. I think it's my duty to say that directly. And we are thankful to the Prime Minister for his ideas," Putin said.
Putin thanked PM Modi for his efforts and continued support for resolving the Ukraine conflict through dialogue.
"We are thankful for his desire to put an end to this conflict through peaceful means and as soon as possible," he added.
Prime Minister Modi and Putin last met in September on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where they discussed strengthening trade ties, including the implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030, along with cooperation in infrastructure, energy, technology, defence and culture.
PM Modi has repeatedly called for peace, stressing that India has maintained a principled and humanitarian approach to the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
"India has maintained a principled and humanitarian stance on the conflict which is equally appreciated by both President Putin and President Zelenskyy. In line with this, both the leaders spoke to me to share their perspectives on the developments related to the conflict. I reiterated India's principled and consistent stand and encouraged dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict," the Prime Minister said during an interview with Japanese news outlet 'The Yomiuri Shimbun' while on a visit to the country in August.
Responding to a question on India’s role in peace efforts between the two countries, Prime Minister Modi said, "I have already indicated India's willingness to support meaningful efforts aimed at achieving a peaceful resolution of the conflict. I believe, by virtue of our good relations with both sides, including key stakeholders, we can strengthen efforts dedicated to the restoration of an early and lasting peace in Ukraine."
This comes as Putin reiterated Moscow’s long-standing position that Russia has no plans to attack European countries, while warning that it would respond to any aggression with “all weapons” at its disposal.
He also accused Western countries, particularly in Europe, of escalating tensions by discussing preparations for a possible war with Moscow, conducting military drills in the Baltic Sea and seizing Russian vessels.
European leaders and intelligence agencies have warned that Russia could be capable of launching an attack on another country within the next few years, particularly if it emerges victorious from the war in Ukraine.

Trump team is now looking to see if DOJ committed misconduct in investigating Richard Nixon’s Watergate
A burglary at the Watergate complex in June 1972 would ultimately lead to a corruption scandal in Washington and the resignation of President Richard Nixon

President Donald Trump’s Department of Justice is now looking to see if Nixon-era special prosecutors committed misconduct in investigating the Watergate scandal.
An early morning burglary at the Democratic National Committee’s headquarters in the Watergate office complex in Washington, D.C., in June 1972 would become a two-year affair, uncovering corruption inside the White House that would ultimately lead to Republican President Richard Nixon’s resignation.
More than 50 years later, Geoff Shepard, a former Nixon aide who has written books on Watergate, was invited last month to give a two-hour presentation to the DOJ’s Office of Professional Responsibility, an internal watchdog created out of the Watergate scandal, on allegations that the special prosecutor’s office that investigated the break-in committed misconduct, people familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal.
A DOJ spokesperson confirmed to The Independent that Shepherd gave a presentation to the Office of Professional Responsibility, but said it does not mean an investigation has been opened.
"OPR declined Mr. Shepherd's request to open an investigation in 2022 under the previous administration. Given his expertise and scholarship on Watergate, he was recently invited to give a presentation to OPR, but that presentation does not constitute an investigation,” the spokesperson said.
“OPR remains focused on ensuring that Department attorneys meet the highest professional standards."
Shepard showed DOJ officials internal documents from the Watergate Special Prosecution Force, the Journal reported. Special prosecutor Archibald Cox first led the team and then Leon Jaworski after Nixon demanded Cox be fired.
Shepard claims Cox and Jaworski violated defendants' due process rights in the Watergate investigation by secretly meeting with judges overseeing their cases and suppressing evidence from their legal teams, according to the Journal.
Nixon resigned in August 1974 while facing impeachment for allegations of obstruction of justice, abuse of power and contempt of Congress — mostly in relation to accusations that his administration tried to cover up its involvement in the Watergate break-in.
Speaking at the Richard Nixon Presidential Library in California in June, Vice President JD Vance drew parallels between Nixon and President Donald Trump, who has been indicted multiple times and claimed it was the result of a witch hunt.
“If you look at the story of how the deep state took down Richard Nixon, it’s not all that different from what the same groups of people, the same institutions tried to do to Donald Trump in the first Trump administration,” Vance said.
He also theorized that if the Watergate scandal were to happen in today’s media landscape, it wouldn’t impact the White House as greatly as it did in Nixon’s time.
“If Watergate happened tomorrow, it would be like a 12-hour news story. The idea that it would have taken down a presidency is crazy,” Vance said.

Ram temple tightens security after donations theft, orders 100% staff verification
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has sought comprehensive details from its employees, including information about their family members and relatives. Verification and character certificates issued by the police will also be mandatory.
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has decided to carry out 100 per cent verification of all staff working at the Ram temple in Ayodhya as part of stepped-up security measures, sources said on Thursday.
The verification will include police checks, character certificates and detailed information about employees’ families and relatives.
The move comes as the temple administration reviews its functioning and tightens security following the donations' theft that came to light in June this year. Eight people were arrested in connection with the case and are currently in jail. A 70,000-page chargesheet was filed last week.
The Trust has sought comprehensive details from its employees, including information about their family members and relatives. Police verification and character certificates issued by the police will also be mandatory.
The verification exercise is being undertaken under the leadership of the temple’s newly appointed chief executive officer, retired Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra, who took charge last month.
The temple administration has also undergone a major restructuring, with former general secretary Champat Rai and Trust members Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao relieved of their responsibilities.
Trust member Dinendra Das said the decisions taken by the Trust would be accepted by everyone associated with the temple.
“Whatever decision the Trust takes will be accepted by everyone. The worship rituals are proceeding smoothly, donations are being received properly and a large number of devotees are visiting the temple for darshan and aarti,” he told news agency PTI.
The Trust has also stepped up monitoring of staff and is focusing on improving facilities for devotees as part of the broader overhaul of the temple administration.

Manipur Cabinet approves Rs 10 lakh aid for kin of 49 missing since 2023 violence
The Manipur Cabinet has approved Rs 10 lakh each for the families of 49 people still missing since the May 2023 violence. The meeting also cleared higher ex-gratia for security personnel, a pension rise for retired journalists and the Fifth State Finance Commission.
The Manipur Cabinet on Thursday approved a one-time special humanitarian assistance of Rs 10 lakh each for the next of kin of 49 people who have remained missing since the violence that erupted in the state on May 3, 2023.
The 49 people remain untraced despite sustained search efforts. The total financial implication of the assistance will be Rs 4.90 crore, which will be borne by the Manipur government.
The decision was among four key measures approved at the state Cabinet meeting held on Thursday.
RS 10 LAKH EX-GRATIA FOR DEATH OF ARMY, CAPF PERSONNEL
The Cabinet also approved revised ex-gratia compensation for Army and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel killed or injured in extremist violence or related actions while operating in Manipur.
Under the revised rates, Rs 10 lakh will be provided in case of death, while compensation for injuries has been fixed at Rs 2 lakh for permanent disability, Rs 1 lakh for grievous injury and Rs 20,000 for simple injury.
The earlier ex-gratia compensation was Rs 2 lakh in case of death and Rs 10,000 for injuries. These rates had been fixed in 2006.
PENSION HIKE FOR RETIRED JOURNALISTS
The Cabinet also approved an increase in the monthly pension for retired journalists under the Manipur Working Journalists' Pension Rules, 1996.
The pension will rise from Rs 8,000 to Rs 10,000 per month, while the family pension for families of deceased journalists will increase from Rs 5,000 to Rs 7,000.
The revised pension rates will require amendments to the relevant rules. There are 20 beneficiaries in each category, with the annual financial requirement expected to increase from Rs 31.20 lakh to Rs 40.80 lakh.
FIFTH STATE FINANCE COMMISSION APPROVED
In another decision, the Cabinet approved the constitution of the Fifth Manipur State Finance Commission for the period from 2026-27 to 2030-31.
The commission will review the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities and make recommendations on the sharing of state taxes and grants-in-aid with Panchayats, Autonomous District Councils and Municipalities.
The four decisions were taken at the Manipur Cabinet meeting on Thursday.

Christa Pike would have been the 30th person executed in the U.S. this year after Florida carried out an execution on Tuesday
