A rumor that U.S. President Donald Trump's White House misspelled United States as "Unites States" on its "super intelligence" accord circulated online in late September 2026.
Trump and a group of tech industry leaders signed the voluntary accord at the White House on Sept. 29, reportedly as part of an effort to address fears about the future of artificial intelligence. On the same day, Trump also signed an executive order renaming "artificial intelligence," or "AI," as "super intelligence," or "SI."
Users shared the "Unites States" claim on Bluesky (archived), Facebook (archived) and X (archived).
(@paleofuture.bsky.social via Bluesky)
Snopes received reader mail and searches generally asking if the misspelling genuinely occurred. In an age of misinformation, it isn't out of the realm of possibility that someone might secretly change one or more characters in such a document and circulate the corrupted version to discredit its signatories.
That was not the case in this instance. An official White House X post sharing an image (archived) of the two-page accord confirmed that whoever prepared the document truly misspelled "United States" under Trump's signature so it read, "President of the Unites States."
The document didn't feature any official letterhead or other graphical designation, but it did include a title attributing its ownership to the White House. That title read, "White House Accord on Super Intelligence."
(The White House via X)
The spelling error appears on the accord's second page, which features Trump's prominent signature, as well as those from Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, "XAI" CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. 
(The White House via X)
Snopes emailed the White House to ask if they wanted to share a statement responding to the users sharing the error and will update this article if we receive further details.
The document also appears to contain other errors. For example, the word "joint" near the top is misaligned, suggesting someone may have added it later. On the second page, Musk's name and signature appear next to "XAI." The company was previously named "xAI," with a lowercase X, before SpaceX purchased it in February and renamed it SpaceXAI.
(The White House via X)
Trump's 'super intelligence'
Trump's executive order explained his administration's reasoning for attempting to rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," or "SI" — specifically referencing the name change as guidance for the government's executive branch:
The terminology used by the Federal Government should reflect the transformative capabilities of these technologies and the limitless opportunities they create for the American people. Accordingly, the term "Super Intelligence" more appropriately captures the promise, potential, and rapidly advancing capabilities of these technologies. It is therefore the policy of my Administration that, to the maximum extent permitted by law, the executive branch shall use the terms "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" and will not acknowledge the usage of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" in any applicable setting.
For further reading, we previously reported on the White House misspelling a word on a placard displayed during a Cabinet meeting.

eSafety commissioner says ‘time for new leadership’ after 10 years in role
Julie Inman-Grant, the eSafety commissioner, confirmed this morning “it’s probably time for new leadership” at the body after serving 10 years in the role.
She spoke to RN Breakfast this morning, saying 10 years was a “good, round, solid number”, adding:
We’ve increased the office tenfold. We’ve done amazing things. I think with the new digital duty of care, I’m going to be actively shaping that to the extent that I can and getting all the right pieces in place.
But it’s probably time for new leadership. This is not an easy gig from a personal perspective, but also professionally, it’s been the role of a lifetime. And, you know, to be able to try and make some positive change has been an incredible opportunity. But yeah, I think it’s time to be thinking about what’s next.
‘Threat environment is getting more serious’ in online game space, eSafety commissioner says
Julie Inman-Grant, the eSafety commissioner, said she expected by now there would be “better protections” for children in the online gaming space as “the threat environment is getting more serious”.
She told RN this morning some changes had been made, but other companies were lagging behind:
Some are doing better than others. We’re starting to see Roblox uplift. And Minecraft has education based games that are safer than, say, the online version. But we would expect to see more from Fortnite.
And Steam and Valve are really the outliers. They’re still relying on self-declaration for age assurance, even though in March we have required all gaming platforms to be able to age assure those under 18 and prevent harmful content being served to them.
Inman-Grant said it was a “shame” that some companies needed regulatory pressure to better their safety standards.
We’re starting to see gaming platforms act more like social media platforms. They’re trying to keep the kids on the platforms longer. … They’re introducing new services like dating services and shopping malls where the primary demographic is 8 to 13 and they’re allowing adults to intermingle. I mean, what could possibly go wrong there?
A Sydney man has been charged after allegedly restraining, choking and sexually assaulting a young woman in a park, Australian Associated Press reports.
A 23-year-old woman was walking from Flemington Station through Airey Park in Homebush, in Sydney’s west, around 11.15pm on Friday, 18 September, when she was stopped by a man not known to her, police say.
Police will allege the man, 27, then allegedly restrained the woman and dragged her into nearby bushland, where he sexually assaulted her.
Police searched a Padstow property about 8.50am on Thursday, arresting the 27-year-old man and seizing several items for forensic examination.
He was charged with aggravated sex assault - inflicting actual bodily harm, intentionally choking without consent, taking a person with intent to commit a serious indictable offence and stalk/intimidating with intent to cause fear of physical harm.
The man is due to appear in Bankstown Local Court on Friday.
Some findings from the eSafety report on online game companies
The eSafety commission released a major new report into online game service providers today, examining how the companies keep kids safe on the internet, or fail to do so.
The report found that “left unchecked or unmoderated, there is a risk that these games could contain unlawful material or serve as high-risk environments for child sexual exploitation and abuse or activity which promotes, incites or instructs in matters of crime or violence”.
Most of the providers employed tools to proactively detect unlawful or harmful material, but the quality and coverage of those tools varied across each one, eSafety said. It expected the industry to raise the bar to combat serious harms like child sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual extortion and material or activity that promotes or incites violence.
Some of the providers also took longer than others to respond to user or automatic reports of specific harms, which could leave other users exposed to serious harms for longer.

Industry minister says it is important Australia works in tandem with AI
Tim Ayres, the minister for industry and innovation, was asked this morning why the government’s rhetoric on artificial intelligence had softened after an initially stern tone on the OpenAI breach.
Ayres said the government had, in fact, been direct with OpenAI, but maintained the country and tech giants had to work in tandem. He told RN Breakfast:
It reinforces the government’s approach here, which is about making sure that artificial intelligence investment here supports Australia’s national interest, happens on Australia’s terms.
He said Albanese had initially given a direct, firm message to the founder of OpenAI, but that has since been followed by “extensive, enhanced cooperation, working through the issues in a constructive way”.
It underscores why it is that we’re legislating AI standards, why it is that we’re seeking to secure the right level of artificial intelligence investment, including training investment here in Australia, because it makes Australia stronger and means that we are part of shaping the technology and that is crucial for Australia and Australians.
Minns government vows to regulate labour hire in NSW
The Minns government has pledged to regulate labour hire in New South Wales if reelected, a move meant to protect workers and businesses from dodgy labour hire providers.
An independent report found earlier this year a number of labour supply companies had been incorporated within days of each other at the same address, with the same director and secretary, during the Western Sydney Airport Metro project.
The investigation found suspected underpayment of workers, insurance fraud, tax fraud and unaccounted invoices worth than $10m.
The contractor was terminated after the report.
Other entities, including farmers and unions, have raised concerns about labour hire providers in the horticulture sector.
Sophie Cotsis, the minister for industrial relations, said in a statement:
The NSW Government has zero-tolerance for the exploitation of workers, and this commitment builds on the work we are doing to stamp out dodgy labour hire firms.
Every worker deserves fair pay, access to their entitlements, and to work and live in a safe environment and a labour hire licencing scheme is an important step in ensuring safer workplaces for labour hire workers.
Former Wallaby hooker Nathan Charles diagnosed with MND at 37
The former Wallaby Nathan Charles, who became the first cystic fibrosis sufferer in the world to play a contact sport professionally, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).
AAP reports the 37-year-old, who played four Test matches for Australia, revealed he has been diagnosed with the same disease as retired South Sydney NRL star Jai Arrow.
During a Stan Sport interview with former Wallaby turned commentator Justin Harrison, Charles said he had only recently been diagnosed.
Atlassian enters 10-year solar energy deal with community co-op to power Sydney HQ
A solar farm owned by a group of community investors has secured a 10-year deal with one of Australia’s biggest technology companies to help power its headquarters, Australian Associated Press reports.
Atlassian announced its virtual power purchase agreement with the Goulburn Community Energy Co-operative on Friday in a deal that will fund almost 70% of the project’s output over the next decade.
Electricity generated by the project in NSW’s Southern Tablelands will help to meet the renewable energy needs of the tech firm’s 39-storey Sydney base, currently in construction near Central station, when it opens in 2028.
The announcement comes amid heated debate over whether technology companies should be required to invest in renewable energy generation to meet growing demands from data centres and artificial intelligence operations in Australia.
The solar and battery farm, located on 2.2 hectares of industrial land in Goulburn, features 2,300 solar panels and a four megawatt-hour battery. Owned by a group of about 288 local investors, who contributed a minimum of $400, the farm connected to the electricity grid in March 2026, 12 years after it was proposed.
The agreement follows a $2.3m NSW government grant and would support local workers and suppliers, AndrewBray, the Goulburn Community Energy Co-operative chair, said:
Our active volunteers and investor community worked patiently and diligently across a number of years to see this project come to fruition.
To have a blue-chip Australian company like Atlassian come on board as a commercial partner is a huge vote of confidence in what we have built.
Online gaming 'shortcomings' put children at risk, eSafety report finds
Sarah Basford Canales
Online gaming services are failing to take enough action to prevent children being exposed to harmful content, a new report from the eSafety Commissioner has found.
In a report published today, the online safety watchdog found measures adopted by gaming providers were not up to standard and varied in quality between platforms.
Platforms with the dominant purpose of gaming are not covered under Australia’s under-16s social media ban but are subject to the eSafety Commissioner’s information gathering notices.
The report – which drew details from Fortnite’s developer, Epic Games, Roblox, Minecraft and Valve’s Steam – found some positive signs but overall determined “disparities and shortcomings”.
Among them, examples of some platforms relying on age self-declaration resulting in children being able to easily access third-party content lacking sufficient content moderation as well as a limited number of human moderators to respond to harmful content.
The commissioner, Julie Inman-Grant, said:
While we have seen some safety improvements as a result of sustained regulatory pressure, including the recent court-enforceable undertakings we accepted from Roblox, there is still significant work to be done across the board to prevent serious harms in online gaming to children.

People who have a Medicare Advantage plan — and wind up needing care and prescriptions next year — are in for a rude awakening.
Medicare Advantage insurers are raising out-of-pocket costs for enrollees, drastically cutting money for dental work and other benefits, and eliminating plans that have broad networks of hospitals and doctors, according to federal data released this week and analyzed by STAT and several investment firms. That could result in more shock for older adults, like discovering their doctor is no longer accepted by their plan, if they don’t shop carefully during Medicare’s annual enrollment period for 2027 plans, which starts Oct. 15.
Big companies like UnitedHealth Group, Humana, and others are chasing higher profits by pruning benefits, after investors grew dissatisfied with margins that were smaller than the insurers had promised. The changes in plans even come even after the industry won a payment increase and delayed reforms from the Trump administration in April.

- Fortnite has four FNAF animatronics you can find on the map: Freddy, Foxy, Chica, and Bonnie.
- Freddy and Foxy spawn at Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria in every match, whereas Chica and Bonnie have random spawn points.
- Upon depleting an animatronic's health bar, you can wear their suit for an extra life in a Fortnite match.
Fortnite has released the much-awaited Five Nights at Freddy’s crossover in Fortnitemares 2026, and players can now see it live in-game. Apart from the FNAF Fortnite skins, there’s much more around the crossover to discover, and it’s none other than the four beloved animatronics now running wild around the island. If you’re wondering where to find the FNAF Animatronics in Fortnite and wear their suits, we’ve got you covered.
All FNAF Animatronics and Their Locations on Fortnite Map
The Fortnitemares 2026 update has added four animatronic characters from a Five Nights at Freddy’s crossover to the Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 island. These animatronics can be found across the map as hostile NPCs, and you can eliminate them to wear their animatronic suits.
Here’s the list of all FNAF animatronics in Fortnite and their locations on the new map:
| FNAF Animatronic | Location | 
|---|---|
| Freddy Fazbear | Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria | 
| Foxy the Pirate | Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria | 
| Chica the Chicken | Random spawn across the map | 
| Bonnie the Rabbit | Random spawn across the map | 
While Freddy and Foxy are easier to find on the Fortnite map since they have a fixed spawn at the Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria landmark, Chica and Bonnie rotate among randomized spawn locations. So it’s quite hard to keep track of the latter two animatronics. However, if you’re looking for Freddy and his pal Foxy, we’ve got their location tracked down for you in Fortnite below.
Fortnite Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria Location
The Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria landmark is located northeast of the Nightmare Neighborhood POI on the Fortnite Override map. You’ll find the Freddy Fazbear and Foxy the Pirate animatronics located right inside the pizzeria building.
Once you land outside the Freddy’s Fazbear Pizzeria in Fortnite, enter through the main door and walk inside. As you enter, you’ll see Freddy and Foxy performing on stage. However, as you walk closer to them, their eyes will turn red, and both animatronics will run towards you with pickaxes in their hand.
All you need to do at this point is equip a Fortnite loot pool weapon like an 8-Bit Shotgun or the Ranger Pistol in Fortnite and stay on the move to get a clear shot at each of them. Keep firing rounds at them to stun them both, since they have 300 HP each. Once their health bars deplete, both the animatronics will stop moving and keep glitching on the spot where you “eliminated” them.
As you walk closer, you’ll see a Possess interaction in front of each FNAF animatronic in Fortnite.
How to Wear FNAF Animatronic Suits in Fortnite
Once you’ve managed to stop an FNAF animatronic in Fortnite and they become immobile, walk closer to them and interact with them to perform a “Possess” action.
You’ll need to hold your interact key for three seconds for you to be able to wear the FNAF animatronic’s suit during a Fortnite match. As soon as that happens, you’ll have successfully worn that particular animatronic’s suit over your Fortnite skin.
However, it isn’t just a mere suit, as it comes with its own benefits. You see, the Five Nights at Freddy’s animatronic suit offers you a one-time immunity against being eliminated. When you’re wearing the suit and suppose an enemy manages to deplete your health bar to zero, instead of getting downed or DBNO, you’ll instantly jump out of the suit with your existing shield bar and 30 HP, but no overshield.
This works as a failsafe from being eliminated, similar to the 1-Up Extra Life token in Fortnite, but more closely to a Bush item. Once the suit breaks, you’ll need to find another FNAF animatronic in Fortnite to wear their suit and use it in your Battle Royale match.
So, did you meet any animatronic from Five Nights at Freddy’s yet during a Fortnite match? Let us know in the comments below!

New Delhi, Sep 23: Expansive red flags raised by two Election Commissioners within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision of voters list triggered a massive political storm on Wednesday, with the Opposition accusing CEC Gyanesh Kumar of indulging in "one-man autocracy" and demanding his removal.
Officials said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had flagged multiple issues, including deletion of names, in various states during the voter roll cleanup but the poll body was unanimous in its decisions related to the pan-India Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voters' list.
The reactions poured in after a report in The Indian Express revealed that questions were raised on issues related to the SIR of electoral rolls within the three-member Election Commission (EC) itself, time and again by two of the three Election Commissioners.
The national rollout of the SIR has been under the supervision of all three Commissioners. But Sandhu and Joshi have formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the last 10 months -- four times on a single day -- to decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge, the report in the English daily said.
Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared the screenshot of the media report on X.
Ramesh said that on behalf of the party, his colleague Abhishek Singhvi will be speaking in detail to the media on the sensational revelations made in the leading national newspaper on the way "the CEC has destroyed the credibility and integrity of the Election Commission of India".
Congress general secretary in-charge organisation K C Venugopal said there is no doubt remaining that Kumar has no right to remain in office.
"How the hell can one man, acting on His Master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow Constitutional officers to only take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?" he said.
"The right to vote is an essential Constitutional power given to every citizen, the fundamental bedrock of our democracy. If it is to be taken away, due process must be followed with utmost probity," he said.
"Today, when we are staring at crores of genuine voters being excluded and a similar number of bogus voters being added to the rolls, it is clear that Gyanesh Kumar was the Chief Architect of the nationwide 'Vote Chori' exercise, with the the Modi top brass pulling the strings," he alleged.
"We demand Gyanesh Kumar's immediate removal and a Supreme Court-monitored impartial investigation to expose the rot that has destroyed the ECI's credibility," Venugopal said.
If Kumar remains in office, the people of India will come forward and make sure that our democracy is not destroyed by a mere bureaucrat, he added.
Congress' media and publicity department head Pawan Khera lashed out at Kumar, saying he is "planted" and being "protected" by the BJP to hollow out the Election Commission of India from within.
"It was already known that things were not exactly well within the ECI. But just how messy, dysfunctional and, frankly, disturbing things had become is laid bare by this brilliant expose by @IndianExpress," he said on X.
Kumar has to be the single most sold-out bureaucrat of the Modi era who has disenfranchised crores of Indians, and he must face the law, he alleged.
Congress MP Manish Tewari also reacted to the media report, saying that if the ostensible facts as reported are correct then it seems to suggest that there is an "invisible hand" running the Election Commission.
"If rules were not allegedly followed and decisions were taken that were not unanimous or by majority then all the decisions of @ECISVEEP are per -se arbitrary and capricious if not completely illegal," Tewari said on X.
"This is perhaps a fit case for serious considering an impeachment proceeding but more importantly the fundamental question is as to how will the credibility of @ECISVEEP be ever resurrected," he said.
Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal demanded Kumar's suspension and filing of an FIR to probe who is behind his actions.
Former chief election commissioner O P Rawat said changes to the statutory voter registration Form 6 are "absolutely wrong and illegal", while describing revelations of differences within the Election Commission as "very serious" and "unfortunate".
CPI(M) MP John Brittas said this is no longer an Election Commission, it is a "one-man autocracy" under CEC Kumar.
"Two Election Commissioners have formally objected 14 times in 10 months. They branded the addition of new voters and mass deletion 'unauthorised and illegal'. They recorded objections to secret deletions, restorations, and form 6 changes that harass young first-time voters - all while being kept in the dark," he said.
This is the open subversion of the EC and our democracy too, Brittas said.
"Parliament must immediately start the process for the removal of the CEC. We had in fact submitted a notice for removal on 24th April, 2026 as per the constitutional stipulations - solid grounds and around 70 members signing( 50 in the stipulated number)," he said.
The Constitution provides this power for precisely such moments of institutional capture and subversion, he said.
"The Supreme Court must annul the entire SIR process without delay. When two of the three Commissioners put on record that the exercise is illegal and destructive of the electoral roll's integrity, judicial silence becomes complicity," Brittas said.
What Kumar is doing is the death knell of a democratic nation, he said.
"Remove the CEC. Strike down the SIR. Or accept that free and fair elections in India are already being buried," the CPI(M) MP said.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut also cited the media report, and said "A-Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail! He will have to go! His masters will flee the country and run away!"
TMC Rajya Sabha leader Derek O'Brien said on X, "Five months ago, 60+ Rajya Sabha MPs (50 needed) wrote to Chairman RS moving Motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar. After big news break today that two Election Commissioners objected to many of CEC's actions, it's time to bring out the RS Motion today. Impeach CEC to save democracy".

Mojang has not officially revealed the name of the Minecraft 26.4 update yet. Based on the features revealed so far and looking at the past naming patterns, we predict the name of the Minecraft 26.4 drop might be Frozen Depths.
The name of the update is purely speculative for now, but it seems to fit the environment and the upcoming new biome called Ice Caves. The heart of the update is in the frozen biomes, and the new frozen zombie variant lurking in the shadows of the Ice Caves.
What other update names come to your mind when you think about the features revealed in the Minecraft Live in September 2026? Share them with us in the comments below. With that said, let’s wait for Mojang’s official announcement to learn about the Minecraft 26.4 update name.
All New Minecraft Winter Drop Features
The upcoming Minecraft 26.4 drop is going to be focused on exploring the cold-weather biomes and the structures that generate underneath. Alongside the new biome, Mojang is also adding some environmental blocks such as a light source, a dangerous ceiling hazard, a new zombie variant, and more. So, here are all the Minecraft Winter Drop features announced till now:
Ice Caves
The Ice Caves are the third brand-new biome Mojang has added to the vanilla game in 2026, with The Sift in Minecraft launching as a new dimension in 2027.
As the name suggests, the Ice Caves are massive underground caves filled with frozen blocks. Unlike the Dripstone and Lush Caves, these generate underneath the frozen biomes in Minecraft.
The Ice Caves feature packed ice, blue ice, calcite, and other ice blocks. In addition to that, you can also find stone and deepslate blocks for mining different forms of ores inside the caves.
Ice Crystals
The ice crystals are new light source blocks in Minecraft, found in the Ice Caves biome. You can find them naturally generating on the floors, giving off a glowing appearance inside the caves. The shape of the ice crystals should remind you of Amethyst in Minecraft; however, they’ve got a unique icy texture and variant.
So, instead of filling up an Ice Cave with torches, you can use these crystals to illuminate your path. Alternatively, you can collect them and build a majestic Ice-themed castle, a palace, or similar house ideas in Minecraft.
Icicles
The icicle is another major environmental addition generated on the ceiling of the Ice Caves in Minecraft. They can form clusters and become large frozen stalactite-shaped structures similar to the Sulfur Spikes from the Minecraft Chaos Cubed update.
However, these aren’t merely decorative. When exposed to light sources, the icicle can drop down, causing harm to any entity standing under it. Falling icicles can also damage you, thereby adding an environmental hazard to the Ice Caves area.
Frozen Zombie
The 26.4 update also introduces a hostile mob in Minecraft in the form of the Frozen Zombie. The Frozen Zombie is essentially covered in ice and snow. You can encounter it mostly in snowy areas and in the Ice Caves.
The primary attacks of a Frozen Zombie include melee hits and ranged Ice Ball throws. While the melee attack can apply the freezing effect, the Ice Balls can deal more damage when thrown from a close distance.
Ice Balls
Ice Balls are a new throwable projectile associated with the Frozen Zombie. While the new zombie variants can attack with the Ice Balls, they also seem to drop the item once defeated.
The damage caused by an Ice Ball depends on its projectile speed. Faster-moving Ice Balls deal more damage, so the closer you stand to a Frozen Zombie, the more health will be depleted when it uses its ranged attacks.
Potion of Freezing
Another use of Ice Balls in Minecraft is the Potion of Freezing. Since it is a negative effect potion, you might need to make its splash variant for a more PvE or PvP-centric application.
With the splash Freezing potion in Minecraft, you can throw it on your friends or enemies to slow them down and also deal a slight amount of damage along the way.
Arrow of Freezing
The Winter update in Minecraft is also adding a new variant of tipped arrows: the Arrow of Freezing. Well, with the new freezing effect and Ice Balls, you must have already guessed what it does.
The Arrow of Freezing applies the freezing effect to the mobs it hits, alongside dealing damage. This means you can freeze enemies from a distance and potentially even the Warden in Minecraft, making the boss fight slightly less traumatizing.
And that completes the list of all features going to be released with the upcoming Minecraft 26.4 update, also known as the winter drop. What are your thoughts on the features? Tell us in the comments below.
When will the Minecraft winter update be released?
The Minecraft 26.4 winter update is speculated to be released around December 15, 2026. Mojang has not yet confirmed the official release date of this update.
What will be the name of the Minecraft 26.4 drop?
Mojang has not announced the name of the upcoming Minecraft winter update. Stay tuned for more details.

Meta billionaire Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have donated €150,000 to three GAA clubs in west Waterford, Ireland, just months after the couple purchased the historic Strancally Castle and its 440-acre estate.
The couple have chosen Shamrocks GAA in Knockanore, Tallow GAA and Lismore GAA, with each club set to receive €50,000 over a two-year period, according to multiple Irish media reports.
The donations will support projects ranging from coaching and player development to dressing-room upgrades, floodlighting, spectator facilities and community walkways.
The three clubs were selected because they are among those located closest to the couple's new property at Strancally Castle.
A spokesperson for Zuckerberg and Chan told RTÉ News that the couple wanted to support local clubs after becoming new members of the Waterford community.
In a statement, the couple said: “The GAA is at the heart of communities across Ireland.”
“As new members of the Waterford community, we're proud to support these local clubs and the important role they play,” they added.
The decision therefore appears to be linked to the couple's connection with the area rather than a wider nationwide GAA funding initiative. The donations are focused on clubs near their newly acquired Waterford estate.
Shamrocks GAA in Knockanore will receive €50,000 from the couple.
Club secretary Tim Lenehan welcomed the donation, saying it would make a significant difference to the relatively small club's fundraising efforts.
“We are delighted to receive this donation from Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan,” Lenehan said, according to The Irish Sun.
“Shamrocks is a small club and this donation will make a huge difference to our fundraising efforts,” he added.
The club plans to use the funding to support improvements, including dressing-room upgrades.
For Tallow GAA, the €50,000 donation is set to support both player development and infrastructure.
GAA treasurer Kieran Geary said the donation was the largest single donation the club has received in its 139-year history, according to The Irish Sun.
“Our first priority is to invest in coaching and games, supporting the development of our players and teams at all levels,” Geary said.
The club also plans to use the money for capital projects, including tarmacking its community walkway and developing a spectator stand at Páirc Éamonn de Paor.
The planned improvements are intended to benefit not only players but also people attending matches and other activities at the ground.
The third recipient, Lismore GAA, plans to put its €50,000 towards facility upgrades.
According to the club, the money will assist with projects including proposed floodlighting and new pitch-side fencing.
Lismore GAA secretary Emer Barry said the investment would help improve facilities for the wider community and future generations.
“This donation will help develop our facilities, which in turn will benefit the community at large, most especially the future generations,” Barry said, according to The Irish Sun.
She also welcomed the Zuckerberg-Chan family to west Waterford and said the club was proud to have been recognised through the donation.
The donation comes after Zuckerberg purchased Strancally Castle, a historic property located on the banks of the River Blackwater, north of Youghal.
The castle sits on a 440-acre estate. The price of the off-market transaction has not been publicly disclosed, although Irish media reports have estimated it at around €20 million to €30 million.
The present castle is about 4.5km upriver from the ruins of an earlier Strancally Castle, which was among several fortifications built in the area by the Desmond family.
Zuckerberg and Chan are understood to continue living in the United States, with Strancally Castle expected to serve as a base when the family is in Ireland.
The property could also be used when Zuckerberg is carrying out business for Meta in Ireland, where the technology company has a significant presence.

England call up Crane and rest Archer for Pakistan series
- Published
Leg-spinner Mason Crane could play for England for the first time in eight years after being recalled for the one-day international tri-series in Pakistan.
The 29-year-old won his only Test cap against Australia in Sydney in 2018 and is now given an opportunity in the series which also involves Sri Lanka next month.
Crane, who also played two T20 internationals in 2017, could also push his case in the fight to be England's number one spinner in Test cricket.
Sam Curran and Adil Rashid both return after injuries, and uncapped pair James Coles and Henry Crocombe are included.
Jos Buttler is out with the hamstring injury he sustained last week, while Jacob Bethell is continuing his recovery from knee surgery.
Brydon Carse, who is under an investigation from the Cricket Regulator following an incident outside a nightclub in Derby in August, remains absent.
———————————————————
England squad for tri-series in Pakistan: Harry Brook (Yorkshire – captain), Gus Atkinson (Surrey), Sonny Baker (Hampshire), Tom Banton (Somerset), James Coles (Sussex), Jordan Cox (Essex), Mason Crane (Glamorgan), Henry Crocombe (Sussex), Sam Curran (Surrey), Liam Dawson (Hampshire), Ben Duckett (Nottinghamshire), Will Jacks (Surrey), Jamie Overton (Surrey), Adil Rashid (Yorkshire), Joe Root (Yorkshire), Josh Tongue (Nottinghamshire).
———————————————————
England are on a diet of white-ball cricket until three Tests in South Africa in December as they build up to the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa next year.
The tri-series in Pakistan involves the three teams taking part playing each other twice, with the top two advancing to the final. Following the trip to Pakistan, England play three one-day internationals and five T20s in Australia in November.
As England continue to shape their backroom staff following the arrival of Stephen Fleming as Test coach, Jeetan Patel, Mike Yardy, David Saker and Carl Hopkinson will assist white-ball head coach Bendon McCullum in Pakistan.
That means Marcus Trescothick, who took temporary charge of the Test team for the series against Pakistan in the home summer, misses the trip.
It is understood the make-up of the coaching staff is part of a plan to rotate the coaches – fielding coach Sarah Taylor and fast-bowling coach Tim Southee are also not going to Pakistan.
All of Trescothick, Taylor and Southee are likely to be part of England's coaching team for other tours this winter.
Can Crane push case for spot in Test squad?
The return of Glamorgan's Crane is eye-catching, given the close proximity of the World Cup and the uncertainty surrounding the spin-bowling in England's Test team.
The former Hampshire man is rewarded for consistent performances across formats in domestic cricket.
This season Crane took 34 wickets in the County Championship and demonstrated his improvement with the bat by making his first two first-class hundreds.
England national selector Marcus North said: "Mason Crane has been performing consistently for Glamorgan across both formats during the summer. He's an experienced, high-class leg-spinner who thoroughly deserves another opportunity at international level."
Archer is a first choice in all three formats for England and his absence from the Pakistan trip is a clear indication of how the pace bowlers could be managed across the winter.
McCullum has already indicated other seamers could skip the T20 series in Australia in order to prepare for the three Tests in South Africa.
England are expected to name their squad for the Australia tour, along with their new list of centrally contracted players, next week.

TEL AVIV, Israel — A commercial flight traveling from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Tel Aviv was forced to make an emergency landing after issuing an emergency alert onboard.

He was one of the most passionate propagandists for Hugo Chávez’s Bolivarian revolution: a feisty leftist TV personality who spent more than two decades singing the movement’s praises on his state-funded show, The Razorblade.
Mario Silva’s devotion was such that he often hosted his programme with Chávez’s portrait behind him and he had El Comandante’s curly signature tattooed on to his left wrist.
But nine months after Venezuela’s political landscape was scrambled by Donald Trump’s abduction of Chávez’s heir, Nicolás Maduro, Silva’s show has been cancelled, and its host is livid about the revolution’s direction under Maduro’s former deputy, Delcy Rodríguez.
“[I feel] a lot of disappointment – depressed … and sometimes I wake up and feel like the world is collapsing around me,” the 66-year-old said during a rare interview at his home studio in the mountains outside the capital, Caracas.
Silva has spent recent weeks railing against Rodríguez’s interim administration on YouTube, his home since his programme on state TV was axed, berating those he blames for Venezuela’s “shameful and utterly illegitimate surrender” to the US.
Since January, a parade of high-ranking US officials – including the head of the CIA, the chair of the joint chiefs of staff and the energy secretary, Chris Wright – have visited Caracas, while Trump recently trumpeted striking “the biggest oil deal in world history” with Rodríguez’s regime. Last week, Rodríguez and Trump met on the sidelines of the UN general assembly, posing for a smiley photograph that left diehard Chavistas such as Silva aghast.
“I thought it [the photo] was artificial intelligence or something like that. But it’s surrealism, utter surrealism … It’s impossible to understand,” Silva fumed on YouTube as a red flag emblazoned with the faces of Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels and Vladimir Lenin hung behind him.
“They have surrendered this country and surrendered it the most vile and despicable way,” Silva went on. “Honestly, they are dragging the country’s name through the mud. They are dragging Chávez’s name through the mud.”
In another broadcast, Silva seethed about the cosy post-Maduro relationship that has developed between one-time anti-imperialist flagbearers in Caracas and Trump officials: “Traitors and lackeys, you will have to answer for this!”
Silva is not the only Chavista loyalist struggling to comprehend the ideological U-turn being executed by Rodríguez, who was Maduro’s vice-president but has engineered a historic rapprochement with the US since his rendition on 3 January.
Elías Jaua, a vice-president and foreign minister under Chávez, is also up in arms, and claims the feeling is widely shared. “What I hear from comrades across the country is bewilderment, disagreement and indignation,” said Jaua, who believes Trump’s oil deal “amounts to an act of pillage against an entire nation”.
Juan Barreto, a former member of the ruling Socialist party (PSUV) and mayor of Caracas, said such an agreement would have been unimaginable when the Bolivarian revolution began after Chávez’s 1998 election. He said Chavistas, who had once vowed “Not a drop of oil to the empire if Venezuela is attacked!”, were now in effect saying: “All of the oil reserves [for the US], for as long as you want!”
“The current situation is one of tutelage,” Barreto said.
Rodríguez has defended the deal, claiming it will create more than $209bn (£158bn) in revenues that will help improve healthcare and education. “We are thinking of Venezuela’s future,” she said in a recent TV broadcast.
Héctor Rodríguez, another prominent Chavista politician, has sought to deflect criticism of Venezuela’s interim government by recalling how Chávez was forced to make a tactical retreat after his failed coup attempt in 1992. “No one can tell me Chávez was a coward. He understood that the balance of power had shifted … and decided to take a step backwards,” Rodríguez said recently.
Last week as Delcy Rodríguez met Trump in New York, thousands of people joined a pro-government rally in Caracas, where supporters parroted the slogan “Delcy avanza, tú tienes mi confianza!” (“Move forward, Delcy. I trust in you!”).
“No matter how much they kick and scream, there’s nothing they can do to try to cover up the success of President Delcy Rodríguez’s visit to New York,” her interior minister, Diosdado Cabello, told the crowd. Unlike at previous marches, there was scant mention of Maduro and few calls for him to be released.
The depth and potential consequences of Chavista anger over Rodríguez’s embrace of Venezuela’s longtime foes in Washington remain unclear.
Orlando Pérez, a Latin America expert from the University of North Texas at Dallas, recognised there was indignation at what some considered a sellout of their anti-imperialist ideals. “There are Chavistas that are pissed off, there’s no question about it,” he said. “There are Chavistas who see this as a betrayal of Hugo Chávez and the betrayal of the movement.”
But Pérez believed that for many Chavistas who had remained in power after Trump’s invasion, the “pragmatic reality” was that working with Washington was “a necessary evil” if it meant keeping Venezuela’s opposition out of power.
“If that means negotiating with Trump, if that means dealing with the CIA etc, it’s fine,” he said. “Beyond whatever ideological position they might have … I suspect most of them are gritting their teeth and just going along with this process as long as they can stay in power and keep their jobs. I think for most it’s as simple as that: it’s about their material wellbeing.”
However, Pérez believed Rodríguez’s government would need to demonstrate to supporters “tangible benefits to the cooperation” with the US in order to avoid a backlash. “They’re going to have to show that these things have a material consequence to the lives of their social base … if you don’t deliver, then it is going to get very volatile,” he warned.
So far there has been no sign of significant resistance from outraged supporters of Chavismo. But Silva claimed the government’s new direction and economic policies could eventually trigger a social uprising and protests.
“Worsening economic conditions will degrade [people’s] quality of life, and that pressure is bound to explode. It has to explode – it’s not just wishful thinking. This isn’t a prediction born of desire, it’s an inevitability,” said the broadcaster, who has claimed he is facing investigation for alleged acts of “aggravated defamation and slander against the interim government”.
Silva lit one cigarette after another as he recalled the early hours of 3 January 2026 when, as US troops swept into Venezuela’s capital, he realised the revolution he had spent more than 20 years defending was not going to defend itself.
The Chavista broadcaster said he moved from one strategic point to another across Caracas before finally calling the commander at his assigned post. “I said: ‘Hey, what happened? Where are the weapons?’” Silva recalled, his face settling into a sad grin as he remembered the answer. “Go to sleep, Mario,” he was told.
Silva pauses. “You have no idea how disappointed I was.”

'I don't even know if my parents are alive' - the war heroes jailed 25 years ago
- Published
Hanna Petros Solomon breaks down in tears as she recalls how she and her siblings effectively became orphans 25 years ago when their father was arrested in Eritrea and jailed without trial. Their mother was subsequently detained - and no-one has heard from either of them - or of them - since.
"He had a towel on his shoulders like a sportsman," she tells the BBC about the last time she saw her father when she was 10 years old, and he had gone out for a jog.
"He used to work out every morning."
Her parents met when they both fought in the long liberation war that saw Eritrea gain independence from Ethiopia in 1993.
Her father Petros Solomon had been one of the senior leaders during the war and is regarded by many as a national hero for his critical role.
After independence, he had served as defence minister, then foreign minister and had been heading the fisheries ministry when his troubles began.
That was in May 2001 when he and 14 other high-profile politicians signed an open letter to President Isaias Afewerki calling for the implementation of a constitution that was ratified after independence and demanding national elections. They became known as the G-15.
Isaias, the leader of the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF) which had fought against Ethiopia, did not take the criticism well.
Unbeknown to Hanna, her father had been dismissed as a minister, though he still went out early to get some exercise each day.
It was not until a few days after 9/11 - when the world was distracted by the al-Qaeda attacks on the US - that the country was to discover the full extent of Isais's displeasure in what became a watershed moment in Eritrea's history.
In the early hours of 18 September, the security forces positioned themselves outside the homes of 11 senior government officials in the capital, Asmara, on the president's orders.
Petros was picked up by security agents as he left in his tracksuit.
The family had no idea what had happened to him. Hanna and her three siblings went to stay with their paternal grandmother as their mother, Aster Yohannes, was away studying in the US.
It was only some days after Petros had disappeared that things became clearer, says Hanna about the painful memories.
"My classmates told me that my father sold out his country.
"That is when I understood how serious the situation was, and how people framed my dad and his colleagues who fought for the independence of their country. I was hurt."
In the US, Aster was shell-shocked by what had happened - and was in a very bad way. She asked government officials if they could issue the children with passports - but they refused, telling her to come home.
After agonising about the situation for two years and reportedly receiving assurances from government officials, she packed her bags to return.
Hanna and her siblings desperately wanted her back - but they were also worried.
"I told her on the phone: 'What if they arrest you?'" Hanna remembers.
"She insisted nothing would happen to her, saying: 'I haven't done anything wrong, and am only coming to raise my children.'"
Hanna says she learned later that President Isaias himself had promised Aster that she would be safe. But while the family waited at Asmara International Airport on 11 December 2003, she failed to emerge through arrivals with the other passengers.
Their hopes began to wilt along with the flowers they had brought: "It was a long, long wait. Eventually we gave up and went back home.
"First we called to the US, friends and relatives told us they saw her off at the airport."
Then ominously an official called from the airport asking Aster to collect her luggage. That is when they realised she had arrived in the country but would not be coming home.
All pleas and requests for information fell on deaf ears in the months that followed. Instead Hanna's grandmother was warned by authorities to stop inquiring.
The family later heard that Aster was being held in the infamous jail known as Karshelli in the heart of Asmara.
Hanna's father is believed to be detained, with the others arrested on 18 and 19 September 2001, in the remote, hostile and highly secretive prison known as Ela-Ero, located in eastern lowlands north-east of Asmara. Accused of treason, none of them has ever been brought to trial or allowed to see their relatives.
At around the same time, the government also shut down all the fledgling independent newspapers and detained their editors and journalists - also believed to be imprisoned in Ela-Ero.
The Eritrean government - including its embassy in the UK - has not responded to the BBC's request for comment regarding the whereabouts of the prisoners or whether or not they are alive.
Hanna, like many thousands of young Eritreans fleeing conscription and in search of better opportunities, left the country - travelling secretively over the border without a passport.
Now 35 years old, she is married and lives in the US, working as a trauma specialist - but still feels traumatised herself by how she lost her parents.
As she stares at old pictures of her parents, she worries her memories will fade of the happy times before their arrest - the laughter, the family gatherings, the birthday parties: "My dad always wanted to gather people in the house, they were good days."
She also hankers after her mother's "unmatched" egg and potato sandwiches.
On trips down to the coast when her father was the minister of fisheries, Hanna remembers him organising singing competitions in the car: "He would ask us to sing one by one and whoever won would get a present."
One of his favourite songs included the lyrics: "I had a sweater, a blue sweater, that my sister took" - which reminded him of his sister who was also a freedom fighter and had been killed during the war.
She also has memories of her mother loving music - playing and singing hits by Abba, Dolly Parton and Whitney Houston.
Until her father's arrest, Hanna remembers September as being full of hope with its three big Orthodox Christian festivals, including the Geez New Year. Now the month brings her no joy.
Ibrahim Sherifo knows exactly how she feels. Both his parents, who were senior members of the ruling People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), were among the G-15 people arrested 25 years ago.
He was 13 years old at the time
"For me 18 September 2001 is a dark day, but not only for me, it is a dark day for Eritrea and its people, because it is the day when law and democracy was detained," he tells the BBC.
He is now 38 and living in exile in the Netherlands, where he was granted asylum, and is pursuing an MA in political science - following in his father's footsteps.
His dad Mahmoud Ahmed Sherifo was the local government minister and de facto deputy president before his detention.
Ibrahim was with his mother, Aster Fissehatsion, staying with her sister when he remembers security agents knocking on the door early in the morning and taking her away in her pyjamas.
Worried about his father, Ibrahim immediately ran to his nearby house but was told he had already been picked up when he had gone out for exercise.
Both Hanna and Ibrahim say they are forever grateful to the friends and family who offered them care and supported them as they grew up without their parents, despite the risks.
They are also proud of what their parents stood for and daring to call for reforms.
"They had conscience and couldn't observe idly while what they fought for what had been hijacked by Isaias and his coterie," says Ibrahim.
"As a family, we should be informed whether they are alive or not," he adds, accusing the government of wanting to erase all memory of the political prisoners.
Hanna also wants the plight of the many others whose relatives have disappeared over the years to be heard too.
Sometimes it is calm and you can float, but other times the sorrow comes back to you like a wave and drowns you deep down"
Human rights groups, including the UN, consider the G-15 prisoners of conscience and have been calling for their release.
President Isaias, now 80, has still not implemented the country's first constitution - approved in 1997 - and remains in power without ever holding an election.
Hanna recalls that on the eve of her father's disappearance, she had a "bad feeling" - and had crept into his bed and tied his legs to her own with string while he slept.
"In the morning he woke up to find he was tied up and to release himself he pulled my legs and I woke up. I begged him not to leave but he assured me that he would return [after his run]."
Describing the years of sorrow since, she says it is like living in the deep sea.
"Sometimes it is calm and you can float, but other times the sorrow comes back to you like a wave and drowns you deep down.
"Sometimes you lose hope and you are out of breath."
Asked what she would say if she could get a message to her parents, she replies: "Don't worry about us.
"Like you survived the struggle through sheer steadfastness, we hope you can pull through this too and return to us."

President Donald Trump's daughter-in-law addressed a possibility that the White House has largely sought to downplay: The war in Iran could cost Republicans the midterms.
In an appearance on the YouTube show "Harry Cole Saves the West" on Wednesday, Lara Trump, who is married to Donald Trump's son, Eric Trump, spoke about the possible impact of the war on the midterms as Americans contend with the conflict's rising economic toll.
On his show, Cole asked the Fox News host and former cochair of the Republican National Committee about Donald Trump's handling of the ongoing war, saying that it "could cost him his legacy."
"Well, it could cost him these midterms," Lara Trump said. "I think Donald Trump's legacy has yet to be written, and I think that in a lot of ways — I still say he's going to go down in history as one of the greatest presidents, if not the greatest America has ever seen — but you're right. The last two years really matter."
At the White House on Thursday, Donald Trump was asked if he agreed with his daughter-in-law's political assessment.
The president told reporters "it's possible" the war could hurt Republicans in the midterms, but argued it "should help" because Iran would not have a nuclear weapon.
"So when you say, 'Is it OK for Iran to have a nuclear weapon?' I would say 100% of the people say no, including worldwide," he said."So when you say it that way, it would help. If you don't say that, it could hurt."
Though Lara Trump holds no official role in the Trump administration, her statement appeared to be a rare acknowledgment from a member of the president's inner circle that Republicans could struggle to maintain control of the House and the Senate if the war continues.
Still, later in the interview she said the president "really hates the way that things have gone with Iran" and wished that "things had more swiftly happened."
Vice President JD Vance took a different approach when asked in September if the Iran war would be over by the midterm elections. Vance said that he "wouldn't call it a war," touted the accomplishments of Operations Midnight Hammer and Epic Fury, and added, "You would have to ask the Iranians."
The Iran war remains a tough sell as voters grapple with rising energy prices and inflation driven by the conflict. In June, Moody's Analytics estimated that the war cost US households $100 billion in its first three months — nearly $750 per household.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider.

Srinagar, Sep 22: National Conference MLA from the Baramulla constituency, Javid Hassan Baigh, on Tuesday said tourism was not solely dependent on the scenic beauty of the destination but was deeply tied to the prevailing situation of the place as well.
Talking to Greater Kashmir outside the Assembly complex, MLA Baramulla cited the example of Gulmarg, which witnessed no visitors during the period of conflict.
"Tourism is not only related to beauty, it is also related to the situation. Gulmarg is a beautiful place, but during tense situation no one visited the place. You should not link tourism to beauty," MLA Baigh told Greater Kashmir.
He said tourism is a culture that needs to be developed through a gradual process.
"I will share details of several projects for Baramulla once they materialise. When many such projects will come for Baramulla, I will share them with you. You will get an idea of where our government is and how many projects have come to Baramulla," he said.
Talking about the developmental challenges in his constituency, MLA Baramulla said Baramulla's problems are inherited, with land scarcity being the foremost hurdle.
"The problem in Baramulla is that we have inherited from the past. For example, we do not have acute scarcity of land," he said.
He said the expansion and decongestion of Sopore, a project worth Rs 500 to 1,000 crore, was under discussion.
"CM Omar Abdullah (sahab) called me and asked to identify 200 acres of land so that we can decongest Baramulla. I met the Commissioner Secretary of Urban Development. But the issue is that land is not available," he added.
"I do not have land for a hockey ground in Baramulla. Do you have any land in Baramulla? The whole land in Baramulla is either with defence or the government offices. So, how can we decongest Baramulla? you tell me," he said.
He also pushed back against the perception that Baramulla alone had been left behind, saying, it wrong to say that only Baramulla is backward.
"Not only Baramulla, but everyone in Kashmir has seen an unexpected situation over the last 35 years," he said.
He, however, said that people of Baramulla will soon receive the good news with regard to the developmental projects.

Man City not 'above the rules', says No 10 after backlash to Burnham remarks
- Published
Downing Street has said Manchester City are not "above the rules" after Andy Burnham was criticised for his comments about the club's breaches of Premier League financial rules.
The prime minister said on Wednesday he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners decide to sell up after City were found guilty by an independent commission of most of the 115 charges they faced.
His remarks were branded "completely out of touch" and "extraordinary" by the Tories and took many in the football community by surprise.
In a statement following the backlash, Downing Street said the PM had made clear "the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules".
In an attempt to clarify the PM's position, a No 10 spokesperson added: "He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.
"Wherever wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."
Man City deny any wrongdoing and have until Friday to submit an appeal.
Sources told BBC Sport that City are expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of an appeal.
Among the independent panel's findings were that City arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m.
The Premier League said City "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade".
In an interview on Wednesday with the BBC's political editor Chris Mason, Burnham - who was mayor of Greater Manchester until June - said he was "not getting directly involved in the process", saying it must be undertaken independently by the Premier League.
He said the situation was "contested by Manchester City" and it would be "wrong" to "jump to a conclusion".
Asked if he was worried the club's owners since 2008 - led by Sheikh Mansour, a royal and the United Arab Emirates deputy prime minister - might sell up, Burnham said: "I would be really concerned to lose them.
"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.
"I can't intervene more in the process, it would be wrong for me to do that."
In response, the Tories accused Burnham of "publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues" and questioned whether "political pressure" was being applied.

Shadow minister for sport Louie French called for the government to "keep politics out of football and ensure the Premier League's independent commission can do its job free of outside influence".
"The club face unprecedented allegations and fans are horrified by what they are reading in the papers," the Tory MP said.
"Yet Burnham is publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues. Fans will rightly ask whether political pressure is being applied here and how it relates to the owners' well-reported investments in Manchester.
"Football must be governed independently, with the rules applying equally to everyone. Fans deserve confidence that no club or owner is above those rules."
And Lib Dem MP Anna Sabine, the party's spokesperson on sport, said: "Fans of every club deserve to know the rules apply to everyone... Burnham needs to remember he's prime minister for everyone, not just Manchester."
It comes as the chairwoman of the Commons Treasury committee, Labour MP Dame Meg Hillier, wrote to HMRC on Thursday to ask for reassurance that it has "seized of the importance" of the case for any potential tax implications.
In his BBC interview, Burnham also said he was "of course" confident that his own interactions with City's owners as Greater Manchester mayor would stand up to scrutiny.
He compared City's situation to how the club he supports, Everton, had been charged with a more minor breach of Premier League financial rules in 2023, but said he "hold[s] the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process".
Burnham made his comments amid widespread shock in football about the scale of the independent commission's findings – and the strength of Premier League comments about City's actions.
The independent panel that found City guilty of rule breaches will hold a sanctions hearing – which could take months to convene – to decide the punishment, which could include a huge fine or points deduction.
City have maintained their innocence of all the accusations made.
The chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) – set up by the government in 2025 – said the case had raised "serious issues".
In a statement, David Kogan said the IFR "has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate", while "taking account of the findings made by the Leagues".
He added that proceedings remain ongoing and he hoped for a quick resolution.

- The claim that a video shows shoppers in a U.K. grocery store standing in gender-segregated lines is still under investigation.
- The footage itself is real, meaning not created by an artificial intelligence tool. It shows shoppers at Masala Bazaar in Chadwell Heath, East London, standing in lines split by gender. A TikTok user who appears to be a store employee, as of this writing, posted it on Sept. 28, 2026.
- Some social media users speculated that the apparent gender segregation seen in the clip was due to the shoppers' Muslim faith or culture.
- The store's management reportedly told the Daily Mail newspaper it does not have a gender segregation policy. The video shows the lines were not entirely segregated and other footage from the store on different dates shows men and women mixing freely.
- It remains unclear at the time of publication why shoppers at Masala Bazaar stood in mostly gender-segregated lines in the Sept. 28 footage.
- Snopes contacted the person who posted the original clip and Masala Bazaar to ask about the lines. We await replies to our queries.
In September 2026, footage circulated online purportedly showing shoppers in a U.K. grocery store standing in gender-segregated lines.
For example, a popular Facebook user who posted a video commenting on the clip appears to speculate that the alleged segregation was due to the ethnic, cultural or religious community or communities the shoppers belong to. The narrator says (archived):
This video is going viral online because everybody's wondering, "Why is it, how is it, that in the year 2026 you could be in the U.K. and have to stand in a separate line depending on your gender?"
That tells you, you have a community of people that really, really do not want to adapt. I mean, the U.K. is not going to require women to stand in a different line. But for whatever reason, these communities want that.
Posts on Reddit (archived) and Instagram (archived) say English shoppers were "irritated" for being "forced to obey the rules of Islamist migrants in their own country."
The footage appears to be authentic, meaning not created using artificial intelligence. It was seemingly recorded inside Masala Bazaar, a supermarket in Chadwell Heath near Romford, East London. A TikTok user, who also appears in a promotional video (archived) for the supermarket, posted the clip (archived) of the apparently gender-segregated lines to TikTok on Sept. 28, 2026.
While the video appears to show a real-life situation, it is unclear whether the shoppers "had to" stand in what appear to be gender-segregated lines or whether the grocery store or anyone else "forced" them to do so, as some social media users have said.
Snopes contacted the TikTok user who posted the original video, who appears to be a store employee at the time of publication, and Masala Bazaar to ask whether the store enforces gender-segregated lines or whether it has another explanation for why the shoppers appeared to line up this way. We await replies to our queries.
In the meantime, because the reason for the apparent gender-segregated lines is unconfirmed, we leave this claim unrated.
According to British tabloid newspaper the Daily Mail, bosses at Masala Bazaar told the outlet the supermarket does not have a gender segregation policy and that the lines in the video were the result of "temporary queue management" during a busy sale event.
Closer inspection of the footage shows the lines of shoppers were divided mostly along gender lines. However, at least one person with a beard can be seen in the line primarily made up of women, and one person wearing a headscarf is standing toward the front of the line predominately consisting of men.
(@mutabbirmia21, accessed via TikTok, illustrated by Snopes)
It is unclear as of this writing whether men and women lining up mostly separately was driven by cultural or religious norms rather than supermarket rules.
Some social media posts appear to suggest the apparent division happened because the shoppers are Muslims. Some, but not all, Muslims practice gender segregation in some situations, such as during prayers in a mosque or in schools.
Other videos, posted by the same TikTok user who shared the Sept. 28 clip, show that while men and women inside the store sometimes group together (archived) with their own gender, shoppers also sometimes mix (archived) regardless of gender.
According to the most recent census data from 2021, 31% of people in the London Borough of Redbridge, where Masala Bazaar is located, are Muslims, meaning it is possible the shoppers were Muslims.

China’s intelligence service used a front company to pay grants to British universities and steal crucial research about technology projects, MI5 said on Wednesday in a rare public espionage warning.
Britain’s domestic security service said researchers and academics should cease work with the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI), sometimes also known as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT). MI5 believes it poses a “significant threat”.
The Chinese organisation has given money to 100 or more academics at a string of universities across the UK, in return getting access to the research, which it is alleged found its way back to China’s intelligence service.
MI5 is now prepared to say publicly that the CGTRI is a front for Chinese intelligence, namely the Chinese ministry of state security (MSS). It said continued collaboration could be prosecuted under the National Security Act 2023.
Areas of research targeted include AI, cybersecurity, covert communications, and the embedding of data in pictures online called steganography. MI5 believes it has clear evidence of sensitive information being passed back to Chinese intelligence. The Guardian understands that as well as research money, some British-based academics were given awards, as in honours, by the Chinese.
Successive British governments have courted Chinese investment and encouraged cooperation.
In the alert issued on Wednesday, the Security Service said: “MI5 has identified that the primary purpose of CGTRI is to fund academic research that directly improves MSS technical capability for espionage.”
It said that the CGTRI had “very strong ties to the … MSS, China’s civilian intelligence and security service”.
It added: “Many academic institutions and individuals will to date have engaged with CGTRI in good faith given CGTRI’s obfuscated links to MSS.
“UK academic institutions are strongly advised to immediately review any ongoing or planned collaboration with CGTRI. This is to ensure MSS derives no further benefit from UK universities or research institutions. Further, academics are advised to establish the ultimate funding source when conducting any research collaboration with Chinese institutions, to ensure CGTRI is not involved.”
The alert warns of “potential criminal consequences”, in a section issued after consultation with the Crown Prosecution Service, which authorises criminal prosecutions in England and Wales.
“Through this espionage alert, MI5 has placed the fact that CGTRI has very strong ties to MSS in the public domain,” it states. “Going forward, academic institutions, staff and researchers should ensure they are aware of the National Security Act 2023, particularly offences under section 3 (assisting a foreign intelligence service) and section 17 (obtaining a material benefit from a foreign intelligence service).
“Under section 3, an offence is committed if the person a) engages in conduct that is likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out UK-related activities, and b) knows, or having regard to other matters known to them ought reasonably to know, that their conduct is likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out UK-related activities.”
Such is the scale of Chinese state espionage targeting the UK that MI5 has decided on a deterrence strategy via a public alert such as this, rather than pursuing every single case. It hopes universities will heed the warning and immediately cease their work with the CGTRI.
The Guardian understands MI5 believes Chinese intelligence gained access to cutting-edge British research on scraping social media (searching and retaining useful information from social media sites).
The National Security and Investment Act 2021 could prevent a state such as China, assessed as having hostile intent towards the UK, from buying access to the technology on a commercial basis.
The security minister, Dan Jarvis, demanded universities end ties to the CGTRI. He said: “This alert exposes attempts by Chinese intelligence to covertly benefit from the expertise and research of our academics, undermining our national security and that of our allies.
“I have written to all university vice-chancellors to ensure they support their staff to end all arrangements with this company, preventing further benefit to the Chinese intelligence services and ensuring compliance with the National Security Act.”
He added: “International partnerships are vital to ensure our universities and research institutes continue to thrive, but we will take robust action to defend against the threats we face. That means supporting our police and intelligence services to expose and disrupt harmful activity, using the full force of the law.”
Responding to the MI5 alert, Vivienne Stern, the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents 142 institutions across the UK, said universities took their responsibilities around research security and national security extremely seriously.
“The sector has made significant investments in recent years to strengthen due diligence, risk assessment and research security processes, while continuing to support the international collaboration that is essential to world-leading research and innovation,” she said.
“Close engagement between government and the higher education sector is vital to ensuring that universities and the country continue to benefit from international collaboration while effectively managing national security risks.”
Libby Hackett, the chief executive of the Russell Group of research-intensive universities, said: “All our universities take national security responsibilities very seriously. Working closely with government departments and the security services enables universities to take swift action to protect UK interests – and we will continue to do so in the face of new and emerging threats”.
The Chinese embassy has been approached for comment.

A roar from the crowd reached a crescendo and waned amidst mighty chinars, encircling the Sher-e-Kashmir Cricket Stadium in Srinagar, on Thursday (October 1, 2026) marked the first-ever Irani Cup 2026 match and created history. Cut to 1983, the same ground and the same month saw 21 men storming the ground during the lunch break and damaging the pitch in a bid to disrupt the India versus West Indies match.
With the J&K Cricket Association (JKCA) limiting the crowd strength to a manageable 5000 in the stadium, those who sit in the stands are monitored to ensure the history is not repeated. The Association also screened beforehand the guests and invitees and issued limited passes to the outside crowds, officials told The Hindu.
As the J&K Team dominated the Rest of India at pace on day one of the five-day match, it has buoyed even the political will of the ruling National Conference (NC). “It is a good sign that Kashmir is hosting the Irani Cup 2026. We are happy to see the first-ever five-day match being played in Kashmir,” said Nasir Aslam Wani, NC leader and adviser to Chief Minister Omar Abdullah.
Back on October 13, 1983, the same party, NC, was ruling J&K when 21 men, with 12 accused identified later, waited in the wings till lunch was declared and stormed into the ground to dig the pitch, “in a bid to internationalise the Kashmir issue”. Those accused included two separatist leaders, Shakeel Bakshi and Shabir Ahmad Shah. However, the court acquitted them in 2011 “for lack of evidence”. Locals supported West India more than the Indian team. It took 22 years of trial to decide the case and acquit the accused later.
However, this time the political atmosphere, even though there are multiple security rings, has taken a complete turn with crowds whistling, clapping, bugling and enjoying the match.
“We intend to invest in cricket infrastructure of Kashmir to host IPL matches in the future too. We are indeed in the process of that. Right now, our focus is upgrading the infrastructure in districts and tehsils. We want to hone the skills of local talent and provide a platform to showcase their skills,” said Mr. Wani.
Pointing out the pacer Aquib Nabi, who debuted in a test match for India last month, Mr. Wani said, “Kashmir has cricketing potential. Mr. Nabi already proved it. These kinds of matches will allow our talent not to establish at the local level but at the country level,” said Mr. Wani.
With this Irani Cup rewriting the history on the ground, BCCI chairman Mithun Manhas is enthusiastic to “to bring more matches to Kashmir”. “A match of this level is happening after almost four decades, so it is a matter of great happiness. Cricket has returned. Efforts from the Board will continue and JKCA will have full support of the BCCI so that they can organize matches on a bigger scale and also bring international games,” said Mr. Manhas.
With uncanny celebrations in the stands, the West Indies’ victory over India by 28 runs in 1983 may have restrained the government’s will to host more such matches in the Valley, but the Irani Cup has already succeeded in writing a new chapter of history on the same ground.
