What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
LONDON — He was one of my most memorable interviews. Even though we were both speaking English, I could barely understand a word he was saying.
"The costermongers, wheeze used to fly-pitch, on this frog and toad," he said — at least I think, after listening to my tape several times again, none the wiser.
Our interview was back in 2016, on one of my first NPR reporting trips to London. George Major, then 78, was a local celebrity. We walked together through the East End, where the factories and docklands that Major grew up around during World War II have given way to glass skyscrapers. A vendor ran out into the street to slap him high-five. Tourists snapped photos.
Major had turned up in bling: A black suit and flat cap, both festooned with sequins, sparkles and mother-of-pearl buttons. His title — Pearly King of Peckham — was spelled out in shimmering buttons across the back of his jacket.
He was a charming wheeler-dealer. But his language — a mix of what he called "backspeak" and Cockney rhyming slang — was impossible for this hapless American visitor to understand.
At one point in our video interview, I glanced at the camera and exclaimed, "We might need a translator here!"
Ten years later, I chuckle whenever I land at Heathrow Airport, where a portrait of Major covers an entire wall. But this summer, a former colleague alerted me to an item in the local press, which hit me harder than I expected: The Pearly King of Peckham died Aug. 1, aged 88.
He was buried Sept. 14 in a cemetery not far from the Cockney Museum he founded. A horse-drawn cart carried his casket into a little chapel, whose walls shook with mourners singing raucous pub songs. One of the gardeners outside looked bewildered.
At the gravesite, I approached the Major family, offered condolences, and hesitantly shared the story of my brief, confusing 2016 encounter with their loved one.
A horde of pearly kings, queens, princes and princesses — four generations of Major's family, all in matching pearly suits — turned and looked at me, some through tears, then threw back their heads and laughed.
"A real Cockney cheeky chappy!" his daughter Janet Major said, hugging me.
Who are the pearly royals?
In the 1870s, an orphaned street sweeper named Henry Croft began decorating his suit with mother-of-pearl buttons scavenged from the streets outside textile factories that used to dot London's East End.
His pearly garb infused menial work with dignity — a royal air, even — and launched what would become a working-class East London institution: The pearly kings and queens.
"These pearly suits are now cultural artifacts with fantastic designs, telling a profound story about London and Cockneys, what we call the non-posh Londoners," says Andy Green, co-founder of the Modern Cockney Festival, an annual celebration of diverse, working-class communities in London.
Some of the so-called pearlies were street hawkers, market vendors or fly-pitchers — unlicensed traders. Others canvassed for charity. Many were immigrants, their slang peppered with words from Yiddish or Bengali. They became neighborhood fixtures, in mother-of-pearl finery.
"You had what are called costermongers, which is a posh word for street hawkers, street sellers," Green says. "Imagine you're a newly arrived immigrant in the country. One of the first jobs you could possibly do might be to hustle, sell goods on the street."
That's what George Major did. Born in 1938 inside a military barracks in Peckham, southeast London, he was abandoned as a child, grew up in a workhouse, and found odd jobs in the local market as a teenager, his daughter Janet explains.
"Dad eventually became one of the costermonger kings that used to run market stalls," she says. "It was not an easy childhood, but he followed the ideals of Henry Croft. That was before the welfare state, when you had to help your friends, your neighbors, your community."
Janet Major describes the weekends of her childhood, with her father leading all seven of his children, walking door to door in matching pearly suits, asking for money for charity.
Nowadays, a dwindling number of pearlies still canvass for charities like children's hospitals, women's shelters and veterans groups. They appear at summertime street festivals and march in parades.
George Major later trained as a plumber and ran a plumbing supply shop, she says.
The pearlies in pop culture
Onscreen, the pearly kings inspired the streetwise, heart-of-gold chimney sweep character of Bert in Walt Disney's Mary Poppins film — played by Dick Van Dyke, an American who later owned up to what he called "the most atrocious Cockney accent in the history of cinema."
The Major family and others believe George Major himself inspired another fictional character: Del Boy, the happy-go-lucky East London huckster in the long-running British sitcom Only Fools and Horses. He's a cheeky salesman, always scheming to get rich quick, with the catchphrase, "This time next year, we'll be millionaires!"
At his funeral, Major's eulogy was riddled with Del Boy quotes.
But like the TV protagonist, Major also broke the law. In 2012 he was sentenced to six months in prison, after pleading guilty to benefits fraud. He was released early.
"If he could avoid the tax man, he would!" his daughter laughs. "He used to say, 'Discount for cash!' He'd love a bargain."
His fame overshadowed his legal troubles. Major was one of dozens of pearly royals who marched in the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics.
What's Cockney rhyming slang?
Years later, I finally figured out what Major meant back in 2016 when he told me he was a "costermonger" (street hawker) who used to "fly-pitch" (sell stuff without a license) on the "frog and toad" where we did our interview.
In Cockney rhyming slang, "frog and toad" means road. "Porky pies" means lies. "Apples and pears" means stairs. "Whistle and flute" means suit. "Ruby Murray" means curry. The vocabulary is extensive, and bewildering to outsiders — which is precisely the point. Green, the Cockney expert, says this type of slang likely originated as a code to confuse the police, or to secretly rig prices among street vendors.
To complicate things, Major also spoke in what he called "backspeak," sometimes also called backslang, which is even more confusing. One example that's crept into mainstream British slang is the word "yob" for boy. Take any word at all, and simply spell it backwards.
Bidding "lleweraf" to a pearly legend
One of the only parts of that 2016 interview I could understand at the time was when Major waxed poetic about his family's unique pearly suit pattern. He pointed to a row of buttons on his sleeve, calling them "the line of life."
Ten years later, at his funeral, I found myself examining the same pattern on a pearly outfit worn by his great-granddaughter.
"There's a straight line, which is your life line," Aleisha Gordon, 19, said, pointing to a row of shimmering buttons. "The triangles are the ups and downs in life, and the flowers are the friends and family that help you along the way."
After the funeral, children threw handfuls of earth as George Major's coffin was lowered into the ground. The undertaker brought out four caged doves for Major's descendants to release skyward. The birds circled twice overhead, then disappeared.
People shared anecdotes about a "real rascal" and "the most hilarious person" who was nevertheless "very particular" about who made his tea. Someone turned on a boombox, and mourners began kicking their legs like the can-can, singing along to 1950s songs.
They paraded out of the cemetery toward a nearby nuclear sub — what Cockneys call the pub — for a cool pint of pig's ear, or King Lear.
At least that's what the Pearly King of Peckham would have called it. Now I finally understand.

The Men’s ODI World Cup is set to adopt a new format of competition.
The 14-team tournament will retain the same number of participating teams but adopt a four-stage format.
The International Cricket Council has said that the revamped structure is designed to ensure greater consequence from the opening match and a stronger competitive narrative throughout the tournament.
- Pre-tournament: CWC Qualifiers
This is where the eight qualified teams, four from League 2 and four from the Qualifier Play-offs, meet the two lowest-ranked non-host full-member nations, Ireland and West Indies in this edition.
The 10 teams will compete in a tournament, with the top four eventually securing spots at the World Cup. The top-ranked team will advance directly to the second round, while the other three will play a single round-robin Super Series, with the winner joining them in the second round.
- Super Series - stage one of the main event
This Super Series will get the tournament officially underway from October 2. The Three-time Super Series will be held in Windhoek and will decide the final Group Stage team. This has been a contentious development with Associate Members making their displeasure known.
- Group stage
The main group stage will be played in a round-robin format with the top three teams from each group and the next best-ranked side progressing to a seven-team super 7 stage.
- Super 7 stage
Seven teams that have made this stage will play a round-robin phase from which the top four teams will qualify for the semifinals.
- Semifinal and Final
The top four teams after the Super 7 phase progress to the semi-finals. The team finishing top of the Super 7 standings will face fourth, with the second and third-placed teams going head-to-head.
The first Semifinal will be held on 17 November in Cape Town and 18 November in Tshwane. Both semifinals will have a reserve day.
The Final will take place on 21 November in Johannesburg, with a reserve day on 22 November if necessary.

ixigo backed e-intercity bus operator Fresh Bus reported a 2.4X jump in its FY26 operating revenue to ₹63.5 Cr from ₹26.3 Cr as it expanded its electric fleet and route network. The startup’s top line grew on the back of a rapid expansion of its bus fleet and routes, founder and CEO Sudhakar Reddy Chirra told Inc42. The expansion also led to the startup’s bottom line for the fiscal swelling 33% to ₹43.6 Cr from ₹32.8 Cr loss incurred in the previous fiscal. The startup’s bottom line was weighed down by a sharp increase in expenditure over the fiscal. Its total expenses rose 81.4% YoY to ₹107.2 Cr from ₹59.1 Cr in the year-ago period. The jump in expenses in FY26 was primarily linked to the expansion of the fleet, according to Chirra. Lease costs rise with the number of buses, while maintenance, captain salaries, tolls and distribution expenses increase as operations scale, he said. Fresh Bus’ Growth Plans The startup is now targeting a revenue of ₹180 Cr in revenue in FY27, while reducing its loss to around ₹25 Cr-₹30 Cr, Chirra said. Chirra claims that the startup became contribution-margin positive in March 2026, with a current contribution margin of 15%-17%, according to Chirra. He expects Fresh Bus to turn profitable around April-June 2027. The startup is looking to improve its bottom line by reducing up to 30% of its costs by doubling down on larger bus fleets. This will benefit increasing fare rates as well customer stickiness, the founder believes. Founded in 2019, Fresh Bus operates electric buses on intercity routes. It leases buses from fleet providers including Vertelo and Drivn and offers users a digital platform to search for and book tickets. The startup claims to have completed 25 Lakh journeys for 9 Lakh passengers. At the end of the fiscal year, Fresh Bus operated 100 e-buses across 10 routes, primarily in South India. It intends to double this number to 200 by the end of FY27 and broaden its route options to 16. Beyond FY27, Fresh Bus plans to reach 500 buses by March 2028, initially focusing on southern India before expanding westward and then into the north. It expects to reach 1,000 buses across the three regions by March 2029. The startup currently operates at 85-90% occupancy, with around 1.6-1.7 Lakh seats offered each month, Chirra said. Established routes such as Bengaluru-Tirupati, Bengaluru-Chennai and Hyderabad-Vijayawada have repeat ratios of more than 55%. Moving forth, the startup is planning to deepen its presence in southern India, with routes including Chennai-Madurai, Chennai-Tanjavur, Chennai-Trichy, Bengaluru-Trichy, Bengaluru-Madurai and Bengaluru-Tanjavur planned by March. In August, Fresh Bus and ChargeZone expanded their partnership to support 400 additional electric buses, taking the fleet supported by ChargeZone's charging network to 500 buses. ChargeZone will add 30 MW of charging capacity to the 10 MW already dedicated to Fresh Bus. The expanded network is expected to connect 20 cities and 17 additional towns across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana over the next 15 months Fresh Bus had last raised ₹87.5 Cr in Series A funding in August 2024, with participation from Maniv Mobility, Shell Ventures, Alteria Capital and Riverwalk Holdings. The company had said the capital would be used to add 150 electric buses and expand its route network. In August 2026, ixigo agreed to sell a 17.39% stake in Fresh Bus to Twelve Stone LLP for ₹36.6 Cr. Moreover, it recognised a ₹11.22 Cr share of loss from Fresh Bus in FY26.

The Kindle will turn 20 in 2027. Amazon says it plans to celebrate the milestone throughout the year, but to kick things off, it's starting with an entirely refreshed Kindle lineup.
On Thursday, the company introduced a handful of new Kindle models: a new 6-inch base Kindle, a 7-inch Kindle Paperwhite, and a 7-inch Kindle Colorsoft. You can buy Signature Editions of the latter two and Kids versions of the entire range, which include artist-designed kids cases, a year of Amazon's worry-free guarantee for damage, and a year of Kids+, the company's subscription service that offers unlimited access to ad-free, child-appropriate books.
The highlight is Amazon's use of aluminum for the Kindle's construction rather than traditional plastic. The starting tier is plastic, but you can upgrade to an all-aluminum model (Amazon uses 80 percent recycled aluminum) if you prefer that Kindle model and you just want something more robust.
It can get a little confusing with all the different SKUs, so here's a quick rundown:
Lighter and Premium
The base Kindle, the aluminum version, and the Kids Kindle are on sale starting today. The Paperwhite and Colorsoft are available for preorder on a rolling basis and will launch at the end of October.
The base Kindle's screen offers 30 percent faster page turns than its predecessor, Amazon says. The build is a whole millimeter thinner at 6.8 mm, and Amazon cut the weight by around 18 grams to 140 grams. The Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft are both similarly lighter (204 grams) and thinner (6.8 mm), retain the waterproof design, and feature adjustable warm reading lights. The screen refreshes 30 percent faster than the base Kindle, and the screen has a higher pixel density that makes text appear sharper.
Upgrading to the Signature Edition for both nets you the aluminum build, an ambient light sensor that adjusts brightness automatically, an accelerometer that lets you turn the screen to landscape orientation and have the pages adjust accordingly. The upgrade also adds the ability to use a double-tap gesture to turn pages.
Uniquely, the Signature Editions feature pogo pins that let you charge via Amazon's new $60 dock, which props the device up as it charges. There's also a new Page-Turn Cover ($80)—a case with physical page-turn buttons that magnetically attaches to the back of the devices and pairs via the pogo pins, which Amazon says offers page-turn buttons to the vocal minority that still loves them (around 5 percent of Kindle users) without adding unnecessary bulk to the device.
Don't worry, you don't need the case, the Signature Edition, or even a new Kindle if you just want page-turn buttons. Amazon is debuting its own Kindle Click, a $35 page-turn accessory that pairs over Bluetooth for the non-Signature (and older) Kindle models.
Kindle Ablaze
The Kindle business is booming. Amazon's Kevin Keith, vice president of product, says Kindles have seen double-digit growth over the last three years, with 2025 being the highest sales year in more than a decade. He says 60 to 65 percent of people buying new devices have never had a Kindle before, with Gen Z, millennials, and even Gen Alpha driving the lion's share. This past January saw the highest single-month Kindle reading volume in history.
At the same time, Kindles are more expensive than ever. “Memory pricing is a little bit crazy,” Keith says, referring to the memory shortage behind the general price bump on all electronics. Amazon upped prices of existing Kindles earlier this year; the new devices match those prices.
Part of the redesign aims to lower overall manufacturing costs and standardize the hardware. Take the refreshed display on the base Kindle—Keith says many of the improvements trickle down from the development of the Kindle Scribe. For the first time, the base Kindle has a display that sits flush with the body, just like its pricier counterparts. (It previously had a raised plastic bezel around the screen.) That whole front panel is also available in a new color: Ube (purple).
While Amazon has made Kindles with colorful fronts (like the matcha green Kindle from 2024), it hasn't done this with flush displays. That's because simply coloring the front would make the Ube color, for example, scatter around the screen as the frontlight reflects it, casting a purple hue on the display. To counter this, Keith says Amazon developed a new “edge-to-edge” color technology that prints two different colors under the cover lens: the Ube color backed by a layer of black. The black absorbs the light, which solves the problem. Amazon says it perfected this tech in the Scribe and ported it down here.
Color is important. Keith says alternative colors typically make up just 15 to 20 percent of sales—the rest being classic options like black or white—but the matcha green model captured a surprising 55 percent. Amazon also chose that color because, at the time, it noticed a general increase in the popularity of matcha in drinks and sweets (it also noted that folks on #BookTok are reading in coffee shops). Hence the new ube color, which is based on the popular purple yam of the same name.
“We've been tracking food trends, and two years ago, ube just exploded—ube was growing 200 percent year over year,” says Chris Green, Amazon's vice president of design. “We expect it to do far better than the matcha.”
For the aluminum housing, instead of milling the device's frame from a block of aluminum and using a lot of water in the process, Amazon stamps a flat sheet, which then goes into a forge that presses down to create the backplate and sides. The process supposedly takes seconds compared to the hours it can take to machine a single aluminum device frame (like an iPhone or MacBook) saving material and energy. It helps lower the Kindle's carbon footprint, which is now equivalent to 11 hardcover books.
Green says these improvements bring down the device's density. The density of the average human body is around 1 gram per cubic centimeter; an iPhone is around 2.2 grams per cubic centimeter. The new Kindles are around 1.2 grams. Lowering that number can help make the hardware “disappear” during prolonged use.
“I truly want people to never think about the Kindle,” Green says. “I just want them to think about the magical world that the author has created inside of this device.”
For Green, who has designed nearly all of Amazon's hardware in his 19-year tenure at the company (and yes, he says he's embarrassed by the Fire Phone), chasing that 1.2-grams-per-cubic-centimeter target is all about getting the gadget out of the way so the Kindle can mimic the analog calm of physical print.
“More people are reading on paper, more people are reading on Kindles,” Green says. “Is it a backlash to AI? Probably. People are trying to find things more authentic—we're in a crisis of authenticity.” Surveys have shown that overall leisure reading is down across the US, but the people who are reading are buying more than ever.
As for the 20th anniversary of the Kindle in 2027, Keith says the company may roll out a significant refresh to the Kindle's user interface, though he didn't share more. Expect special anniversary editions of some Kindles. When I asked whether we could expect the return of the Kindle Oasis—an asymmetrical e-reader with physical page-turn buttons—Green chuckles.
“The first Oasis was one of my passion projects,” he says. “I loved that. I really, really loved that product. But I was a vocal minority on that—most of the people wanted slabs.”
So, probably not.

Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
- Published
Vladimir Putin has said Russia will use all weapons at his disposal if it considers its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad to have come under direct attack.
The Russian president insisted that Moscow was "not threatening anyone" and merely responding to statements by Western leaders that it was preparing for war in 2029 or 2030.
Throughout this week, Russia has accused Nato of preparing to blockade its territory, which borders Lithuania and Poland, warning that it would even be prepared to use nuclear weapons if the West tried to cut off Kaliningrad from the rest of Russia.
Nato has sought to calm the situation, stressing that it was a defensive alliance and urging Moscow to stop its "nuclear threats".
Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months.
Last week alone, Poland said a Russian helicopter had strayed into its territory adjacent to Kaliningrad and Lithuania said its population felt "constantly threatened" by Russia, in part because of drones entering the nation's airspace.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes.
In a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum, Putin told his audience that he believed that international conflicts were highly likely to continue, but would get better as "Western hegemony" weakened.
Although the Russian leader himself began the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, he again blamed the West for provoking the invasion, arguing that Moscow had simply been forced to defend itself and take up arms.
He also insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea.
"Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," he said.
Putin admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war.
Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since the war in Ukraine started in 2022. Other civilian infrastructure is also regularly hit, with a key bridge in Kyiv attacked by drones on Thursday.
Putin also accused the West of instigating other conflicts.
"If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation, in this case we are talking about Kaliningrad but possibly some other territories, of course the issue of use by the Russian Federation of all arms at the disposal of our country will inevitably and immediately be on the agenda," he said.
He accused Nato of holding naval manoeuvres in the Baltic Sea that he argued represented serious threats to Kaliningrad. If the territory came under Western blockade, he said Russia would be prepared to use all means and forces, including nuclear.
"We are not threatening anyone. We do not intend to attack anyone in 2029, in 2030, in 2050. But if we come across an aggression we will have to respond. Citizens of European countries should be fully aware of that."
He added that while he was aware of the nuclear capabilities of countries such as the UK and France, the weapons at its disposal were unparalleled.
Western officials have long feared that, rather than invading Kaliningrad, Russia would use the relatively small distance between the exclave and ally Belarus - known as the Suwalki Gap - were it to attempt to seize Lithuanian territory by force.
Lithuania's prime minister told the BBC last week that his country had made evacuation plans in case Russia invaded and thousands of Nato troops are stationed there.
Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte made clear on Wednesday that none of the alliance's "exercises or activities" posed any threat to Moscow and that the Kremlin's messaging was "absolutely not called for and not helpful".
Putin spent some time talking about leading countries in the world having armaments at their disposal that could "swipe away all life or at least push the Earth to catastrophic consequences", and said that unfortunately no-one could be sure they would never be used.
He drew the analogy of a gun sitting on a theatre stage - if it was hanging there at the start of the show, it would certainly be fired at the end.
He appeared to call for the rules of warfare to be rewritten and warned of the increasing risk of artificial intelligence.
"The automation and digitalisation of warfare leads to its gamification. This leads to degradation and sliding back of humanity to barbarity," he said.

Egyptian authorities arrest entire editorial team of independent media site
Egyptian authorities have accused six journalists of belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood
NEW YORK -- Egyptian authorities on Thursday accused six journalists detained this week of membership in the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood, saying they produced fabricated news for an online outlet in exchange for funding from abroad.
The arrests swept up the entire editorial team of Matsadaash, Arabic for “Don't Believe,” one of Egypt’s few independent outlets, which started eight years ago as a fact-checking platform and has since expanded into investigative reporting in Egypt and other Arab countries.
“The claims are false,” said Abdelrahman Mansour, one of the founders of Matsadaash. He noted that after two of its editors were arrested in 2023, State Security investigators found no affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. The editors were released after 36 hours and never charged.
“It's very difficult for us to understand why this is happening,” he said.
Egypt is among the world’s worst jailers of journalists, according to the US-based Committee to Protect Journalists. The Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights says 26 journalists are now behind bars in Egypt.
Matsadaash, founded in 2018 as an online platform, has gained credibility and a large following in Egypt, where independent media are stifled and government censorship and oversight over newspapers and TV networks are the norm. The Matsadaash website is blocked in Egypt, but its Facebook page has more than one million followers.
Over 80 international and regional rights groups, civil society organizations and independent media called on the Egyptian authorities to release the journalists, condemning what they called an escalating crackdown on independent media.
“Matsadaash has operated openly for years and has built a reputation for credible and accurate reporting on a range of public interest issues across Egypt,” the petition, signed by groups including Human Rights Watch and Reporters Without Borders, said. “Egyptian authorities’ failure to allow free exercises of expression to thrive flies in the face of a purported commitment to dialogue, transparency, anti-corruption, and regional leadership.”
In a statement Thursday, Egypt’s Interior Ministry described Matsadaash as an unlicensed page managed from abroad by a “fugitive Brotherhood member” it identified as Mansour.
It said the six detained were part of a Brotherhood “media committee” that prepared false and fabricated news for Mansour to publish. Only one of the six is a member of the Journalists’ Syndicate, the statement said. It said legal measures have been taken but did not specify charges.
Accusing critics of membership in the Brotherhood is common in Egypt, which designated the group as a terrorist organization in 2013, after the military ousted then-President Mohammed Morsi, a senior Brotherhood figure. Since then, authorities have frequently accused journalists and critics of belonging to the group or spreading false news.
The first arrest occurred Monday about 9 p.m. when authorities went to the home of Abdallah Qadry, Mansour said. The other five members of staff were arrested Tuesday, starting with Mohamed Abu Emaira, who was taken from his home about 1 a.m. According to Mansour, Emaira’s library and internet router were destroyed during the arrest.
Omar Helal was arrested in Port Said and Islam Barakat in Gharbia Governorate. Two other members of Matsadaash’s newsroom, Mohamed Mahmoud and Mohamed Adel, were arrested in Cairo.
All had their cellphones and computers confiscated.
The Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, a prominent advocacy group, said the whereabouts of all six remain unknown.
“They have not been allowed to contact their families or legal team,” EIPR said, adding that it was the first time an entire newsroom had been arrested in Egypt.

Trump gets back at Ken Paxton after he criticized GOP convention calling struggling Senate hopeful a ‘pain in the a**’
Trump has repeatedly insulted Paxton, spending both days of his GOP convention complaining about his fashion sense
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article

Donald Trump has thrown a jab at Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton after the struggling Senate hopeful criticized the Republican midterm convention that the president headlined last month.
Trump went to a truck factory in Denton, Texas, Thursday to tout the administration’s work on American manufacturing. But, like in previous speeches, he couldn’t help but insult Paxton in the process.
"He can be a pain in the ass sometimes, I'll be honest,” the president said about the Republican nominee whom he endorsed.
Trump then looked to his left and asked: “Is he here, by the way? Oh, there he is. Good. I didn't even know if he was here! I don't care."
Trump’s comments come a day after Paxton was reportedly caught slamming the Dallas convention that the president used to drum up support for Republican candidates in tight races.
“To be honest with you, the numbers — when we did that convention — it dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped. Right now, yeah, not good,” Paxton said during a private Washington fundraiser, according to an audio recording obtained by The New York Times.
Paxton and his Democratic opponent James Talarico are neck and neck in the polls.
Talarico was two percentage points ahead of Paxton in a Fox News poll released Thursday, with 51 percent of voter support compared to Paxton’s 49 percent.
The Democrat had an even larger lead over Paxton in a Marist University poll conducted from September 17 to 20. In that poll, 50 percent of Texas voters said they support Talarico and 44 percent said they back Paxton.
Talarico was leading Paxton by three percentage points before the convention.
A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll released on August 24 found Talarico with 42 percent of voter support compared to Paxton’s 39 percent.
Paxton’s senior adviser Nick Maddux disputed the reporting on Paxton's private conversation with donors, telling the Times, “This is more manipulated nonsense from The New York Times to create a story that doesn’t exist.”
“Our latest poll from the last week has Ken Paxton leading by three points, and every serious pollster will tell you that our numbers have improved since early September.”
During both nights of the GOP convention, Trump insulted Paxton over his fashion sense.
“And I said something yesterday, and I don't know if he'll ever talk to me again…My people said, ‘Please don't say that.’ So I won't say it, but I'll tell you what I was thinking about saying,” Trump said during his closing address on September 10.
“I said, ‘I don't like the way Ken dresses,” the president said. “Although I also said he looked really sharp in that suit yesterday. I thought it was spiffy.”
The night before, Trump told the crowd that Paxton “may not be the best-looking guy I've ever seen, but you know what he is? He's the greatest Attorney General in America, and he deserves to be your next senator.”

Minecraft Dungeons 2 has plenty of secrets hidden away from the main path, and some of the most valuable ones are the secret Talismans. To find these hidden collectibles, you must explore the Overworld and the Sift extensively, and not just by checking out the important points of interest on the map. So, check this guide to learn all about the locations of all Minecraft Dungeons 2 secrets and how to get them.
List of All Secret Talismans in Minecraft Dungeons 2
The Secret Talismans are spread across different regions and dungeon types. While some can be found in fixed locations and chests, others require you to defeat specific bosses or enemies in Minecraft Dungeons 2. So, here’s a brief overview of the Minecraft Dungeons 2 secret Talismans and their locations:
| Talisman | Location | 
|---|---|
| Amethyst Lens | Howling Woods | 
| Emerald of Good Fortune | Lullaby Hills | 
| Glowstone Flask | Overworld Dungeons | 
| Lucky Clover | Frozen Highlands | 
| Medallion of Momentum | Humbler Husklands | 
| Ocelot’s Paw | Overworld Rifts | 
| Soul Chip | Sift Dungeons | 
| Thrifty Pendant | Rainy Plains | 
| Wonderful Wheat | Mosstrosity secret boss | 
Amethyst Lens
The Amethyst Lens is hidden in the Howling Woods, the second location you will unlock in the Overworld. As you begin at the Hidden Grove fast travel minecart station, head down from the waterfall and go past it. Then climb up the hilly area to reach the platforming section.
Jump on the platforms to reach a higher level, and then turn left to head inside a secret area, where you will find the chests containing the Amethyst Lens.
With this Talisman equipped, you’ll be able to deal more damage with your Ranged attacks.
Emerald of Good Fortune
Obtaining the Emerald of Good Fortune secret talisman requires you to travel to the Sift dimension in Minecraft Dungeons 2. First, reach the Lullaby Hilltop checkpoint, head to the right direction, and then go straight. At the end of the path, you will find a series of bridges to your left.
Carefully jump on these bridges to reach the bottom, where you will be ambushed by a group of Illagers. Clear the Ambush and open the secret chest to obtain the Emerald of Good Fortune.
Glowstone Flask
The Glowstone Flask is a special Talisman in Minecraft Dungeons 2 due to its random acquisition method. It can be found in a random dungeon of the Overworld region; however, that dungeon should have a 4-brazier layout.
Keep clearing the dungeons, looking for such a layout, and once you find that, extinguish the 4 lit braziers to expose a hidden chest containing the secret Glowstone Flash Talisman.
The Glowstone Flask can reduce the potion cooldown speed drastically, helping you efficiently heal in Minecraft Dungeons 2.
Lucky Clover
This Minecraft Dungeons 2 secret has a tiny puzzle associated with it. Visit the Frozen Fortress checkpoint in the Frozen Highlands. Head to the Library Towers here, and then climb the stairs to reach the top of the bridge, which has a broken railing around its center.
Jump down, and walk to the left direction to find a small catapult that will launch you onto an elevated platform. Here, you will find the secret chest that contains the Lucky Clover Talisman.
The Lucky Clover grants a bonus 2% chance to get additional loot drops while defeating enemies.
Medallion of Momentum
The Medallion of Momentum is hidden in the Humbler Huskland, a region in The Sift on the Minecraft Dungeons 2 map. Arrive at the Echo Den fast travel station and keep heading all the way up. Once you reach the entrance of a dungeon, walk to the left to uncover a secret path.
Now, head inside and proceed forward to find a bridge containing a bunch of chests at its endpoint. Open the last chest to find the Medallion of Momentum secret Talisman in Minecraft Dungeons 2.
The Medallion of Momentum is among the few passives that allow you to move fast in the game. Equipping it will speed up your movement speed by 10% when you’re in motion for more than 3 seconds.
Ocelot’s Paw
Similar to the Glowstone Flask, this Minecraft Dungeons 2 secret has a random acquisition method. You must head inside the Rifts of the Overworld and find an interactable wall in the Sift dimension.
Interacting with the wall will expose a hidden pocket that contains the secret chest with the Ocelot’s Paw Talisman. The Ocelot’s Paw provides a bonus damage boost to all of your jump attacks in the game. Yes, jumping is a new mechanic in the sequel, along with more gameplay features you can find in the Minecraft Dungeons 2 beginner’s guide.
Soul Chip
Again, the Soul Chip follows a method similar to the Glowstone Flask and the Ocelot’s Paw. For this, you must head inside a dungeon from the Sift dimension. The particular layout you’re looking for is the one with bouncing platforms.
Once you find it, walk on top of the platform to bounce on it and reach an enclosed area full of enemies in Minecraft Dungeons 2. Defeat each of them to reveal a hidden chest that contains the Soul Chip Talisman.
Thrifty Pendant
Travel to the Rainy Plains location and reach the White Tower fast travel checkpoint. From there, keep heading up until you reach a broad river. Now, keep jumping on the vanishing platforms to reach an open beach where the secret chest will be located.
Open the secret chest to find the Thrifty Pendant in the game. With this equipped, you can have a 25% damage boost based on the number of emeralds you have. It pairs up perfectly with most of the weapons in Minecraft Dungeons 2.
Wonderful Wheat
Once you’ve collected all eight Minecraft Dungeons 2 secrets, you gain access to a secret door in the Overworld. Enter this area to complete a boss fight, and then you’ll be able to obtain the Wonderful Wheat Talisman.
After unlocking the secret Talismans, head to the Hidden Grove checkpoint and keep moving up along the river to find the entrance to the secret dungeon. This area will be located at the very end of the map, above the spider dungeons.
Once you enter inside, you’ll encounter the Mosstrosity boss. Defeat it to obtain the last Minecraft Dungeons 2 secret Talisman.
And that completes the list of all Minecraft Dungeons 2 secrets you can obtain, along with their effects and uses. So, how many of these have you collected yet? Let us know in the comments below

After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky is leaving the company. Roslansky, who until recently was the CEO of LinkedIn, was promoted to the head of Office last year and then took control of Microsoft Teams earlier this year. Roslansky’s departure has triggered another leadership shuffle inside Microsoft.
Microsoft’s Office and Teams chief is leaving
Ryan Roslansky is leaving after nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft.
“Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position,” says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella in an internal memo. “Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible.”
Roslansky is leaving a week after Microsoft announced its new Copilot, which the company is positioning as “the OS for work.” He’s also leaving around a month after calling fully AI-generated documents “a doom loop” for workers. “If we’re not careful, we’ll end up with a very expensive way to avoid writing and reading in an ocean of sameness, genericness,” said Roslansky in his LinkedIn post.
Microsoft is now moving the teams behind Office and Microsoft Teams over to Charles Lamanna, as part of the Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) organization. This is the second major reshuffling of the Office teams after Rajesh Jha, former head of Microsoft’s experiences and devices group, retired from Microsoft earlier this year.
Microsoft’s chief design officer, Jon Friedman, is also moving to report to Copilot chief Jacob Andreou. Microsoft appointed Dan Shapero as its LinkedIn CEO earlier this year, and he will continue in this role and report directly to Nadella.
Roslansky describes the decision to leave Microsoft as a hard one in his own memo to his teams, and reveals he wasn’t willing to move to Microsoft’s Redmond headquarters full time. “I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day,” says Roslansky. “But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area.”
Here’s Roslansky’s memo in full:
Team,
In 1996, as a college freshman, I taught myself to code so a few friends and I could help other students find a place to live around campus. I didn’t know much. I did know the internet was about to change how people found things, and I wanted to be as close to that as possible.
In 2009, Jeff Weiner made me his first hire at LinkedIn. I’ve spent the nearly 18 years since working on a much bigger version of that same idea: helping people find opportunity, and then helping them do great work once they have it.
This has (obviously) been the best professional experience of my life.
As a product manager, I got to build dozens of features that are still around today (some good, some not so good!). When I became CEO in 2020, the world was months into a pandemic that changed what work even meant. Nobody hands you a playbook for that. This team wrote one anyway. Since then, LinkedIn has passed a billion members and nearly tripled its business, and every bit of that belongs to the people who built it.
Last year, Satya asked me to help build the future of M365. Once again, the old rules didn’t apply. AI was rapidly changing how professionals work, and the world’s largest productivity suite needed to lead the way. That meant figuring out what Copilot, and the future of work, should look like as one ecosystem.
We still have a ways to go, but the progress over the past year has been inspiring to watch. A lot of talented people set aside their own roadmaps to make that happen. Thank you. I know it wasn’t easy.
Satya, thank you. When LinkedIn joined Microsoft, you gave us room to build, and then trusted many of us with a lot more. I’ve learned more from you than I can fit in an email, and I’m grateful for the friendship that came with it.
All of which made this a hard decision. I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day. But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area. My wife Leigh gives her time to more local organizations than I can keep track of. Our youngest daughter just started high school, and our dog Buddy remains deeply committed to the trails on the Peninsula!
I thought about this for a long time. It’s the right call. The work now goes to leaders who are set up to take it further. I can’t wait to see what they do with it.
Over the years, people have asked me what’s kept me so energized and motivated in this work. I think the answer is that I got to spend my career working where doing good and doing well are the same thing. In technology, that’s the best place to operate.
Most companies start by focusing on doing well, so doing good becomes a compromise. It’s the last slide of the PowerPoint, or a separate .org. But when doing good is built into the product itself, it becomes a real competitive advantage. When we build valuable products, people find jobs, they hire, they learn skills, they start companies, they run companies. That creates value for members, customers and the world. And for our business too.
Not many companies get to work this way, and not many people get the chance to build something like it. We do.
That matters more now than it ever has. Technology will continue to touch every job on the planet, and the people building it will decide what kind of world it helps create. I can’t think of a better group to figure that out than the people reading this note.
Thank you for the best 18 years I could have asked for.
RR

Punish Man City this season, say other club chiefs
- Published
Manchester City's punishment for breaching Premier League rules should be handed down before the end of this season, senior football figures have told BBC Sport.
The Premier League said on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
They included artificially inflating revenue by more than £900m through "sham" sponsorship deals.
City have repeatedly denied guilt and signalled an intent to lodge an appeal by the end of this week.
There have been fears that the process, which has taken three years since City were charged, could be drawn out for much longer.
However, senior figures within football have told BBC Sport they see no reason why the case cannot be concluded by the end of this season.
Speaking on condition of anonymity, one club official said: "It benefits everyone for this to be resolved as quickly as possible."
When asked if they believed it would be, they said: "Instinctively yes, but it has to be done right.
"We can all see what the risks are if it's not. But those risks have been there throughout the process, as they've won the league multiple times during it."

Another source said the process "should" be resolved by the end of the season, and they hoped any appeal would be "compressed".
The final decision rests in the hands of the independent commission, with the Premier League board - and City - able to suggest a suitable punishment before the panel makes its decision.
There is increasingly a desire to have the case resolved by the end of the season amid fears that allowing City to get to the end of the campaign without punishment could lead to uncertainty and farce, particularly if they were to win the title.
One section of the Premier League regulations says an appeal should conclude no more than 12 weeks after it is filed, and a decision should be made within 30 days of its end.
Procedures can be hurried to meet certain deadlines, like the end of a league season.
However, Ferran Soriano, the club's chief executive, has suggested the case will run for a long time.
Manchester City cannot make a further appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), but could potentially claim the process was not impartial at the High Court.
The Premier League's statement, formally announcing the guilty verdicts read on Monday, said it wants the process to be "concluded as soon as possible".
City sponsor Etihad considers legal action
Meanwhile, City club sponsor Etihad Airways said it is considering legal action against the Premier League.
In a statement issued on Wednesday, the United Arab Emirates-based airline said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".
It added: "The Premier League's public communication of the commission's findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings."
Etihad, City's main sponsor since 2009, also said it was given no opportunity to engage in a process that now reflects "adversely on the airline".
The statement added: "Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly.
"The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision.
"The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.
"Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests."
The Premier League declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

National Conference leader and MLA Uri Dr Sajad Shafi Tuesday said the government must hand over the defunct Salamabad Trade Facilitation Centre to local stakeholders for promotion of tourism.
Talking to Greater Kashmir outside the Legislative Assembly, Dr Sajad Shafi said the infrastructure at Salamabad has been lying unused since LoC trade was suspended several years ago.
“I requested the Chief Minister to hand over the tourism (facility) to us so that we can utilise it. Our local people can benefit from it,” he said.
The MLA said the trade centre was a source of livelihood for many local families before its closure.
“When the Salamabad Trade Facilitation Centre was there, many people got employment. Now they are unemployed. When the tourism facilitation centre will be back, unemployment among the youth will be reduced,” Dr Shafi said.
He said a road being built from Gulmarg by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) will touch Uri, opening new tourism circuits in the region.
“We are building a road from Gulmarg which will touch Uri. Tourists will come to Gulmarg. Beyond that, there are beautiful places — they will see our Pandu Temple, Chhatti Padshahi, Baba Rangi Imam, Baba Kazi Nag, Baba Fareed,” he added.
“People are tired of seeing Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Yusmarg, Sonmarg. They must come and explore Uri,” he added.
MLA Dr Sajad Shafi said Uri has two hydroelectric projects, one built by Sweden, which remained functional even during the 2005 earthquake as they are fully underground.
“From a security point of view, it is a border area. Operation Sindoor took place. There were many conflicts. Nothing happened to those powerhouses. That is also something to look at. I want Uri to be brought to the tourism map in a new way,” he said.
MLA Uri further said that the rare Markhor species is found only at the Limber Wildlife Centre in Lashipura. “I want to give a huge boost to tourism,” he said.

Effects of preventive treatment for tuberculosis could start to wane after just one year of completing the antibiotics course in high-burden settings, while the protection lasts for at least eight and 13 years in medium and low-burden countries, a study has found.
Findings published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine show that tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) offered a strong protection during the first 12-24 months across settings with all levels of TB burden.
Consisting of antibiotic medicines that can prevent inactive TB infections from developing into active disease, TPT is considered an important public health tool for protecting individuals and countries from the deadly infectious disease.
Preventive treatment can include medications, such as isoniazid and rifapentine -- typically prescribed for four months -- and is critical for the World Health Organization's goal to end the global TB epidemic by 2035.
TPT has been shown to be highly effective, but how long this protection lasts -- and whether its duration varies by region or community risk level -- remains unclear, researchers at the US' Boston University and the University of California, Berkeley, said.
They estimated TB risk among people with TB infections in 24 countries and found that TPT offered strong initial protection, but long-term protection varied depending on the burden of TB disease in each area.
"Of 4,66,523 participants from 47 studies, we included 84,128 individuals from 44 cohort studies across 24 countries. TPT was highly protective within the first year but declined over the course of follow-up in all settings, with greater effects observed in low-burden and medium-burden settings," the authors wrote.
The results showed that high-burden countries should consider combining TPT with other interventions to achieve the long-term benefits these medications are capable of providing, they said.
Lead author Lauren Linde, an epidemiology doctoral student at Boston University's school of public health, said, "In this study, our results corroborated something that was already well-established -- TPT is highly effective at preventing TB progression among close contacts and people who have been infected with TB."
"However, our finding that the initial effect of TPT declined so rapidly in very high-burden settings strengthens the case for not placing too much emphasis on TPT in isolation from other interventions that address ongoing community transmission," Linde said.

The Jammu and Kashmir government has approved the diversion of 51.501 hectares of forest land for 33 projects in Uri over the 2024-25 to 2026-27 financial years, with 20.9352 hectares allocated for the Srinagar-Baramulla-Uri Road, the Legislative Assembly was informed Tuesday.
The figures were disclosed by the Minister for Forest, Ecology and Environment Department, Javed Ahmad Rana in response to an unstarred question by Uri National Conference MLA Sajjad Shafi, who sought details of forest and agricultural land affected by government and private construction in the constituency.
The Ministry said the projects were cleared under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Abhiniyam and related rules.
These projects include work by the Jal Shakti Department, the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) and the Uri-II Stage-II hydroelectric project.
The government said the diversions were in the public interest and subject to “statutory environmental safeguards, conditions and compensatory measures” to minimise and mitigate their impact.
“Under the applicable provisions, user agencies must provide equivalent non-forest or State forest land for compensatory afforestation,” it said.
If such land is unavailable, the government said afforestation is carried out over twice the diverted area on degraded forest land.
Approved plans provide for 1,000 plants per hectare and 10 years of maintenance.
Depending on the project, agencies must also fund slope stabilisation, muck disposal, wildlife mitigation, Catchment Area Treatment and biodiversity management measures.
The Ministry said compensatory, mitigation and strip plantations have been undertaken near developmental and hydropower projects in Uri through CAPEX and CAMPA schemes, wherever feasible.
The response also lists the Uri-I Stage-II hydropower project and several water-supply schemes in Boniyar and Uri among the projects involving forest-land diversion.
Plantation and compensatory afforestation sites have been identified under approved plans, and the respective user agencies or companies are required to bear the costs, the Ministry said.

‘Someone take him to Disney,’ one social media user wrote after seeing a video of his police escort home

A Louisiana boy who survived a stabbing attack that left four others dead made an emotional return home with a police escort as local authorities dubbed him a “superhero.”
The Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office shared a video on Facebook Tuesday of the boy returning to his home in Houma, about an hour’s drive southwest of New Orleans, from the hospital after being seriously injured in the attack.
The boy, wearing a neck brace and a Spider-Man baseball cap, was seen shaking the hands of cops and saying “thank you” for helping him to safety.
“This young man and his family have endured unimaginable loss,” Terrebonne Parish Sheriff Tim Soignet said in a statement. “Today, we stand beside them as he comes home, and we will continue to stand beside them in the days ahead. To this young survivor: you are not alone. Your community is with you, we are with you!”
Members of the sheriff’s office and Houma Police Department had turned on their flashing lights and sirens to escort the boy, calling it “a welcome home for a ‘superhero.’”
Deputies rushed to Ashland Drive in Houma on September 12 to find the boy with stab wounds. He was airlifted to an “out-of-area” hospital in critical condition, the sheriff’s office said at the time.
As police investigated, they found four others dead inside nearby homes from a series of stabbings. A 47-year-old Houma resident, Kaegan Jude Solet, was later arrested in connection with the stabbings and charged with four counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder.
A neighbor named Dulce recalled the moment the boy ran to her house to get inside and find help as the man accused of stabbing him trailed close behind.
“She saw that the boy went running to the back door,” Dulce’s niece, who translated her aunt’s words into English, told WWL Louisiana.
The man who had followed the boy “had wrapped the kid by his shoulders and pushed him down, then hit him again,” Dulce’s niece said, adding that the boy eventually passed out.
Dulce and her family, who were eating dinner with her when the boy rushed over, called the police.
Solet was identified as a person of interest the same day that the stabbings took place. The next day, the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office confirmed that he was taken into custody.
On September 15, the sheriff’s office said Solet was released from medical care, sent to a local jail and booked on the murder charges.
When sharing the video of the boy returning home from the hospital after his horrific ordeal, the sheriff’s office said, “We ask the community to continue lifting up the victim and his family while respecting their privacy as he recovers.”
One Facebook user said, “Someone take him to Disney.”
“Choked up and crying like a baby. Bless his heart,” another wrote.
A third commented, “What an amazing police force we have, with all the hell that that sweet baby has been through our police officers escort him home and made him feel special.”

20 December 2024 was a crucial moment for Luxembourg in supporting WHO and strengthening global public health, to make progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals in 2025–2028. A Strategic Partnership Framework (SPF) with the Ministry of Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Affairs was signed amounting to €46.5 million – the largest-ever agreement WHO has had with Luxembourg. Furthermore, the first-ever multiyear agreement with the Ministry of Health and Social Safety €1 million was launched, as the country’s first voluntary contribution to WHO.
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General greets with Luxembourg's Martine Deprez, Minister of Health and Social Safety and Xavier Bettel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Cooperation and Foreign Trade. © MAE Luxembourg
“From now till 2028, this contribution will help finance priority areas in Luxembourg’s collaboration with WHO” said Martine Deprez, Minister of Health and Social Safety during the bilateral meeting, “notably for sanitary crisis preparedness and response and the fight against health inequalities, with a special focus on gender.”
The amount of €46.5 million contains fully flexible and thematic funding, and allocations for the Universal Health Coverage Partnership, tropical disease research and polio eradication. The fully flexible funding enables WHO to allocate the money to the areas of highest need.
“By signing two new partnership agreements, we have reaffirmed Luxembourg's continued support for the WHO and its mission,” said Xavier Bettel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Cooperation and Foreign Trade. “This reflects our strong commitment to promoting global health and multilateralism. We launch these agreements with WHO because we believe the best way to avoid is to prevent.”
To support the achievement of WHO’s priorities, the strategic partnership framework with Luxembourg includes support for WHO’s core work to develop, deliver and implement high-quality technical products – the guidelines, norms and standards on which many countries rely.
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, remarked how symbolic it was that the agreements were signed on the International Day of Solidarity. They are “a strong statement of solidarity by Luxembourg, not just with WHO, but with the people of the world”, said Dr Tedros.
Xavier Bettel, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Martine Deprez at the signing ceremony. © MAE Luxembourg
WHO and Luxembourg continue their historical strategic partnership, collaborating to fulfill a shared mission to promote, provide and protect health.

Few things are more frustrating than packet loss or high ping causing in-game lag. It always seems to happen at the worst possible moment, when you’re about to snipe an unsuspecting opponent or screech into a hairpin bend. While there are other potential causes, your substandard router could be doing you dirty. The best gaming routers promise rock solid connections and can usually prioritize game-related traffic to reduce the risk of issues. They also frequently feature fancy designs and customizable lighting to fit your gaming room.
Now, you don’t necessarily need a special gaming router. A good router is a good router, and you’ll find tons of them in my guides to the Best Routers and Best Mesh Systems. You can also get a better connection simply by running an Ethernet cable from your router to your gaming PC. That said, I have tested several gaming routers, and my top pick is the fastest router I have ever tested.

Best Asus Gaming Routers
The brand I recommend as the best for gamers is Asus. The Taiwanese company has a long gaming history and dedicated sub-brands like Republic of Gamers (ROG). It produces fast, highly configurable routers with free security software and many gaming extras. Ports are usually generous, there’s no need for a subscription, and you can combine different Asus routers that support AiMesh into a mesh system to extend your coverage. The potential downsides are the relatively high prices, occasionally buggy firmware, and the need to dig into configuration settings to get the best performance.
Topping my testing charts, the Asus ROG Rapture GT-BE98 Pro is a supremely capable, quad-band Wi-Fi 7 gaming router. In terms of raw speed, this is the best router I have tested to date. That alone makes it feel worthy of the “gimmick” of being designed explicitly for gaming. It is very similar to the RT-BE96U in my regular router guide, but with the ROG model, Asus has added a second 6-GHz band on top of the existing 2.4-GHz, 5-GHz, and 6-GHz bands. This massively increases the available bandwidth, affording you plenty of space for multiple gaming streams, or giving you an extra band for wireless backhaul if you decide to set up a mesh using Asus’ AiMesh connectivity. It also has an extra 10-Gbps LAN port, giving you one 10-Gbps WAN/LAN, two 10-Gbps LAN, four Gigabit LAN, one USB 3.2, and a USB 2.0 port. The USB ports come in handy for NAS devices. You must pay extra for these additions, so if you don’t have multiple gaming streams or a NAS, you can save money with the RT-BE96U and still get great performance.
This is also easily the biggest router I have ever tested at nearly 14 inches across, with eight huge antennas, and it weighs 4.4 pounds. It is far from subtle, won’t blend in, and could prove tricky to place due to its size. Because it’s a gaming router, Asus has included Aura RGB lighting, so you can pick the colored lighting you want and make it a feature.
AiProtection Pro security software and parental controls, powered by Trend Micro, are bundled into the cost. This comprehensive security combo includes a firewall, intrusion prevention, malicious site blocking, automatic updates, and more. Parental controls include scheduling, website filtering by age, and usage stats. You also get VPN support with the option to connect remotely when you are out and about. You can redeem a free year of NordVPN service with this router. Naturally, there are some gaming-focused features, with game acceleration enabling you to prioritize gaming-related traffic through ports and packet analysis. If you have Asus’ ROG gear, it can be prioritized with a click, and Asus includes server acceleration to minimize latency through the third-party WTFast service.
Apart from the size and cost, there isn’t much to complain about here, but it is worth considering that the range on the 6-GHz band is limited and struggles to penetrate through walls, so you will need Wi-Fi 7 devices nearby to take full advantage of this router. Ideally, have it in the same room as your gaming PC or laptop. This router was originally touted to get Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) support, but it never did (look at the next pick if that’s something you want).
Asus ROG Strix GS-BE12000 for $400: If you don’t want to spend as much, but you’re set on a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router, and you want lots of ports, this model could make sense. I found it stable and seriously speedy on the 6-GHz and 5-GHz bands. It boasts 320 MHz channels on the 6-GHz band, Multi-Link Operation (MLO), and 4K-QAM (read my How to Buy a Router and Wi-Fi 7 guides for a breakdown on these terms). It has a 2.5 Gbps WAN and seven 2.5 Gbps LAN ports, two of which are dedicated gaming ports, and a USB 3.2 Gen 1 port. You get mostly the same excellent software and gaming options as my top pick. This is a scaled down version of the BE18000 ($530), and has 2 x 2 MIMO on the 6-GHz band instead of 4 x 4, but I think it’s a better buy for most folks, especially if you see it on sale. It’s worth noting that both models have official Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) support, which extends the range of the 6-GHz band to make it more comparable to the 5-GHz band range. I can’t test this here in the UK, as it’s only available in North America and requires your precise real-world location so local regulators can authorize it.
Asus TUF Gaming BE9400 for $265: The cheaper end of Asus gaming routers, this model is still a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router, and it doesn’t make too many compromises. It has one 2.5 Gbps WAN, three 2.5 Gbps LAN ports, and a USB 3.2 Gen 1 port. You miss out on some ROG-exclusive gaming features, the design is not as nice, and it lacks RGB lighting. But this router performed far better than the price would suggest, keeping pace with my top pick at close range, though coverage doesn’t extend as far.
Asus ROG Rapture GT6 (2-Pack) for $350: This Wi-Fi 6 system is a solid gaming mesh. Aside from the look, Asus touts game modes that boost performance and prioritize related traffic. My 2-pack of black routers (they come in white too) was simple to set up, and each sports a 2.5-Gbps WAN port, three Gigabit LAN ports, and a USB 3.2 Gen 1 port. The tri-band Asus ROG Rapture GT6 finished in the top half of the table in most tests. It has a single 2.4-GHz band and two 5-GHz bands (one is used for backhaul unless you connect the routers with an Ethernet cable). While the 2.4-GHz band performance was very good, the 5-GHz results were among the best I have recorded, and this system supports the wider 160-MHz channels and WPA3 for security. You also get AiProtection security software and comprehensive parental controls free for the lifetime of the product. The GT6 has VPN support, too, and you can use it as a VPN server when you are out. If your gaming rig doesn’t have Wi-Fi 7 yet and you need a mesh system for your home, this is worth a look.
Best TP-Link Gaming Routers
You can sometimes get a little more for your money with TP-Link, and it offers a dedicated gaming line-up under the Archer brand (prefaced with GE), but I don’t think they always offer the best value for performance compared to its regular Archer routers. Folks in the US may also hesitate because TP-Link has not yet secured a Conditional Approval from the FCC’s router ban (Asus and Netgear have). All routers that were already on sale (including everything here) are unaffected by the ban and software updates have a waiver at least until January 1, 2029. There’s a slim risk the waiver doesn’t get extended, but it’s unlikely (read my guide for more information).
This stunning tri-band Wi-Fi 7 gaming router features an angled design with customizable RGB lighting that screams Vader’s castle but also provides room for antennas to ensure extremely fast performance across the board. You also get a 10-Gbps port for your incoming internet connection, a further two 10-Gbps and four 2.5-Gbps Ethernet LAN ports, and a USB 3.0 port. The Tether app is solid, with some gaming-specific options, but separate subscriptions are required for extra security and parental controls. Despite the blazing fast results, the GE800 couldn’t quite match my top Wi-Fi 7 gaming pick above on the 6-GHz band, and it produced quite a lot of heat and audible fan noise. The upside is that it’s significantly cheaper.
TP-Link Archer GE400 (BE6500) for $220: This dual-band Wi-Fi 7 gaming router is a solid performer. At close range on the 5-GHz band, it can go toe-to-toe with most of the best routers. It also offers dedicated gaming features, though some of them require subscriptions. I was disappointed by the limited range, and the comparable TP-Link Archer BE400 (BE6500) ($180) is currently on sale for less. You also don’t have to spend much more to get the far superior, tri-band Archer BE600 (BE9700) ($250), giving you the full 6-GHz Wi-Fi 7 experience. For gamers who live alone in apartments or small homes, this router could still be a decent buy.
Other Gaming Routers I’ve Tested and Liked
Netgear used to manufacture dedicated gaming routers under the Nighthawk brand, but the latest Nighthawk routers are billed more as mainstream products (you’ll find a few in my Best Routers guide).
Netgear Nighthawk RAXE300 for $285: This Wi-Fi 6E gaming router has a curvy spaceship design in matte black with wings containing antennas for a strong signal throughout your home. The Nighthawk RAXE300 is a tri-band router with 2.4-GHz, 5-GHz, and 6-GHz bands. It served seamless, speedy Wi-Fi during two weeks of testing, with no issues handling a mix of four simultaneous gaming and video streams. A single 2.5-Gbps WAN/LAN port, five gigabit LAN ports, and a USB-C 3.0 port will be enough for most folks.
The Nighthawk app is excellent and offers band splitting, guest network options, and a host of analytical tools. While both the Premium Smart Parental Controls ($8/month or $70/year) and Netgear Armor ($100/year) are slick, the extra expense is hard to swallow when many competitors offer cheaper or free alternatives with similar features. This is discontinued, but a few places still have new stock, and it’s still a great router.
Gaming Routers I Don’t Recommend
Here are a couple of gaming routers I tested that I don’t recommend.
Acer Predator Connect T7: Another brand with gaming pedigree, I had high hopes for this Acer system, but my excitement was short-lived because the half-baked Predator Connect T7 is a mess. Buggy installation, with the firmware update repeatedly failing, followed by flaky performance with frequent dropouts, made testing this system a frustrating experience. The band steering is poor and frequently dumped me onto the slowest 2.4-GHz band. The T7 also dropped my connection multiple times a day, froze video calls, and was a general pain.
MSI RadiX AXE6600: This Wi-Fi 6E tri-band gaming router has that familiar red and black Sith spider look, though you can customize the lighting. It proved very fast in most of my tests, coming close to the top of the table at short range on the 6-GHz band and offering average performance on the 5-GHz and 2.4-GHz bands. But the mobile app had limited options, a confusing layout, and was buggy (it crashed on me more than once). The web interface was better, with more options, including open VPN, simple parental controls, a guest network, and QoS optimization for gaming. Unfortunately, performance was inconsistent, and I suffered random drops twice in a week of testing.
Do I Need a Gaming Router?
The short answer is no. As I said in the intro, a good router is a good router, and you’ll find loads of great options that offer top-notch gaming performance in my Best Routers and Best Mesh Systems guides. That said, gaming routers do sometimes offer specific gaming features to help you prioritize gaming traffic, boost the speed of gaming streams, and keep lag to a minimum, though some of these features are available on regular routers, too. Gaming routers also sometimes have RGB lighting and designs that are supposed to appeal to gamers, though your mileage may vary.
Can I Add Routers or Extenders to Make a Mesh?
Many manufacturers allow you to create a mesh network by adding more routers or devices like Wi-Fi extenders, but check what is supported before you buy. For example, Asus AiMesh enables you to link multiple routers, while TP-Link’s OneMesh only allows you to add power-line adapters or range extenders. EasyMesh is a standard certification by the Wi-Fi Alliance that hopes to allow the mixing and matching of devices from different manufacturers to form a mesh, but few devices support it so far. You can also buy single mesh routers, like an Amazon Eero, and then add more later if you find that you need them. Based on my testing, a mesh is always better than an extender.
How Do Ethernet Cables Compare?
Running an Ethernet cable to create a wired connection between your home router and gaming PC or other device will always provide a faster, more stable, and more secure link than Wi-Fi. But running Ethernet cables everywhere can be messy. Read my Ethernet guide to learn more. Wireless connectivity makes life easy and is fast enough for most tasks.
How I Test Routers
To find the best gaming routers, I use each one for at least a week (usually longer) in a busy family home of four with lots of video streaming, gaming, and video calls. I also test the mobile apps and web interfaces to see how easy it is to change settings, set up parental controls, and access security features. My priority is to learn how well the router works in real-life rather than a lab, but I do also run a set of standardized tests, so that I have numbers to compare.
I run speed tests (downloads and uploads). I transfer files on the network on multiple devices (including iPhones, Android phones, Windows PCs, and MacBooks) from different spots around my home. I use NetSpot to survey signal strength throughout the house and create heat maps for comparison. I run the TamoSoft Throughput Test. I turn the power and modem off and on to find out how each system recovers.

Injured Assefa narrowly misses world record in Berlin
- Published
An injured Tigst Assefa hobbled over the line at the Berlin Marathon on Sunday after looking set to smash the women's world record.
The Ethiopian still won with the third-fastest time in history in two hours 11 minutes four seconds.
But the 29-year-old, a silver medallist at the Paris Olympics two years ago, had been cruising to a new record before fading in the final stages.
Kenyan athlete Ruth Chepngetich's time of 2:09:56, set at the 2024 Chicago Marathon, remains the world record time, though that result is overshadowed by the three-year doping ban she received in 2025.
Assefa, the 2026 London Marathon winner, started rapidly and led the field by a minute at the 15km mark. She was ahead of the record pace at 35km and is a renowned fast finisher - but began to suffer clear discomfort and her pace slowed.
However she still broke the Berlin course record of 2:11:53 that she set in 2023 - which was also her previous personal best.
In addition, she improved on her time of 2:15:41 at the London Marathon earlier this year.
"We have to bow our heads to this performance. She was on a world record course for most of the race but then something happened to her tendon," said race director Mark Milde.
"To finish like this, I've never seen something like this. The pain is hard to imagine.
"With a heavy heart, we saw her set a course record, but it could have been a lot more."
The top five finishers were all from Ethiopia, with Bedatu Hirpa second and Dera Dida third.
Guye Adola - another Ethiopian - won the men's race with a time of 2:02:50.

MobiKwik cofounder and chief financial officer (CFO) Upasana Taku has picked up 1.07 Lakh shares of the listed fintech company via multiple open-market transactions. In a filing with the exchanges, the company said that Taku picked up the stake in two separate tranches of 55,000 and 52,000 shares. She lapped up the shares for a cumulative sum of ₹2.1 Cr. With this, Taku’s shareholding in the company has increased to 10.24% from 10.11% previously. “Since the company's IPO in December 2024, I have purchased a total of 2,94,177 equity shares, which includes 1,87,177 equity shares acquired in December 2025 and 1,07,000 equity shares acquired in September 2026,” Taku said in a filing with the exchanges. The cofounder is bolstering her shareholding in the company amid volatility in MobiKwik shares. The stock has zoomed 26.6% in the past six months, but is still down 15.38% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The gains have likely been attributed to the recent re-introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) on high-value UPI payments and the company’s healthy financial show. The fintech company reported a consolidated net profit of ₹7.6 Cr in Q1 FY27 as against a net loss of ₹41.9 Cr in the year-ago period. Meanwhile, operating revenue rose a marginal 3.7% to ₹281.5 Cr during the quarter under review from ₹271.4 Cr in Q1 FY26. In May, it also received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to operate as a payment aggregator-physical (PA-P) licence.
